issue.title: [SPARK-61380][SS] Keep same-batch matches of stream-stream left semi joins between the watermarks

labels.name: repo-a45ce8d8
labels.description: Trigger AI review by Omnigent on Databricks

issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

A stream-stream left semi join now stores every right input row, including a row whose event time is at or below the batch's eviction cutoff. The eviction at the end of the batch still removes such a row. Inner and outer joins keep skipping it, because they process the left input first.

### Why are the changes needed?

Since SPARK-55973, a left semi join processes the right input of a micro-batch before the left input. The join did not store a right row that the batch evicts, because it assumed that the batch's left rows had already probed it. For a left semi join they have not. With the default `spark.sql.streaming.statefulOperator.allowMultiple=true`, late filtering uses the previous batch's watermark and eviction uses the current one, so a right row between the two passes late filtering but was not stored. A left row of the same batch then found no match and was never emitted.

For example, take `leftKey = rightKey AND leftTime = rightTime` with 0-second watermarks on both inputs. A batch with late-events watermark 100 s and eviction watermark 105 s receives left (1, 102) and right (1, 102). It should emit (1, 102), but emits nothing.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A left semi join now emits a left row whose matching right row arrives in the same micro-batch with event times between the late-events watermark and the eviction watermark. In Spark 4.2.0 to 4.3.0 that row was dropped. Such right rows are now written to state and removed in the same batch, so the number of updated state rows of a left semi join can grow.

### How was this patch tested?

Added four tests to `StreamingLeftSemiJoinBase`. Each sends a left row and its matching right row in one batch whose late-events watermark is 100 seconds. The right row is above that watermark, but at or below the batch's eviction cutoff.

- Same-batch matches between the watermarks, for three conditions:
  - equal event times;
  - a key shifted by 10 seconds while the watermark advances by 50 seconds;
  - a time interval, `leftTime BETWEEN rightTime - INTERVAL 10 SECONDS AND rightTime + INTERVAL 10 SECONDS`.

  Each checks the output, and the state rows after the second and third batches.
- A same-batch match whose right cutoff comes from a bound on another right column: `rightExpiry >= leftTime + INTERVAL 30 SECONDS AND leftTime >= rightTime - INTERVAL 1 HOUR`. Storing only the right rows above the right cutoff at the late-events watermark would drop this match.

The tests run in state format 2 (RocksDB and HDFS), 3 and 4, each with and without changelog checkpointing where it applies: 24 runs in total.

```sh
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingLeftSemiJoinV4Suite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithoutVCFSuite'  # 112 tests, 0 failures
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingInnerJoinV4Suite *StreamingOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingFullOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinV4Suite *StreamingInnerJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithVCFSuite'  # 383 tests, 0 failures
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingInnerJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithoutVCFSuite'  # 184 tests, 0 failures
```

Scalastyle for sql, main and test sources: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Without the fix, all 24 runs of the new tests fail: the join emits no row in the third batch. To check this, `StreamingSymmetricHashJoinExec` was restored from the base commit, and the tests of this PR were kept.

issue.title: [SPARK-61350][SS] Reject negative watermark terms in stream-stream join eviction bounds

issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR rejects a normalized negative opposite-watermark term when inferring a state eviction bound for a stream-stream join.

**Stack.** This is PR 7 of 7 and depends on #60284. Until the earlier PRs merge, this PR also shows their commits, and the merge commits bring in their review fixes. Please review only this PR's own commits: [324b55ecb18](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60286/commits/324b55ecb18c8345cfdc92254751d732dccc69ac) (the fix) and [3a696a71dd6](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60286/commits/3a696a71dd6416df4d2631f438032af0cb2f3196) (review round 1). Merge order:

1. #60279 [SPARK-61344](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61344): Fix stream-stream join range eviction column and output watermark
2. #60280 [SPARK-61345](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61345): Fix stream-stream join watermark direction and equality-key eviction
3. #60281 [SPARK-61346](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61346): Derive stream-stream join range eviction from the late-filtering event time
4. #60282 [SPARK-61347](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61347): Evict stream-stream join range state without a watermark on the stored side
5. #60283 [SPARK-61348](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61348): Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins
6. #60284 [SPARK-61349](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61349): Ignore constant-only bounds in stream-stream join state eviction
7. #60286 [SPARK-61350](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61350): Reject negative watermark terms in stream-stream join eviction bounds (this PR)

- After normalization, a bound such as `CAST(leftTime AS BIGINT) + CAST(rightTime AS BIGINT) > 100` has the opposite watermark with a negative sign. It no longer produces an eviction bound.
- Raise the checkpoint version to 6. Older checkpoints of affected join shapes are rejected with `STREAMING_JOIN_CHECKPOINT_INCOMPATIBLE` before any state is opened.
- The migration guide and the join guide state that a sum of both event times does not qualify.

### Why are the changes needed?

For `CAST(leftTime AS BIGINT) + CAST(rightTime AS BIGINT) > 100`, a later right row can match arbitrarily old left state. Treating the right watermark as an upper bound discarded those matches.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Valid matches are preserved in V2, V3 and V4. Joins without a valid eviction bound may keep more state, and outer or semi plans without a finalization bound fail analysis.

issue.title: [SPARK-61347][SS] Evict stream-stream join range state without a watermark on the stored side

labels.name: repo-a45ce8d8
labels.description: Trigger AI review by Omnigent on Databricks

issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR lets a stream-stream join evict range state on one side using only the opposite input's watermark.

**Stack.** This is PR 4 of 7 and depends on #60281. Until the earlier PRs merge, this PR also shows their commits, and the merge commits bring in their review fixes. Please review only this PR's own commits: [7bd01bd59a6](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60282/commits/7bd01bd59a639721d4cd006f6ee1e95f7c6f111c) (the fix) and [4000ae8f0c6](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60282/commits/4000ae8f0c6012cd60655a093ed642ce08e68651) (review round 1). Merge order:

1. #60279 [SPARK-61344](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61344): Fix stream-stream join range eviction column and output watermark
2. #60280 [SPARK-61345](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61345): Fix stream-stream join watermark direction and equality-key eviction
3. #60281 [SPARK-61346](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61346): Derive stream-stream join range eviction from the late-filtering event time
4. #60282 [SPARK-61347](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61347): Evict stream-stream join range state without a watermark on the stored side (this PR)
5. #60283 [SPARK-61348](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61348): Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins
6. #60284 [SPARK-61349](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61349): Ignore constant-only bounds in stream-stream join state eviction
7. #60286 [SPARK-61350](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61350): Reject negative watermark terms in stream-stream join eviction bounds

- Infer a state range bound from the opposite watermark even when the stored side has no watermark of its own, or its event-time column was pruned from the physical join.
- A column without its own watermark gets no cutoff from a condition that the cutoff solver counts inexactly: whole days in a session time zone that is not fixed-offset, where a day can be 23 or 25 hours, or a truncating cast such as `CAST(ts AS BIGINT)`. The analysis check uses the same rule, so admission and eviction agree. Columns with their own watermark keep their cutoffs.
- Raise the checkpoint version to 4. Older checkpoints of affected join shapes are rejected with `STREAMING_JOIN_CHECKPOINT_INCOMPATIBLE` before any state is opened.
- The join guide states that the impressions example needs no watermark on `impressionTime`.

### Why are the changes needed?

A right watermark and a valid time range are enough to finalize old left rows. For example, a left outer join of impressions and clicks with a watermark on `clickTime` only and `clickTime BETWEEN impressionTime AND impressionTime + INTERVAL 1 HOUR` passes analysis. Because the left input has no watermark, Spark never removes left rows and never emits their unmatched outer rows. The right outer case is symmetric.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

- Joins with a watermark on only one input emit eligible unmatched rows and remove expired state, including after a restart and when the event-time column is pruned.
- A one-sided range join whose only bound uses whole days in a daylight-saving session time zone, or a truncating cast, does not evict that input, and its outer and left semi forms fail analysis. Before, such a join could emit an unmatched row while a match could still arrive.

### How was this patch tested?

All commands below passed on this branch, rebased on Apache Spark master: 1,499 tests, 0 failures.

```sh
build/sbt 'catalyst/testOnly *StreamingJoinHelperSuite *UnsupportedOperationsSuite'  # 331
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingJoinWatermarkAdmissionSuite *StreamingJoinEqualityOutputWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinSelectedEventTimeSuite *StreamingJoinOutputWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinEqualityWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinOneSidedWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinRangeWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinRangeEvictionSuite *StreamingSymmetricHashJoinHelperSuite *MultiStatefulOperatorsSuite *OffsetSeqLogSuite *SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerSuite *SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerEventTimeInKeySuite'  # 240
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingJoinCheckpointCompatibilitySuite *StreamingJoinRangeEvictionCheckpointSuite'  # 239
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingInnerJoinV4Suite *StreamingOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingFullOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinV4Suite *StreamingInnerJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingInnerJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithoutVCFSuite'  # 689
```

Scalastyle for catalyst and sql, main and test sources: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

The new tests cover V2, V3 and V4, both outer-join directions, restart, pruned event-time columns and crossed intervals. To check that they catch the bug, I ran this PR's test files on the code of #60281, the previous PR in this stack. 31 tests failed:

- **Dedicated suites (10):** the six one-watermark tests (V2, V3 and V4, both directions) and the three left outer pruned-column tests never emitted the unmatched outer row, and the helper test derived no eviction predicate.
- **Join suites, V4 and VCF variants (21 runs):** the one-watermark left and right outer joins and the boundary-match tests never emitted the unmatched outer row. The left semi join with only a right watermark reported the wrong state row counts. In V4, the secondary index of a one-sided-watermark interval join stayed empty.

Note on apache/spark#60068 (SPARK-60850): that PR keeps watermarked input columns through column pruning. If it merges first, the test `expiry-column eviction with a pruned event-time column` here needs updating, because its assertion that the physical join no longer outputs `leftTime` would fail.

Review round 1: 8 of the new tests fail on this PR's code before this round's fixes.

issue.title: [SPARK-61345][SS] Fix stream-stream join watermark direction and equality-key eviction
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR checks the direction of each watermark when a stream-stream join is admitted, and evicts equality-key state with the opposite input's watermark.

**Stack.** This is PR 2 of 7 and depends on #60279. Until the earlier PRs merge, this PR also shows their commits, and the merge commits bring in their review fixes. Please review only this PR's own commits: [963f9bb3a4b](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60280/commits/963f9bb3a4bb20cd550cd6f126ecb6f4175e69d1) (the fix) and [c4bdbf09fdb](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60280/commits/c4bdbf09fdbea72fee5ab22ad03b839f1d9d7a37) (review round 1). Merge order:

1. #60279 [SPARK-61344](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61344): Fix stream-stream join range eviction column and output watermark
2. #60280 [SPARK-61345](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61345): Fix stream-stream join watermark direction and equality-key eviction (this PR)
3. #60281 [SPARK-61346](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61346): Derive stream-stream join range eviction from the late-filtering event time
4. #60282 [SPARK-61347](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61347): Evict stream-stream join range state without a watermark on the stored side
5. #60283 [SPARK-61348](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61348): Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins
6. #60284 [SPARK-61349](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61349): Ignore constant-only bounds in stream-stream join state eviction
7. #60286 [SPARK-61350](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61350): Reject negative watermark terms in stream-stream join eviction bounds

- **Directional admission.** Check the direction of each watermark before admitting a streaming outer or left semi join. The rows a side finalizes need a bound derived from the opposite input's watermark. Full outer joins need a bound in both directions.
- **Opposite-side equality eviction.** Derive each side's equality-key eviction predicate and V4 timestamp index from the opposite input's event-time key, which can sit at a different equality-key ordinal. A key that is the opposite event time shifted by a constant interval without whole days or months, such as `lt = rt + INTERVAL 10 SECONDS`, is bounded by the watermark plus that interval, for either sign. A shift with whole days, months or years, such as `lt = rt + INTERVAL 1 DAY`, is bounded by the watermark itself when it never moves a time backward, and gets no bound otherwise, because Spark adds whole days in the session time zone, where a day can be 23 or 25 hours, and months vary in length. This rule does not depend on the session time zone, so the V4 state layout stays the same when a restart changes it. The output watermark uses the same relation, and gives no bound for a shift with whole days, months or years. A truncating key such as `CAST(CAST(rt AS BIGINT) AS TIMESTAMP)` gets no key bound, because a later row can truncate below the watermark. When the key is the input's own event time, V4 eviction scans start after the lower of the late-events watermark and the shifted cutoff at it.
- **V4 point lookups.** A V4 side that is not evicted by key, and whose own event time is an equality key, still stores and looks up its rows at that key, unless it is evicted on another column. A lookup then reads one timestamp instead of scanning every timestamp of the key. The stored timestamps are the same as in released versions.
- **Null keys.** A key selected for eviction can be NULL, including a NULL window. Such a row cannot match, so the rule from SPARK-61344 applies, now also to the key that the opposite watermark selects: a preserved side emits the row padded with nulls on arrival, and no side stores it. V4 no longer reads a NULL window as a struct, which threw a `NullPointerException`. A row with a NULL key can still reach V4 state on a side that is not evicted by key. It is kept out of the timestamp index.
- **Checkpoint version 2.** In every state format, older checkpoints of an aligned own-event-time equality key are still accepted. Old V4 state can hold a NULL selected key at timestamp 0 under its own key bytes. Such a row never shares a list with a real row, and evicting it emits its correct outer row. A shifted key is not accepted for old checkpoints, because older versions evicted it at the unshifted watermark.
- **Finalization check conf.** Add the internal conf `spark.sql.streaming.join.checkFinalization.enabled`, default `true`. When it is `false`, an outer or left semi join whose watermarks and time constraints cannot finalize an input logs a warning instead of failing analysis. Eviction is not affected.
- **Docs.** The migration guide and the join support table describe the required watermark direction. They and the admission error also say which watermark and time constraint a stateful operator after the join needs.

### Why are the changes needed?

- A watermark on the stored side alone cannot prove that an opposite-side match will never arrive. Such outer and semi plans were accepted and could keep unmatched state indefinitely.
- When the event-time keys sit at different equality-key ordinals, using one ordinal for both sides can discard a future match and emit a premature outer null row. One input's watermark also cannot bound its own state against future input from the other side.
- Reading a NULL selected window as a struct crashes V4. Once the eviction key comes from the opposite input, a preserved row whose new eviction key is NULL would never be evicted or emitted, although released versions emitted it.
- When the opposite input has no watermark, V4 would otherwise give up point lookups for a side whose own event time is an equality key. Every probe would then scan all timestamps of the key.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

- Outer and semi plans without the required watermark direction fail analysis, with the missing direction and migration guidance in the error. Valid equality and range plans remain supported.
- Equality joins with a watermark on only one input now keep that input's rows for the life of the query, because the other input has no watermark that bounds them. Such a join holds back its output watermark, so a downstream stateful operator that uses that input's event time stops emitting results. The admission error, the join support table and the migration guide name the watermark and time constraint that avoid this.
- The new internal conf `spark.sql.streaming.join.checkFinalization.enabled` (default `true`) can turn the new outer and semi admission failures into warnings. Eviction stays corrected either way.
- Valid matches are preserved and premature unmatched output is prevented in V2, V3 and V4.
- On a preserved side, a row whose eviction key is NULL is emitted padded with nulls in the batch it arrives, also in a V4 join whose key is only bounded by the other input.
- Equality keys shifted by whole days, months or years keep a bound in every session time zone: forward shifts use the unshifted watermark, as before, and backward shifts get none, so outer and semi joins on a backward whole-day shift fail analysis.

### How was this patch tested?

All commands below passed on this branch, rebased on Apache Spark master: 1,453 tests, 0 failures.

```sh
build/sbt 'catalyst/testOnly *StreamingJoinHelperSuite *UnsupportedOperationsSuite'  # 325
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingJoinWatermarkAdmissionSuite *StreamingJoinEqualityOutputWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinOutputWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinEqualityWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinRangeEvictionSuite *StreamingSymmetricHashJoinHelperSuite *MultiStatefulOperatorsSuite *OffsetSeqLogSuite *SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerSuite *SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerEventTimeInKeySuite'  # 207
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingJoinCheckpointCompatibilitySuite *StreamingJoinRangeEvictionCheckpointSuite'  # 239
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingInnerJoinV4Suite *StreamingOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingFullOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinV4Suite *StreamingInnerJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingInnerJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithoutVCFSuite'  # 641
build/sbt 'hive/testOnly *SparkConfigBindingPolicySuite'  # 3
build/sbt 'core/testOnly *SparkThrowableSuite'  # 38
```

Scalastyle for catalyst and sql, main and test sources: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

To check that the tests catch the bugs, I ran this PR's test files on the code of #60279, the previous PR in this stack. Two suites stayed at their #60279 versions, because their new tests call code that this PR adds or changes: `StreamingJoinHelperSuite` (the new key-bound helpers) and `StreamingJoinCheckpointCompatibilitySuite` (the new state-format argument of the compatibility check). The join suites ran in their V4 and VCF variants. These tests failed:

- **Admission:** 15 analyzer cases and 8 end-to-end runs started the query instead of rejecting it. They cover full outer joins with a bound in only one direction, equality joins whose only watermarked key is on the wrong input, and left outer joins whose key is shifted from an unwatermarked column, truncated, or shifted by one day in America/Los_Angeles. Another 33 analyzer cases were already rejected and failed only on the new error message.
- **Equality-key eviction:** 44 runs across V2, V3 and V4 removed state too early, which emitted premature outer null rows or lost matches. They cover eviction by the opposite watermark, with and without restart; left outer, right outer and left semi joins with one watermark; a full outer join with different key ordinals; a key shifted by -10 seconds; a truncated key; a window key in V4; and one-day and 36-hour shifts, in both UTC and America/Los_Angeles. A key shifted by +10 seconds was never evicted.
- **Null keys in V4:** with a null right window, the full outer join failed with a `NullPointerException`. With a null left window, it emitted the null-key row as unmatched. The state manager test also threw a `NullPointerException`.
- **Eviction predicates:** for `lt = rt` with only a right watermark, the helper built a key predicate for the right state, which must not be evicted. The mixed key and value eviction tests (V2, V3, V4) found no value predicate for the left state.
- **Updated expectations:** 8 runs of existing tests now expect more state to be kept, because the cutoff now comes from the opposite input. They are the windowed inner join (Append and Update), the state metrics test, and the join followed by a window aggregate, which now also checks that a late right row still matches.

Review round 1: on this PR's code before this round's fixes, 19 of the new shifted-key tests fail, and with the previous key cutoff used uncapped, V4 never emits the new boundary row. The new NULL-key tests for crossed keys and for a V4 NULL key timestamp also failed before their fix.

+ * simplifies the condition. So the query is optimized once here, with the optimizer of its

+ * subtrees of subquery plans without an outer reference, become placeholders of their outputs, as

+ * start, as for a query without a lookup join.
+ *
+ * Only the planning errors of the lookup join and of its connector contract fail the start. Any
+ * other error, such as one that an ordinary join raises too, is left to the micro-batch, which

+          session.sessionState.optimizer.execute(
+            StreamingV2ScanPushDown.forStartup(normalized, withStartupValues = false))

+ * share it, so analysis rejects every join that the optimizer cannot convert, except one without
+ * a condition: see [[CheckExternalLookupJoin]].
+ *
+ * A join is an external lookup join when its right side reads a table that supports external
+ * lookup but not batch read, or when the right side carries an `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint. A table
+ * that supports both keeps the ordinary join strategies unless the hint opts in. It must be a
+ * stream-static join: the left side is a streaming query, whose micro-batches tolerate lookup
+ * results that change between requests, and the lookup table is on the right side. The join reads
+ * the table directly, or through hints, aliases, views, and projections and filters that it can
+ * evaluate on the lookup results, so a join that must be a lookup join either runs as one or fails
+ * here, whatever the optimizer later does to its lookup side.
+ */
+object ExternalLookupJoinEligibility extends QueryErrorsBase {
+  sealed trait Eligibility
+  /**
+   * The join stays an ordinary join: it has no `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint, and neither of its inputs is
+   * a lookup-only relation, directly or below unary operators. A lookup-only relation below another
+   * operator, such as a union, is not recognized, and fails later as a batch scan.
+   */
+  case object NotLookupJoin extends Eligibility
+  /** The join runs as an external lookup join. */
+  case object Eligible extends Eligibility
+  /**
+   * The join must run as an external lookup join, with a supported join type, but has no
+   * condition.
+   */
+  case object MissingCondition extends Eligibility
+  /** The join must run as an external lookup join but cannot. */

+      return Ineligible(QueryCompilationErrors.invalidExternalLookupHintError("NOT_ON_LOOKUP_SIDE"))

+    // The lookup-only table must be on the right side; the sides are never swapped.
+    val leftLookupOnlyTable = ExternalLookupRelations.lookupOnlyTable(input(join.left))
+    if (leftLookupOnlyTable.isDefined) {
+      return ineligible("LOOKUP_TABLE_ON_LEFT", toSQLId(leftLookupOnlyTable.get.name()))
+    }
+    val markers = lookupHints(join.right)
+    val lookupOnly = ExternalLookupRelations.lookupOnlyTable(input(join.right)).isDefined

+    // way the join must run as an external lookup join, and the checks below apply.

+    }

+    // filters that the lookup join can evaluate. There is none when another operator, or a stage
+    // that it cannot evaluate, stands in between, or the side reads no DSv2 table.
+    val tableRelation = lookupRelation(join.right)

+      case None =>

+    }

+    }

+    // only when the query reads one.

+    joinStrategyHint(join) match {

+      // Checked before the condition, so that a cross join fails while it is analyzed.
+      case None if !SUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPES.contains(join.joinType) =>

Fixed in [d3477aa9bb5](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/d3477aa9bb5b7e6baee4b76f467a3fc940fe17c9). The shared classifier treats a cross join as an inner join, as for an ordinary join, so `CROSS JOIN` and `crossJoin()` with the key in WHERE now plan like a comma join. A cross join with no key anywhere fails with `MISSING_JOIN_CONDITION`, and right and full outer joins still fail with `JOIN_TYPE`. The change is in this PR rather than in #59909, which owns the classifier, because a key in WHERE only reaches the join from this PR's pushdown on.

+
+  private class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator extends PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] {
+    override def eval(
+        partitionIndex: Int,
+        inputs: Iterator[InternalRow]*): Iterator[InternalRow] = {
+      assert(inputs.length == 1)
+      new PartitionJoinIterator(inputs.head, partitionIndex)
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Joins one partition batch by batch, and closes its reader after the last batch. */
+  private class PartitionJoinIterator(input: Iterator[InternalRow], partitionIndex: Int)
+    extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    private val reader = new LookupReader
+    private val parameters = new LookupParameters(partitionIndex)
+    private val resultRows = new LookupResultRows
+    private val transforms = new LookupTransforms(partitionIndex)
+    private val joinOutput = new JoinOutput(partitionIndex)
+    private var cache = if (cacheOptions.enabled) Some(new LookupCache) else None
+    private var batch: Iterator[InternalRow] = Iterator.empty
+    private var inputExhausted = false
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      batch.hasNext
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      if (!batch.hasNext) {
+        throw new SparkIllegalStateException(
+          errorClass = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+          messageParameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup join exhausted"))
+      }
+      batch.next()
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryAdvance(): Unit = {
+      while (!batch.hasNext && !inputExhausted) {
+        val rows = readBatch()
+        if (rows.nonEmpty) {
+          batch = new BatchJoinIterator(rows, parameters, resultRows, transforms, joinOutput, cache,
+            inputRemains = () => !inputExhausted, reader = reader)
+        }
+        inputExhausted = !hasInput
+      }
+      // No later batch reads the cache, so neither it nor the drained batch is kept.
+      if (inputExhausted && !batch.hasNext) {
+        batch = Iterator.empty
+        cache = None
+        reader.close()
+      }
+    }
+
+    private lazy val toUnsafe = UnsafeProjection.create(streamOutput, streamOutput)
+
+    // When a request holds one parameter row because of a selected range, a batch takes the stream
+    // rows of one key rather than one stream row. It ends before the first row with another key,
+    // which starts the next batch. A row that cannot match has no key, and any batch takes it.
+    private var heldRow: UnsafeRow = null
+
+    private def hasInput: Boolean = heldRow != null || input.hasNext
+
+    private def nextRow(): UnsafeRow = if (heldRow != null) {
+      val row = heldRow
+      heldRow = null
+      row
+    } else {
+      input.next() match {
+        case unsafe: UnsafeRow => unsafe.copy()
+        case other => toUnsafe(other).copy()
+      }
+    }
+
+    /** The request row of a stream row that can match, in a reused row, or null. */
+    private def requestRowOf(row: InternalRow): UnsafeRow =
+      if (!joinOutput.canMatch(row)) null else {
+        val requestRow = parameters.requestRow(row)
+        if (parameters.matchesNothing(requestRow)) null else requestRow
+      }
+
+    // An array, because a batch's rows are read by position for every key, match and output row.
+    // The batch holds its rows until its request is read, so it stops once their copies reach
+    // maxBatchBytes, keeping the row that reaches it, as well as at maxParameterRowsPerRequest
+    // rows, or at another key with one key per batch. It always takes one row.
+    private def readBatch(): Array[InternalRow] = {
+      val rows = mutable.ArrayBuffer.empty[InternalRow]
+      var bytes = 0L
+      var batchKey: UnsafeRow = null
+      var keyChanged = false
+      while (!keyChanged && (oneKeyPerBatch || rows.length < maxParameterRowsPerRequest) &&
+          bytes < maxBatchBytes && hasInput) {
+        val row = nextRow()
+        val requestRow = if (oneKeyPerBatch) requestRowOf(row) else null
+        if (requestRow != null && batchKey != null && requestRow != batchKey) {
+          heldRow = row
+          keyChanged = true
+        } else {
+          if (requestRow != null && batchKey == null) batchKey = requestRow.copy()
+          bytes += row.getSizeInBytes
+          rows += row
+        }
+      }
+      rows.toArray
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** The stream rows that share a key, and the one request row sent for them. */
+  private case class KeyEntry(requestRow: UnsafeRow, rowIndexes: mutable.ArrayBuffer[Int])
+
+  /** The stream rows that share a key, and the cached lookup rows that they join. */
+  private case class CachedKey(lookupRows: Array[UnsafeRow], rowIndexes: mutable.ArrayBuffer[Int])
+
+  /**
+   * Joins one batch of stream rows. Rows whose parameters are equal under Spark equality share
+   * one request row, and every result row for a request row that satisfies the selected lookup
+   * predicates joins all the stream rows sharing it. A stream row is finished, which may emit its
+   * unmatched output row, once no more result rows can match it.
+   *
+   * Output rows are projected into a reused row on `next()`, so the consumer copies the rows it
+   * retains, as with other join iterators.
+   */
+  private class BatchJoinIterator(
+      rows: Array[InternalRow],
+      parameters: LookupParameters,
+      resultRows: LookupResultRows,
+      transforms: LookupTransforms,
+      joinOutput: JoinOutput,
+      cache: Option[LookupCache],
+      inputRemains: () => Boolean,
+      reader: LookupReader) extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    metrics.inputRows += rows.length
+    metrics.inputBatches += 1
+
+    private val matched = Array.fill(rows.length)(false)
+    private val finished = mutable.BitSet.empty
+    // Output rows not yet returned: a stream row index and the lookup row it is joined with.
+    private val pending = mutable.Queue.empty[(Int, InternalRow)]
+
+    // One entry for each distinct request row that can match and is not cached, in the order of
+    // first occurrence. A row that can never match, because it fails the stream condition or has a
+    // null parameter, is finished right away, and its parameters are not requested. The stream
+    // condition is checked before the parameters are evaluated, so that it can guard their
+    // expressions. A request row is classified once, on its first occurrence, as a cache hit or a
+    // row to request: every path fans out to all the rows sharing it, so it must not be both, e.g.
+    // across a TTL boundary.
+    private val cachedKeys = mutable.LinkedHashMap.empty[UnsafeRow, CachedKey]
+    private val keyEntries = {
+      val entries = mutable.LinkedHashMap.empty[UnsafeRow, KeyEntry]
+      rows.indices.foreach { index =>
+        lazy val requestRow = parameters.requestRow(rows(index))
+        if (!joinOutput.canMatch(rows(index)) || parameters.matchesNothing(requestRow)) {
+          finish(index)
+        } else {
+          entries.get(requestRow).map(_.rowIndexes)
+            .orElse(cachedKeys.get(requestRow).map(_.rowIndexes)) match {
+            case Some(rowIndexes) => rowIndexes += index
+            case None =>
+              val retained = requestRow.copy()
+              cache.flatMap(_.get(retained)) match {
+                case Some(lookupRows) =>
+                  metrics.cacheHits += 1
+                  cachedKeys.put(retained, CachedKey(lookupRows, mutable.ArrayBuffer(index)))
+                case None => entries.put(retained, KeyEntry(retained, mutable.ArrayBuffer(index)))
+              }
+          }
+        }
+      }
+      entries.values.toArray
+    }
+    cachedKeys.values.foreach { cached =>
+      cached.rowIndexes.foreach { index =>
+        cached.lookupRows.foreach(joinMatch(index, _))
+        finish(index)
+      }
+    }
+
+    // Only a later batch of the partition reads what this one caches, so the last batch caches
+    // nothing. The partition knows whether input remains once the request is sent, before its
+    // results are read.
+    private lazy val cacheWriter = if (!inputRemains()) None else {
+      cache.map(new CacheWriter(_, keyEntries.map(_.requestRow)))
+    }
+
+    // No connector request, and no reader, when no key can match.
+    private var cursor: ExternalLookupResultCursor =
+      if (keyEntries.isEmpty) EmptyLookupCursor
+      else connectorCall(reader.lookup(keyEntries.map(_.requestRow)))
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      pending.nonEmpty
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      if (pending.isEmpty) throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+      val (index, lookupRow) = pending.dequeue()
+      joinOutput.project(rows(index), lookupRow)
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryFillPending(): Unit = {
+      try {
+        while (pending.isEmpty && advanceCursor()) {
+          reader.resultRowRead()
+          // The join checks for a close() before each connector call, so it makes none after it
+          // has seen one.
+          val start = System.nanoTime()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val ordinal = cursor.inputOrdinal()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val connectorRow = cursor.get()
+          metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+          if (connectorRow == null) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName, "NULL_RESULT", Map("method" -> "ExternalLookupResultCursor.get()"))
+          }
+          val entry = requestedEntry(ordinal)
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val resultRow = resultRows.validatedCopy(connectorRow)
+          if (parameters.selectedPredicatesHold(entry.requestRow, resultRow)) {
+            transforms(resultRow).foreach { lookupRow =>
+              cacheWriter.foreach(_.add(entry.requestRow, lookupRow))
+              entry.rowIndexes.foreach(joinMatch(_, lookupRow))
+            }
+          }
+        }
+        if (pending.isEmpty) finishCursor(completed = true)
+      } catch {
+        case error: Throwable =>
+          Utils.tryWithSafeFinally(throw error) {
+            finishCursor(completed = false)
+          }
+      }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Advances the connector's cursor, unless the reader was closed meanwhile. A close() while
+     * next() ran fails the read once next() returns: Spark then reads no row from the closed
+     * cursor, and does not take a missing row for a complete result.
+     */
+    private def advanceCursor(): Boolean = (cursor ne EmptyLookupCursor) && {
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      val advanced = connectorCall(cursor.next())
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      advanced
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Runs a connector call and adds its time to the lookup time metric, which counts only the
+     * time in the connector, not that of the work above the join while a cursor is open.
+     */
+    private def connectorCall[T](call: => T): T = {
+      val start = System.nanoTime()
+      try call finally metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+    }
+
+    private def requestedEntry(ordinal: Int): KeyEntry = {
+      if (ordinal < 0 || ordinal >= keyEntries.length) {
+        throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+          tableName,
+          "INVALID_INPUT_ORDINAL",
+          Map("ordinal" -> ordinal.toString, "numParameterRows" -> keyEntries.length.toString))
+      }
+      keyEntries(ordinal)
+    }
+
+    private def joinMatch(index: Int, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit = {
+      // A semi or anti join knows a stream row's answer at its first match, so it evaluates the
+      // residual condition no further for that row, as the other join operators do. It still
+      // reads the whole result, for the other stream rows of the key.
+      if (!(joinOutput.answeredByFirstMatch && matched(index)) &&
+          joinOutput.matches(rows(index), lookupRow)) {
+        val firstMatch = !matched(index)
+        matched(index) = true
+        joinOutput.matched(lookupRow, firstMatch).foreach(emit(index, _))
+      }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Closes the cursor once. After a complete read, caches the results and finishes every stream
+     * row that was waiting for them. After a failure or a close, the results may be partial, so it
+     * caches nothing and finishes no row: a row without a match could be a row whose match was
+     * never read. A failure fails the task, which discards the cache, and the join never retries a
+     * request. Once the reader is closed, its close owns the cursor and the reader's metrics, so
+     * the join makes no further connector call.
+     */
+    private def finishCursor(completed: Boolean): Unit = if (cursor ne EmptyLookupCursor) {
+      cursor = EmptyLookupCursor
+      if (!reader.isClosed) {
+        try {
+          connectorCall(reader.closeCursor())
+        } finally {
+          reader.updateMetrics()
+        }
+      }
+      if (completed) {
+        cacheWriter.foreach(_.write())
+        keyEntries.foreach(_.rowIndexes.foreach(finish))
+      }
+    }
+
+    private def finish(index: Int): Unit = if (!finished.contains(index)) {
+      finished += index
+      if (!matched(index)) joinOutput.unmatched.foreach(emit(index, _))
+    }
+
+    private def emit(index: Int, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit = {
+      pending.enqueue(index -> lookupRow)
+      metrics.outputRows += 1
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * The lookup results by key, within a task, per input partition (a task that reads several input
+   * partitions, e.g. after coalesce, has one cache per partition). Once its entries take more than
+   * `maxBytes`, the least recently used ones are evicted; an entry expires once it is older than
+   * the TTL, by `cacheTicker`. An entry takes the bytes of its key and of its rows, with the
+   * objects that hold each row, plus a fixed overhead, so that a key without a result counts too.
+   * Its keys and rows are the batches' own copies, which are never changed.
+   */
+  private class LookupCache {
+    // One segment, so that eviction is exactly least recently used, and bounded by `maxBytes`.
+    private val entries: Cache[UnsafeRow, Array[UnsafeRow]] = {
+      val builder = CacheBuilder.newBuilder()
+        .concurrencyLevel(1)
+        .maximumWeight(cacheOptions.maxBytes)
+        .weigher(new Weigher[UnsafeRow, Array[UnsafeRow]] {
+          override def weigh(key: UnsafeRow, rows: Array[UnsafeRow]): Int = {
+            val bytes = ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory.CACHE_ENTRY_OVERHEAD_BYTES +
+              key.getSizeInBytes +
+              rows.iterator.map(ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory.cachedBytes).sum
+            math.min(bytes, Int.MaxValue).toInt
+          }
+        })
+        .ticker(cacheTicker)
+      val expiring = if (cacheOptions.ttlMillis > 0) {
+        builder.expireAfterWrite(cacheOptions.ttlMillis, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
+      } else {
+        builder
+      }
+      expiring.build[UnsafeRow, Array[UnsafeRow]]()
+    }
+
+    def get(key: UnsafeRow): Option[Array[UnsafeRow]] = Option(entries.getIfPresent(key))
+
+    def put(key: UnsafeRow, values: Array[UnsafeRow]): Unit = entries.put(key, values)
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Collects the result rows of one request by key, and caches them once the cursor is done. It
+   * receives only the rows that satisfy the selected lookup predicates, so the cache never holds a
+   * row that Spark's check dropped. A key whose rows take more than a
+   * [[ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory.CACHE_KEY_SHARE]]th of `maxBytes` is not cached, so that
+   * one large result cannot evict most of the cache, and the request holds at most `maxBytes` of
+   * rows for the cache, which could keep no more; a key whose rows would pass that is not cached
+   * either. Such a key is still joined in full. The rows are the batch's own copies, which are
+   * never changed.
+   */
+  private class CacheWriter(cache: LookupCache, keys: Array[UnsafeRow]) {
+    private class KeyResults(val rows: mutable.ArrayBuffer[UnsafeRow], var bytes: Long)
+    private val maxKeyBytes =
+      cacheOptions.maxBytes / ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory.CACHE_KEY_SHARE
+    private val resultsByKey =
+      mutable.HashMap.from(keys.map(_ -> new KeyResults(mutable.ArrayBuffer.empty, 0L)))
+    private val uncacheable = mutable.HashSet.empty[UnsafeRow]
+    private var bufferedBytes = 0L
+
+    def add(key: UnsafeRow, lookupRow: UnsafeRow): Unit = if (!uncacheable.contains(key)) {
+      val results = resultsByKey(key)
+      val rowBytes = ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory.cachedBytes(lookupRow)
+      if (results.bytes + rowBytes > maxKeyBytes ||
+          bufferedBytes + rowBytes > cacheOptions.maxBytes) {

+      case (conjunct, index) if !selectedConjuncts.contains(index) => conjunct

+    // condition is true, so this changes no result.
+    val residual = if (residualRest.isEmpty) residualFirst else {
+      residualFirst.map { conjunct =>

+    // their analyzed order; execution projects the lookup results into them. It keeps only those

+    // which an inner join evaluates in a filter above it; other join types reject them above.
+    val requiredAbove = join.joinType match {
+      case LeftSemi | LeftAnti => AttributeSet.empty
+      case _ => AttributeSet(join.requiredLookupOutput ++ joinFilter.flatMap(_.references))
+    }
+    val lookupOutput = join.right.output.filter(requiredAbove.contains)
+    val residualLookupReferences =
+      residual.flatMap(_.references).filter(join.right.outputSet.contains)
+    // The columns are pruned only now, once the lookup predicates are selected. A column that a
+    // selected lookup predicate reads is kept, because Spark checks the predicate itself on every
+    // row that the connector returns. V2ScanRelationPushDown.pruneColumns prunes a scan the same
+    // way, through PushDownUtils.pruneColumns, which this rule cannot call: it can pass
+    // nested-pruned columns, while a lookup scan receives only whole top-level columns, and it
+    // binds the read schema by the resolver, while a lookup scan binds it by exact name.

Thanks, fixed: the message keeps its current text and adds that a time range condition must bound a TIMESTAMP column of the finalized input by the other input's event time. The numeric, DATE, TIMESTAMP_NTZ and window tests assert the new sentence ([f885a5a0876](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60283/commits/f885a5a08766d0a1ce402ab9dff35dce9af28b98)).

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM: Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), running as an SP2K agent on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Confirmed: a whole-window comparison such as `lw > rw` no longer bounds state, so outer and left semi joins bounded only that way fail analysis, and inner joins keep that input's state. We are keeping this. Master accepted these comparisons for any window lengths, and that is wrong when the stored windows are shorter: with 10-second left windows and 20-second sliding right windows, master evicts a left window, and then a later right window still matches it. Telling the safe and unsafe cases apart needs window lengths that the attributes do not carry, so supporting it would add new metadata to every window column, for a form the guide does not document. The guides now say that comparing time windows does not qualify, and new tests pin the rejection and the inner-join match that eviction would lose ([f885a5a0876](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60283/commits/f885a5a08766d0a1ce402ab9dff35dce9af28b98)).

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM: Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), running as an SP2K agent on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Confirmed with a test, fixed in SPARK-61345 (#60280, [c4bdbf09fdb](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60280/commits/c4bdbf09fdbea72fee5ab22ad03b839f1d9d7a37)).

- **The failure.** A V4 inner join on `k = rt + INTERVAL 1 DAY`, started in America/Los_Angeles and restarted in UTC, lost every match for rows buffered before the restart.
- **The fix.** Whole days now count as inexact in every time zone, so whether a key gets an ordinal depends only on its shape. Forward whole-day shifts get an ordinal in every zone, and backward ones get none in any zone, so the V4 layout no longer changes with the session time zone.
- **Tests.** They restart in both directions, with a forward and a backward one-day shift.

<!-- sp2k-review1 reply 4523762444 -->

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM: Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), running as an SP2K agent on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Confirmed. Results were unchanged, but each probe into that state became a prefix scan. In a one-sided join with 200k keys, probe batches were about 1.3 to 1.5 times slower than on master. Fixed in [c4bdbf09fdb](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60280/commits/c4bdbf09fdbea72fee5ab22ad03b839f1d9d7a37): when no opposite key bounds a side, its V4 state manager still stores and looks up rows at its own event-time key, unless that side is evicted on another column. The stored timestamps are the same, so the state layout does not change, and probe time is back to master's.

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM: Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), running as an SP2K agent on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Confirmed, thanks. The drop is older than this PR. Since SPARK-55973 (Spark 4.2.0), a left semi join processes the right input first and does not store a right row that the batch evicts, so a plain `lt = rt` join already loses a left row whose match arrives in the same batch between the two watermarks. This PR raises the right cutoff for positively shifted keys, so those keys now hit the same case. The fix is in a separate PR against master, SPARK-61380 (#60307): a left semi join now stores every right row, and the eviction at the end of the batch removes it. Its tests cover a plain key and a shifted key in V2, V3 and V4.

+/**
+ * Executes synchronous, parameterized external lookup joins without a shuffle. Each task joins
+ * its input rows in batches, through an [[ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory]].
+ */
+case class ExternalLookupJoinExec(
+    tableName: String,
+    lookupParameters: Seq[Expression],
+    lookupInput: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupOutput: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupTransforms: Seq[ExternalLookupTransform],
+    nullSafeParameters: Seq[Boolean],
+    lookupKeys: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupKeyPredicates: Seq[String],
+    joinType: JoinType,
+    residualCondition: Option[Expression],
+    @transient scan: Scan,
+    readerFactory: ExternalLookupReaderFactory,
+    maxParameterRowsPerRequest: Int,
+    cacheOptions: ExternalLookupCacheOptions,
+    child: SparkPlan) extends UnaryExecNode with SupportsCustomDriverMetrics with PredicateHelper {
+
+  // The connector's value rows follow the read schema, which `lookupInput` describes, and the
+  // lookup-side stages turn them into rows of `transformedLookup`. The lookup columns keep their
+  // analyzed order, and take the types and nullability of those rows. In `lookupInput`, the
+  // nullability at every nested level combines the table's and the read schema's: a field is NOT
+  // NULL when either says so.
+  private lazy val transformedLookup = lookupTransforms.lastOption.map(_.output)
+    .getOrElse(lookupInput)
+  private lazy val inputByLookupOutput =
+    AttributeMap(transformedLookup.map(attr => attr -> attr))
+  private lazy val lookupColumns = lookupOutput.map(inputByLookupOutput)
+
+  override def output: Seq[Attribute] = joinType match {
+    case LeftOuter => child.output ++ lookupColumns.map(_.withNullability(true))
+    case LeftSemi | LeftAnti => child.output
+    case _ => child.output ++ lookupColumns
+  }
+
+  // Each task joins its input rows where they are, so the stream side's partitioning holds.
+  override def outputPartitioning: Partitioning = child.outputPartitioning
+
+  // The conjuncts of the residual condition that read only stream columns, and the rest. A stream
+  // row that fails the first cannot match, so the join checks them on each stream row before the
+  // lookup, and does not request the row's key. The join then evaluates them for rows without a
+  // match too, and before the conjuncts written ahead of them, so only conjuncts that can never
+  // fail are checked early: those that ExprUtils.canEvaluateUnconditionally accepts, as for the
+  // streamed side of other joins. `Expression.throwable` is not enough, because most expressions
+  // that can fail, such as an ANSI cast, do not report it. A conjunct that reads no column stays
+  // with the rest: the optimizer has already folded it if it could.
+  private def splitResidualCondition: (Option[Expression], Option[Expression]) = {
+    val (streamConjuncts, joinedConjuncts) =
+      residualCondition.toSeq.flatMap(splitConjunctivePredicates).partition { conjunct =>
+        conjunct.references.nonEmpty && conjunct.references.subsetOf(child.outputSet) &&
+          ExprUtils.canEvaluateUnconditionally(conjunct)
+      }
+    (streamConjuncts.reduceOption(And), joinedConjuncts.reduceOption(And))
+  }
+
+  // Spark does not trust the connector to evaluate the selected lookup predicates as Spark does,
+  // so it checks them itself on each row that the connector returns. The check reads that row
+  // after the parameter row of its request, and compares lookup key i with parameter i as its
+  // selected predicate does.
+  private def lookupKeyCheck: Option[Expression] = lookupParameters.indices.map { index =>
+    val parameter = lookupParameters(index)
+    val parameterValue = BoundReference(index, parameter.dataType, parameter.nullable)
+    val keyOrdinal = lookupInput.indexWhere(_.exprId == lookupKeys(index).exprId)
+    val key = lookupInput(keyOrdinal)
+    val keyValue = BoundReference(lookupParameters.length + keyOrdinal, key.dataType, key.nullable)
+    lookupKeyPredicates(index) match {
+      case "=" => EqualTo(keyValue, parameterValue)
+      case "<=>" => EqualNullSafe(keyValue, parameterValue)
+      case "<" => LessThan(keyValue, parameterValue)
+      case "<=" => LessThanOrEqual(keyValue, parameterValue)
+      case ">" => GreaterThan(keyValue, parameterValue)
+      case ">=" => GreaterThanOrEqual(keyValue, parameterValue)
+      case other => throw SparkException.internalError(s"Unexpected lookup predicate $other")
+    }
+  }.reduceOption(And)
+
+  override def references: AttributeSet =
+    AttributeSet(lookupParameters.flatMap(_.references)) ++
+      residualCondition.map(_.references.intersect(child.outputSet)).getOrElse(AttributeSet.empty)
+
+  // A connector's custom metrics are registered under prefixed keys, so that they never collide
+  // with the operator's own metrics; the UI shows the connector's descriptions.
+  override lazy val customMetrics: Map[String, SQLMetric] =
+    scan.supportedCustomMetrics().map { metric =>
+      ExternalLookupJoinExec.sourceMetricKey(metric.name()) ->
+        SQLMetrics.createV2CustomMetric(sparkContext, metric)
+    }.toMap
+
+  override protected lazy val sparkMetrics: Map[String, SQLMetric] =
+    ExternalLookupJoinExec.OPERATOR_METRICS.map { metric =>
+      val sqlMetric = if (metric.isTiming) {
+        SQLMetrics.createNanoTimingMetric(sparkContext, metric.description)
+      } else {
+        SQLMetrics.createMetric(sparkContext, metric.description)
+      }
+      metric.name -> sqlMetric
+    }.toMap
+
+  override protected def doExecute(): RDD[InternalRow] = {
+    postDriverMetrics(scan.reportDriverMetrics().map { metric =>
+      new CustomTaskMetric {
+        override def name(): String = ExternalLookupJoinExec.sourceMetricKey(metric.name())
+        override def value(): Long = metric.value()
+      }
+    })
+    val (streamCondition, joinedCondition) = splitResidualCondition
+    val evaluatorFactory = new ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory(
+      tableName,
+      lookupParameters,
+      nullSafeParameters,
+      lookupKeyCheck,
+      child.output,
+      lookupInput,
+      lookupTransforms,
+      transformedLookup,
+      output,
+      joinType,
+      streamCondition,
+      joinedCondition.map(_.transform {
+        case attr: Attribute => inputByLookupOutput.getOrElse(attr, attr)
+      }),
+      readerFactory,
+      math.min(ExternalLookupJoinExec.MAX_PARAMETER_ROWS_PER_REQUEST, maxParameterRowsPerRequest),
+      conf.getConf(SQLConf.JOIN_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_MAX_BATCH_BYTES),
+      cacheOptions,
+      ExternalLookupJoinMetrics(
+        outputRows = longMetric("numOutputRows"),
+        inputRows = longMetric("numInputRows"),
+        inputBatches = longMetric("numInputBatches"),
+        requests = longMetric("numLookupRequests"),
+        parameterRows = longMetric("numLookupParameterRows"),
+        cacheHits = longMetric("numCacheHits"),
+        lookupTime = longMetric("lookupTime")),
+      new ExternalLookupReaderMetrics(customMetrics))
+    if (conf.usePartitionEvaluator) {
+      child.execute().mapPartitionsWithEvaluator(evaluatorFactory)
+    } else {
+      child.execute().mapPartitionsWithIndexInternal { (index, input) =>
+        evaluatorFactory.createEvaluator().eval(index, input)
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  override protected def withNewChildInternal(newChild: SparkPlan): ExternalLookupJoinExec =
+    copy(child = newChild)
+
+  override def simpleString(maxFields: Int): String = {
+    Utils.redact(conf.stringRedactionPattern, s"$nodeName ${scan.description()}")
+  }
+
+  override protected def stringArgs: Iterator[Any] =
+    Iterator(child, simpleString(conf.maxToStringFields))
+}
+
+object ExternalLookupJoinExec {
+  /** The clock of the cache TTL; tests replace it. */
+  @volatile private[sql] var cacheClock: Clock = new SystemClock()

We'd like to keep TTL. A micro-batch can already run very long, for example an hour or more under `Trigger.AvailableNow`, and real-time mode will need it soon, so removing it now would only mean adding it back. The global test hook is gone. In [c45ebaea1e7](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/c45ebaea1e785c3674e8cc06b6872823725f1d62), the clock is passed into the physical join through the evaluator factory, and production uses the system ticker.

Done in [715364e7feb](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/715364e7feb368a24073954e6c43a9ce3a8e9ecf): when a range forces one parameter row per request, a batch takes all the stream rows of one key, and ends at the second distinct key. So three identical rows now send one request. The connector contract is unchanged.

issue.title: [SPARK-61348][SS] Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR lets the stream-stream join bound solver derive a range cutoff only for a TIMESTAMP
column of the input it bounds. The analysis check for outer and semi joins and runtime range
eviction both use this solver, so both now accept the same columns.

**Stack.** This is PR 5 of 7 and depends on #60282. Until the earlier PRs merge, this PR also shows their commits, and the merge commits bring in their review fixes. Please review only this PR's own commits: [bc4367d9300](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60283/commits/bc4367d93000dc04334a0bb0e7e0f877db9a8ad9) (the fix) and [f885a5a0876](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60283/commits/f885a5a08766d0a1ce402ab9dff35dce9af28b98) (review round 1). Merge order:

1. #60279 [SPARK-61344](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61344): Fix stream-stream join range eviction column and output watermark
2. #60280 [SPARK-61345](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61345): Fix stream-stream join watermark direction and equality-key eviction
3. #60281 [SPARK-61346](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61346): Derive stream-stream join range eviction from the late-filtering event time
4. #60282 [SPARK-61347](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61347): Evict stream-stream join range state without a watermark on the stored side
5. #60283 [SPARK-61348](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61348): Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins (this PR)
6. #60284 [SPARK-61349](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61349): Ignore constant-only bounds in stream-stream join state eviction
7. #60286 [SPARK-61350](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61350): Reject negative watermark terms in stream-stream join eviction bounds

- A range bound on a column that is not TIMESTAMP no longer makes an outer or left semi join
  valid. This covers numeric columns, such as `n > CAST(rightTime AS BIGINT)`, DATE and
  TIMESTAMP_NTZ columns, which the comparison casts to TIMESTAMP, and time windows compared as a
  whole, such as `leftWindow > rightWindow`. Equality keys on the other input's event time or its
  time window still qualify.
- An inner join whose only bound on an input compares whole time windows no longer evicts that
  input's state. Earlier versions evicted such windows by their end, which drops matches when the
  stored windows are shorter than the other input's windows.
- The analysis error, the join guide and the migration guide state the rule.

The checkpoint version is unchanged. Apart from analysis, the only runtime change is that some
inner joins keep rows that they used to evict, and state written before this change stays valid
when fewer rows are evicted.

### Why are the changes needed?

The analysis check accepted range bounds on numeric, DATE and TIMESTAMP_NTZ columns, although
runtime range eviction compares the cutoff, in timestamp units, with the column itself and only
tries TIMESTAMP columns. Such outer joins could never emit their unmatched rows. Whole-window
comparisons were evicted by window end, which is wrong when the stored windows are shorter than
the other input's windows: a later, longer window can still order below an evicted one.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Outer and left semi joins whose only bound on the finalized input is a range condition on a
numeric, DATE, TIMESTAMP_NTZ or time window column fail analysis, and the error message states
the TIMESTAMP-column rule. Inner joins whose only bound on an input compares whole time windows
keep that input's state. Timestamp range joins and equality joins on event time or time windows
remain supported.

### How was this patch tested?

All commands below passed on this branch, rebased on Apache Spark master: 1,507 tests, 0 failures.

```sh
build/sbt 'catalyst/testOnly *StreamingJoinHelperSuite *UnsupportedOperationsSuite'  # 332
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingJoinWatermarkAdmissionSuite *StreamingJoinEqualityOutputWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinSelectedEventTimeSuite *StreamingJoinNumericWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinOutputWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinEqualityWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinOneSidedWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinRangeWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinRangeEvictionSuite *StreamingSymmetricHashJoinHelperSuite *MultiStatefulOperatorsSuite *OffsetSeqLogSuite *SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerSuite *SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerEventTimeInKeySuite'  # 247
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingJoinCheckpointCompatibilitySuite *StreamingJoinRangeEvictionCheckpointSuite'  # 239
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingInnerJoinV4Suite *StreamingOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingFullOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinV4Suite *StreamingInnerJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingInnerJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithoutVCFSuite'  # 689
```

Scalastyle for catalyst and sql, main and test sources: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

The new query test failed before the fix: the left outer query started instead of throwing `AnalysisException`. It runs once, because analysis rejects the plan before any state format is used.

Review round 1: all 7 new tests fail on the code of #60282 before this round's fixes.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

Thanks for the [review](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60283#pullrequestreview-5839775963). Answers to the items in its summary; the inline comments are answered in their threads.

- **Shared repair plan 1.** Done ([f885a5a0876](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60283/commits/f885a5a08766d0a1ce402ab9dff35dce9af28b98)): the error message adds the TIMESTAMP-column rule, and the guides apply it to range conditions only, keeping equality on event time or a time window as a qualifying constraint.
- **PR description: runtime change.** Updated: the description now says that an inner join whose only bound compares whole windows keeps that input's state, and that the checkpoint version stays unchanged because state written before stays valid when fewer rows are evicted.
- **PR description: title and scope.** Updated: the title is now "Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins", and the description names numeric, DATE, TIMESTAMP_NTZ and time window columns, and left semi joins.
- **Decision challenge: left semi joins with a numeric bound.** The rejection stays the default: a left semi join whose only bound is on a numeric column never evicts its left state, so it does not meet the requirement that the admission check enforces. Users who need the old admission can set `spark.sql.streaming.join.checkFinalization.enabled` to `false` ([c4bdbf09fdb](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60280/commits/c4bdbf09fdbea72fee5ab22ad03b839f1d9d7a37)). The rejection then becomes a warning, and the query runs as before with unbounded left state, while eviction keeps the corrected rules. The migration guide names the conf.
