+  SparkIllegalStateException, TaskContext}
+import org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.InternalRow
+import org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.expressions.{Attribute, CollationKey, Expression,
+  GenericInternalRow, JoinedRow, Predicate, SpecializedGetters, UnsafeProjection, UnsafeRow}
+import org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.optimizer.NormalizeFloatingNumbers
+import org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.plans.{Inner, JoinType, LeftOuter}
+import org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.util.ArrayData
+import org.apache.spark.sql.connector.metric.CustomTaskMetric
+import org.apache.spark.sql.connector.read.{ExternalLookupReader, ExternalLookupReaderFactory,
+  ExternalLookupResultCursor}
+import org.apache.spark.sql.errors.QueryExecutionErrors
+import org.apache.spark.sql.execution.metric.{CustomMetrics, SQLMetric}
+import org.apache.spark.sql.types.{ArrayType, DataType, Decimal, DecimalType, MapType,
+  StructType}
+import org.apache.spark.util.Utils
+
+/**
+ * Creates the partition evaluators of an [[ExternalLookupJoinExec]]. The factory is sent to the
+ * tasks, so it holds only what they need; the plan node and its scan stay on the driver.
+ *
+ * An evaluator joins its partition one batch of up to `maxParameterRowsPerRequest` stream rows at
+ * a time. For each batch it sends one request with the distinct parameters that can match, and
+ * streams the connector's result rows into output rows. Parameters are deduplicated per request,
+ * that is within one batch: a key repeated in a later batch is requested again.
+ *
+ * Spark does not trust the connector with the selected lookup predicates: it evaluates
+ * `lookupKeyCheck` on every row that the connector returns, against the request row that the row
+ * answers, and drops a row that fails it, before it joins the row. The stream rows that share a
+ * request row have Spark-equal parameters, so one check serves all of them.
+ *
+ * The join condition comes in two parts: `streamCondition` reads only stream columns and is
+ * evaluated on each stream row before the request, and `residualCondition` is evaluated on the
+ * joined rows. A stream row that fails `streamCondition` cannot match, so its parameters are not
+ * sent.
+ */
+class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory(
+    tableName: String,
+    lookupParameters: Seq[Expression],
+    nullSafeParameters: Seq[Boolean],
+    lookupKeyCheck: Option[Expression],
+    streamOutput: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupInput: Seq[Attribute],
+    output: Seq[Attribute],
+    joinType: JoinType,
+    streamCondition: Option[Expression],
+    residualCondition: Option[Expression],
+    readerFactory: ExternalLookupReaderFactory,
+    maxParameterRowsPerRequest: Int,
+    maxBatchBytes: Long,
+    metrics: ExternalLookupJoinMetrics,
+    readerMetrics: ExternalLookupReaderMetrics)
+  extends PartitionEvaluatorFactory[InternalRow, InternalRow] {
+
+  require(lookupParameters.length == nullSafeParameters.length,
+    "Every external lookup parameter must define its null semantics")
+
+  override def createEvaluator(): PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] =
+    new ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator
+
+  private class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator extends PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] {
+    override def eval(
+        partitionIndex: Int,
+        inputs: Iterator[InternalRow]*): Iterator[InternalRow] = {
+      assert(inputs.length == 1)
+      new PartitionJoinIterator(inputs.head, partitionIndex)
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Joins one partition batch by batch, and closes its reader after the last batch. */
+  private class PartitionJoinIterator(input: Iterator[InternalRow], partitionIndex: Int)
+    extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    private val reader = new LookupReader
+    private val parameters = new LookupParameters(partitionIndex)
+    private val resultRows = new LookupResultRows
+    private val joinOutput = new JoinOutput(partitionIndex)
+    private var batch: Iterator[InternalRow] = Iterator.empty
+    private var inputExhausted = false
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      batch.hasNext
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      if (!batch.hasNext) {
+        throw new SparkIllegalStateException(
+          errorClass = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+          messageParameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup join exhausted"))
+      }
+      batch.next()
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryAdvance(): Unit = {
+      while (!batch.hasNext && !inputExhausted) {
+        val rows = readBatch()
+        if (rows.nonEmpty) {
+          batch = new BatchJoinIterator(rows, parameters, resultRows, joinOutput, reader)
+        }
+        inputExhausted = !input.hasNext
+      }
+      if (inputExhausted && !batch.hasNext) reader.close()
+    }
+
+    private lazy val toUnsafe = UnsafeProjection.create(streamOutput, streamOutput)
+
+    // An array, because a batch's rows are read by position for every key, match and output row.
+    // The batch holds its rows until its request is read, so it stops once their copies reach
+    // maxBatchBytes, keeping the row that reaches it, as well as at maxParameterRowsPerRequest
+    // rows. It always takes one row.
+    private def readBatch(): Array[InternalRow] = {
+      val rows = mutable.ArrayBuffer.empty[InternalRow]
+      var bytes = 0L
+      while (rows.length < maxParameterRowsPerRequest && bytes < maxBatchBytes && input.hasNext) {
+        val row = input.next() match {
+          case unsafe: UnsafeRow => unsafe.copy()
+          case other => toUnsafe(other).copy()
+        }
+        bytes += row.getSizeInBytes
+        rows += row
+      }
+      rows.toArray
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** The stream rows that share a key, and the one request row sent for them. */
+  private case class KeyEntry(requestRow: UnsafeRow, rowIndexes: mutable.ArrayBuffer[Int])
+
+  /**
+   * Joins one batch of stream rows. Rows whose parameters are equal under Spark equality share
+   * one request row, and every result row for a request row that satisfies the selected lookup
+   * predicates joins all the stream rows sharing it. A stream row is finished, which may emit its
+   * unmatched output row, once no more result rows can match it.
+   *
+   * Output rows are projected into a reused row on `next()`, so the consumer copies the rows it
+   * retains, as with other join iterators.
+   */
+  private class BatchJoinIterator(
+      rows: Array[InternalRow],
+      parameters: LookupParameters,
+      resultRows: LookupResultRows,
+      joinOutput: JoinOutput,
+      reader: LookupReader) extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    metrics.inputRows += rows.length
+    metrics.inputBatches += 1
+
+    private val matched = Array.fill(rows.length)(false)
+    private val finished = mutable.BitSet.empty
+    // Output rows not yet returned: a stream row index and the lookup row it is joined with.
+    private val pending = mutable.Queue.empty[(Int, InternalRow)]
+
+    // One entry for each distinct key that can match, in the order of first occurrence. A row
+    // that can never match, because it fails the stream condition or has a null parameter, is
+    // finished right away, and its key is not requested. The stream condition is checked before
+    // the key is computed, so that it can guard the parameter expressions.
+    private val keyEntries = mutable.LinkedHashMap.empty[UnsafeRow, KeyEntry]
+    rows.indices.foreach { index =>
+      lazy val key = parameters.key(rows(index))
+      if (!joinOutput.canMatch(rows(index)) || parameters.matchesNothing(key)) {
+        finish(index)
+      } else {
+        keyEntries.get(key) match {
+          case Some(entry) => entry.rowIndexes += index
+          case None => keyEntries.put(
+            key.copy(),
+            KeyEntry(parameters.requestRow(rows(index)), mutable.ArrayBuffer(index)))
+        }
+      }
+    }
+    private val requestedKeys = keyEntries.keys.toArray
+
+    // No connector request, and no reader, when no key can match. The connector gets copies of
+    // the request rows, so that the ones that Spark checks the results against stay its own.
+    private var cursor: ExternalLookupResultCursor =
+      if (keyEntries.isEmpty) EmptyLookupCursor
+      else connectorCall(reader.lookup(keyEntries.values.map(_.requestRow.copy()).toArray))
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      pending.nonEmpty
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      if (pending.isEmpty) throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+      val (index, lookupRow) = pending.dequeue()
+      joinOutput.project(rows(index), lookupRow)
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryFillPending(): Unit = {
+      try {
+        while (pending.isEmpty && advanceCursor()) {
+          reader.resultRowRead()
+          // A close() during either call fails the read before Spark copies or joins the row.
+          val start = System.nanoTime()
+          val ordinal = cursor.inputOrdinal()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val connectorRow = cursor.get()
+          metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+          if (connectorRow == null) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName, "NULL_RESULT", Map("method" -> "ExternalLookupResultCursor.get()"))
+          }
+          val key = requestedKey(ordinal)
+          val resultRow = reader.copyRow(resultRows.validatedCopy(connectorRow))
+          if (parameters.selectedPredicatesHold(keyEntries(key).requestRow, resultRow)) {
+            joinResultRow(key, resultRow)
+          }
+        }
+        if (pending.isEmpty) finishCursor(completed = true)
+      } catch {
+        case error: Throwable =>
+          Utils.tryWithSafeFinally(throw error) {
+            finishCursor(completed = false)
+          }
+      }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Advances the connector's cursor, unless the reader was closed meanwhile. A close() while
+     * next() ran fails the read once next() returns: Spark then reads no row from the closed
+     * cursor, and does not take a missing row for a complete result.
+     */
+    private def advanceCursor(): Boolean = (cursor ne EmptyLookupCursor) && {
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      val advanced = connectorCall(cursor.next())
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      advanced
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Runs a connector call and adds its time to the lookup time metric, which counts only the
+     * time in the connector, not that of the work above the join while a cursor is open.
+     */
+    private def connectorCall[T](call: => T): T = {
+      val start = System.nanoTime()
+      try call finally metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+    }
+
+    private def requestedKey(ordinal: Int): UnsafeRow = {
+      if (ordinal < 0 || ordinal >= requestedKeys.length) {
+        throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+          tableName,
+          "INVALID_INPUT_ORDINAL",
+          Map("ordinal" -> ordinal.toString, "numParameterRows" -> requestedKeys.length.toString))
+      }
+      requestedKeys(ordinal)
+    }
+
+    private def joinResultRow(key: UnsafeRow, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit =
+      keyEntries(key).rowIndexes.foreach(joinMatch(_, lookupRow))
+
+    private def joinMatch(index: Int, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit = {
+      if (joinOutput.matches(rows(index), lookupRow)) {
+        matched(index) = true
+        joinOutput.matched(lookupRow).foreach(emit(index, _))
+      }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Closes the cursor once. After a complete read, finishes every stream row that was waiting for
+     * its results. After a failure or a close, the results may be partial, so it finishes none:
+     * a row without a match could be a row whose match was never read. Once the reader is closed,
+     * its close owns the cursor and the reader's metrics, so the join makes no further connector
+     * call.
+     */
+    private def finishCursor(completed: Boolean): Unit = if (cursor ne EmptyLookupCursor) {
+      cursor = EmptyLookupCursor
+      if (!reader.isClosed) {
+        try {
+          connectorCall(reader.closeCursor())
+        } finally {
+          reader.updateMetrics()
+        }
+      }
+      if (completed) keyEntries.values.foreach(_.rowIndexes.foreach(finish))
+    }
+
+    private def finish(index: Int): Unit = if (!finished.contains(index)) {
+      finished += index
+      if (!matched(index)) joinOutput.unmatched.foreach(emit(index, _))
+    }
+
+    private def emit(index: Int, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit = {
+      pending.enqueue(index -> lookupRow)
+      metrics.outputRows += 1
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** The cursor of a batch that sends no request, or whose cursor is finished. */
+  private object EmptyLookupCursor extends ExternalLookupResultCursor {
+    override def next(): Boolean = false
+    override def inputOrdinal(): Int = throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+    override def get(): InternalRow = throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+    override def close(): Unit = {}
+  }
+
+  /** A check of one value slot: a field of a row, or an element of an array. */
+  private type SlotCheck = (SpecializedGetters, Int) => Unit
+
+  /**
+   * Validates each row that the connector returns, and copies it once into Spark's own row before
+   * Spark checks, joins or keeps it. A connector may reuse its row and its buffers, byte arrays
+   * included, so a row that Spark still holds must not share them. A value that breaks its type
+   * fails the task, at any nested level: a null in a field, array element or map value that the
+   * table or the read schema declares NOT NULL, or a decimal that does not fit its precision and
+   * scale. Spark already relied on them while it optimized the query. The checks are built once
+   * from the read schema, and a field whose type has nothing to check costs nothing per row.
+   */
+  private class LookupResultRows {
+    private val copy = UnsafeProjection.create(lookupInput, lookupInput)
+    private val fieldChecks = lookupInput.zipWithIndex.flatMap { case (field, ordinal) =>
+      slotCheck(field.dataType, field.nullable, Seq(field.name)).map(ordinal -> _)
+    }
+
+    /** The row, validated and copied into a row that Spark owns. */
+    def validatedCopy(resultRow: InternalRow): UnsafeRow = {
+      fieldChecks.foreach { case (ordinal, check) => check(resultRow, ordinal) }
+      copy(resultRow).copy()
+    }
+
+    /** The check of a slot of this type, at this field path, or None if it has nothing to check. */
+    private def slotCheck(
+        dataType: DataType,
+        nullable: Boolean,
+        path: Seq[String]): Option[SlotCheck] = {
+      val valueCheck = nonNullValueCheck(dataType, path)
+      if (nullable && valueCheck.isEmpty) {
+        None
+      } else {
+        Some { (values, ordinal) =>
+          if (!values.isNullAt(ordinal)) {
+            valueCheck.foreach(_(values, ordinal))
+          } else if (!nullable) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName,
+              "NULL_IN_NOT_NULL_FIELD",
+              Map("field" -> QueryExecutionErrors.toSQLId(path)))
+          }
+        }
+      }

issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR fixes when a stream-stream join removes rows from its state and which watermark it forwards downstream.

**Stack.** This is PR 1 of 7. Each PR fixes a separate bug in stream-stream join state eviction and builds on the one before it. This PR has no dependency, so all of it is up for review: [b42068e35be](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60279/commits/b42068e35be610ea06a0b35d9994f3a59c088ac1) (the fix) and [4fd804c5931](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60279/commits/4fd804c59319e26930682a4838f73f995b148c23) (review round 1). Please merge in this order:

1. #60279 [SPARK-61344](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61344): Fix stream-stream join range eviction column and output watermark (this PR)
2. #60280 [SPARK-61345](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61345): Fix stream-stream join watermark direction and equality-key eviction
3. #60281 [SPARK-61346](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61346): Derive stream-stream join range eviction from the late-filtering event time
4. #60282 [SPARK-61347](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61347): Evict stream-stream join range state without a watermark on the stored side
5. #60283 [SPARK-61348](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61348): Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins
6. #60284 [SPARK-61349](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61349): Ignore constant-only bounds in stream-stream join state eviction
7. #60286 [SPARK-61350](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61350): Reject negative watermark terms in stream-stream join eviction bounds

- **Range eviction on the bounded column.** Attach each range-eviction cutoff to the timestamp column that the join condition actually bounds, and use that column for value eviction and for the V4 timestamp index. The input's event-time column is tried first. If it has no bound, the first other timestamp column in schema order with a bound is used. The V4 matching scan applies its event-time window only when both indexes store event-time columns. Timestamp eviction never removes a row whose indexed timestamp is null; the next item covers rows that are evicted on that column. V4 stores such a row at the very start of the timestamp range, which only a real event time in the first millisecond of ISO year -290308 could share.
- **Rows that can never match.** A row whose eviction column is NULL can never satisfy the join condition, because that column is an equality key or a comparison in the join condition bounds it. Eviction never removes it either, because its eviction predicate is unknown. Handle it like a row that fails the pre-join filter: a preserved side of an outer join emits it padded with nulls at once, and no side stores it.
- **Conservative output watermark.** Derive each side's output bound from its actual eviction predicate. A side contributes its cutoff only when the predicate constrains its own event-time column or event-time key. Otherwise it contributes 0 and holds the output watermark back, because buffered rows can still emit older event times: the bound is on a different column, there is no bound, or the equality keys are crossed. The join holds back only for an input whose event time reaches the next stateful operator, found by following that operator's event-time column down to the join. When the plan between them has another shape, for example a union, it holds back for both inputs.
- **Checkpoint validation.** Add the internal conf `spark.sql.streaming.join.checkpointWatermarkSemanticsVersion` (version 1) and pin it in the offset log. An older checkpoint is accepted for joins without watermarks, joins with an unambiguous aligned event-time equality key, and two-sided time-interval joins on the inputs' own event times with exact constant intervals, such as `rightTime BETWEEN leftTime AND leftTime + INTERVAL 1 HOUR`. For these shapes the old and the corrected derivations solve the same conditions for the same columns, so the saved rows keep their meaning. Other shapes fail with the new error condition `STREAMING_JOIN_CHECKPOINT_INCOMPATIBLE` before any state is opened: bounds on another column, one-directional bounds, casts, and whole-day intervals in a time zone with daylight saving time. The version only validates compatibility; it does not select a legacy execution path. Later PRs in this stack raise it when they change which rows are kept.
- **Solver warnings.** When the solved bound still refers to a column after the watermark is substituted, the solver returns no bound without logging a warning. Before, it threw, and every batch logged a WARN with a stack trace.
- **Docs.** The Structured Streaming migration guide explains the rejection and how to recover. The join guide notes that the join condition and the watermarks decide which column is used to remove rows.

### Why are the changes needed?

- For `rightTime BETWEEN leftTime AND expiry`, a left row can still match after `leftTime` passes the watermark. Applying the `expiry` cutoff to `leftTime` removes the row too early, loses later matches, and can emit a premature outer null row.
- An inner join on a non-time key can keep a left row at time 5 while the input watermark advances to 20, and then match a right row at time 100. Forwarding watermark 20 makes a downstream deduplication drop the valid output at time 5.
- For `la = ra AND lb = rb` with watermarks on `la` and `rb`, a buffered right row `(100, 5)` can match a new left row after watermark 40. The join emits the match, but a downstream window aggregate has already advanced past it and drops it.
- For `rightTime BETWEEN leftStart AND leftEnd`, a left row with a NULL `leftEnd`, such as an open interval, can never match. Once range eviction uses `leftEnd`, eviction could never remove that row either, so a left outer join would keep it forever and never emit it. Released versions emitted it once `leftStart` passed the watermark.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. These are corrections relative to all released versions.

- Range eviction and unmatched outer output are corrected in state formats V2, V3 and V4.
- Join output that carries old event times now reaches downstream stateful operators. An operator that uses the event time of an input without an eviction bound may keep more state, finalize later, or stop emitting results.
- Older checkpoints of affected join shapes fail with `STREAMING_JOIN_CHECKPOINT_INCOMPATIBLE`, even if the query never produced incorrect results. Two-sided time-interval joins on the inputs' own event times, including the bundled Spark 2.4.0 and 3.5.1 checkpoints, resume. The migration guide describes the recovery for the others: start a new checkpoint, replay the required input, and account for previously written output.
- On a preserved side of an outer join, a row whose eviction column is NULL is emitted padded with nulls in the batch it arrives. No join keeps such a row in state. Before, such rows could stay in state forever: always in V2 and V3, and in V4 unless an eviction scan started at the beginning of the index.

### How was this patch tested?

All commands below passed on this branch, rebased on Apache Spark master: 1,182 tests, 0 failures.

```sh
build/sbt 'catalyst/testOnly *StreamingJoinHelperSuite *UnsupportedOperationsSuite'  # 237
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingJoinEqualityOutputWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinOutputWatermarkSuite *StreamingJoinRangeEvictionSuite *StreamingSymmetricHashJoinHelperSuite *MultiStatefulOperatorsSuite *OffsetSeqLogSuite *SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerSuite *SymmetricHashJoinStateManagerEventTimeInKeySuite'  # 152
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingJoinCheckpointCompatibilitySuite *StreamingJoinRangeEvictionCheckpointSuite'  # 185
build/sbt 'sql/testOnly *StreamingInnerJoinV4Suite *StreamingOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingFullOuterJoinV4Suite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinV4Suite *StreamingInnerJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithVCFSuite *StreamingInnerJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingFullOuterJoinWithoutVCFSuite *StreamingLeftSemiJoinWithoutVCFSuite'  # 567
build/sbt 'hive/testOnly *SparkConfigBindingPolicySuite'  # 3
build/sbt 'core/testOnly *SparkThrowableSuite'  # 38
```

Scalastyle for catalyst and sql, main and test sources: 0 errors, 0 warnings.

The new regression tests failed before their fixes: the delayed range-expiry match, the downstream deduplication of an old match, and the downstream window aggregate after crossed keys. The V4 null indexed-timestamp tests also failed before their fix: V4 removed the null row (2 rows evicted instead of 1), and a null window struct threw a `NullPointerException`. The collision test failed before its fix: evicting real rows stamped in the first millisecond after the epoch also removed the null-timestamp row.

Both bundled historical join checkpoints (Spark 2.4.0 and 3.5.1) are two-sided time-interval joins on the inputs' own event times. They now resume, and the restored SPARK-26187 and SPARK-48687 tests check their results. No historical equality-join checkpoint is bundled.

Review round 1: the new tests for rows with a NULL eviction column fail with that fix reverted.

The base solver also took bounds that this stack drops (constant-only conjuncts, numeric columns, negative watermark terms), so a comparison through today's solver could call two derivations equal when the base evicted differently. Keeping the base solver only for the comparison would keep a second copy of the code this stack fixes.

That derivation is the bug that SPARK-61345 (#60280), the next PR in the same release, fixes: right rows are not filtered as late, so a right row can still match a left row that the base already evicted. SPARK-61345 changes the eviction and output watermark for exactly this shape and raises the checkpoint version, so the release must reject these checkpoints anyway.

Master is wrong for this shape too: it applies the cutoff solved for `expiry` to `leftTime`, so it emits the left rows with nulls at watermark 400 s although `expiry` is 700 s, and then loses the match from a right row at 460 s. Keeping master's eviction here would therefore bring back wrong output. Moving the TIMESTAMP rule into this PR would leave SPARK-61348 with almost no change of its own, so we are keeping the split.
- **The version only validates and never selects the base behavior.** This is deliberate: the base derivation drops matches and emits null rows too early, so we do not offer a way to run it. Joins whose derivation does not change now resume (above). SPARK-61345 (#60280) adds the internal conf `spark.sql.streaming.join.checkFinalization.enabled` ([c4bdbf09fdb](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60280/commits/c4bdbf09fdbea72fee5ab22ad03b839f1d9d7a37)): it turns the stack's new outer and semi admission failures into warnings, while eviction stays corrected.

- **Restarting from an older checkpoint now fails.** Narrowed: time-interval joins on the inputs' own event times, including the bundled 2.4.0 and 3.5.1 checkpoints, now resume ([4fd804c5931](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60279/commits/4fd804c59319e26930682a4838f73f995b148c23)). - **Existing checkpoints of all join types go through the new restart check.** Yes; with [4fd804c5931](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60279/commits/4fd804c59319e26930682a4838f73f995b148c23) the check accepts every shape whose saved rows keep their meaning, as described above.

Raising that would block a downgrade of every streaming query, not only of joins. We keep the migration guide's warning against using a checkpoint written by the new version with an older one. For the shapes that resume, the saved rows mean the same in both versions, so a downgrade of those joins reads state that means the same in both versions.

issue.title: [SPARK-61349][SS] Ignore constant-only bounds in stream-stream join state eviction
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR ignores constant-only conditions when deriving an advancing state eviction bound for a stream-stream join.

**Stack.** This is PR 6 of 7 and depends on #60283. Until the earlier PRs merge, this PR also shows their commits, and the merge commits bring in their review fixes. Please review only this PR's own commits: [58691f8f798](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60284/commits/58691f8f798fd1935785076cfc7c2efe8fb07a8b) (the fix) and [3efe52a82f2](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60284/commits/3efe52a82f261a9f9e52638a9ecdb71fb70e5737) (review round 1). Merge order:

1. #60279 [SPARK-61344](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61344): Fix stream-stream join range eviction column and output watermark
2. #60280 [SPARK-61345](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61345): Fix stream-stream join watermark direction and equality-key eviction
3. #60281 [SPARK-61346](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61346): Derive stream-stream join range eviction from the late-filtering event time
4. #60282 [SPARK-61347](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61347): Evict stream-stream join range state without a watermark on the stored side
5. #60283 [SPARK-61348](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61348): Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins
6. #60284 [SPARK-61349](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61349): Ignore constant-only bounds in stream-stream join state eviction (this PR)
7. #60286 [SPARK-61350](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61350): Reject negative watermark terms in stream-stream join eviction bounds

- A conjunct that compares a state column only with a constant, such as `CAST(lt AS BIGINT) > 10`, no longer caps the eviction bound. The opposite-input range bound in the same conjunction is kept.
- Raise the checkpoint version to 5. Older checkpoints of affected join shapes are rejected with `STREAMING_JOIN_CHECKPOINT_INCOMPATIBLE` before any state is opened.
- The migration guide and the join guide state that constant-only bounds do not qualify.

### Why are the changes needed?

For `lt > rt - INTERVAL 5 SECONDS AND CAST(lt AS BIGINT) > 10`, the constant cutoff 10 capped eviction forever. At watermark 39, the valid range cutoff is 34, so an unmatched left row with `lt = 20` must be finalized.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Outer joins emit eligible unmatched rows instead of keeping them indefinitely when a constant-only conjunct is present. Outer and semi joins whose only bound is constant fail analysis.

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR derives a range-eviction bound only from the opposite input's timestamp that late-input filtering uses.

**Stack.** This is PR 3 of 7 and depends on #60280. Until the earlier PRs merge, this PR also shows their commits, and the merge commits bring in their review fixes. Please review only this PR's own commits: [da50a738afe](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/60281/commits/da50a738afe416251ec2260071fb7ae12e28dd48) (the fix). Merge order:

1. #60279 [SPARK-61344](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61344): Fix stream-stream join range eviction column and output watermark
2. #60280 [SPARK-61345](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61345): Fix stream-stream join watermark direction and equality-key eviction
3. #60281 [SPARK-61346](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61346): Derive stream-stream join range eviction from the late-filtering event time (this PR)
4. #60282 [SPARK-61347](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61347): Evict stream-stream join range state without a watermark on the stored side
5. #60283 [SPARK-61348](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61348): Reject non-timestamp range bounds in stream-stream outer and semi joins
6. #60284 [SPARK-61349](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61349): Ignore constant-only bounds in stream-stream join state eviction
7. #60286 [SPARK-61350](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-61350): Reject negative watermark terms in stream-stream join eviction bounds

- When the opposite input carries several watermarked columns, use only the first one, which is the column that late-input filtering checks, as the opposite time when inferring the state's range bound.
- Raise the checkpoint version to 3. Older checkpoints of affected join shapes are rejected with `STREAMING_JOIN_CHECKPOINT_INCOMPATIBLE` before any state is opened.

### Why are the changes needed?

With `spark.sql.streaming.statefulOperator.allowMultiple=false`, a join input can carry several watermarked columns, for example the output of an upstream join. An upstream join can emit `(u = 100, v = 5)` after the watermark reaches 50. A downstream join filters late input on `u` but has the condition `l > v`. Substituting watermark 50 for `v` evicts `l = 10`, although the row with `v = 5` still passes late filtering and matches it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Valid matches are preserved in V2 and V3 with `spark.sql.streaming.statefulOperator.allowMultiple=false`. V4 and the default mode already reject multiple distinct event-time columns. The cost of the fix: with `spark.sql.streaming.statefulOperator.allowMultiple=false`, an inner join whose condition bounds one input only through a later watermarked column of the other input no longer evicts that input's state, so the state can grow without bound. To keep eviction, bound it through the first watermarked column, which is the one late filtering uses.

+  Cast, CurrentBatchTimestamp, EqualNullSafe, EqualTo, Expression, ExprUtils,

+  NamedExpression, PythonUDF, SubqueryExpression}
+import org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.plans.{Inner, JoinType, LeftAnti, LeftOuter, LeftSemi}

+import org.apache.spark.sql.types.{BinaryType, BooleanType, ByteType, CharType, DataType,

+  TimestampNTZType, TimestampType, VarcharType}

+/**
+ * Marks the plan below it as the lookup side that the `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint asks an external
+ * lookup join to read. The external lookup join rules consume it when they form the join.
+ *
+ * Join strategy hints are [[ResolvedHint]] nodes with a [[JoinStrategyHint]]. This hint is not,
+ * because that representation cannot keep two of its guarantees:
+ *  - A strategy hint that conflicts with it must fail the query. [[HintInfo]] holds one strategy,
+ *    and `ResolveJoinStrategyHints` merges a strategy hint on an already hinted relation into the
+ *    existing [[ResolvedHint]] with `HintInfo.merge`, which keeps one strategy and only warns.
+ *  - It selects how the lookup side is read, not a physical join. `EliminateResolvedHint` moves
+ *    every [[ResolvedHint]] it can attach into `Join.hint`, for physical join selection.
+ */
+case class ExternalLookupHint(child: LogicalPlan) extends UnaryNode {
+  override def output: Seq[Attribute] = child.output
+
+  final override val nodePatterns: Seq[TreePattern] = Seq(EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT)
+
+  override protected def withNewChildInternal(newChild: LogicalPlan): ExternalLookupHint =
+    copy(child = newChild)
+}
+
+/**
+ * A lookup join retained through ordinary expression and operator optimization.
+ *
+ * @param requiredLookupOutput Lookup-side attributes still required above this join. They are
+ *   part of this node's references, so column pruning keeps them on the lookup side.
+ *   `ColumnPruning` narrows them to what the parent reads, and `PrepareExternalLookupJoin` prunes
+ *   the lookup scan to them.
+ */

+    left: LogicalPlan,
+    right: LogicalPlan,
+    joinType: JoinType,
+    condition: Option[Expression],
+    requiredLookupOutput: Seq[Attribute]) extends BinaryNode {
+
+  final override val nodePatterns: Seq[TreePattern] = Seq(EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN)
+
+  override def output: Seq[Attribute] = joinType match {
+    case Inner => left.output ++ right.output
+    case LeftOuter => left.output ++ right.output.map(_.withNullability(true))
+    case LeftSemi | LeftAnti => left.output
+    case other => throw SparkException.internalError(s"Unexpected external lookup join type $other")
+  }

+  // As an ordinary join's: a semi or anti join returns at most its stream rows, and the other join
+  // types get the product of both sides' sizes.

+    case _ => super.stats
+  }
+
+  override def maxRows: Option[Long] = joinType match {

+    case _ => None
+  }
+
+  override protected def withNewChildrenInternal(
+      newLeft: LogicalPlan,
+      newRight: LogicalPlan): ExternalLookupJoin = copy(left = newLeft, right = newRight)
+}
+
+/**
+ * The join-condition and lookup-side shapes that an external lookup join can run. Analysis,
+ * lookup planning and the optimizer rules for lookup joins share them.
+ */
+object ExternalLookupJoinShapes {
+  /**
+   * A lookup candidate: a comparison of a lookup column with a value, written with the lookup
+   * column on the left.
+   */
+  case class LookupComparison(
+      lookupField: Attribute,
+      parameter: Expression,
+      comparison: LookupKeyComparison)
+
+  /**
+   * `conjunct` of the condition of a lookup join as a lookup candidate: `=`, `<=>`, `<`, `<=`, `>`
+   * or `>=` between a bare lookup column and a value, in either operand order. When the lookup
+   * column is written on the right, the comparison is rebuilt with it on the left, so
+   * `s.ts < t.event_time` is offered as `event_time > ?`.
+   *
+   * The value is the other operand, which Spark evaluates for each stream row to fill the
+   * comparison's parameter. It may read only stream columns, and it may read none, as a literal
+   * does. A value that reads lookup columns, as in `t.a = t.b`, cannot be a parameter.
+   *

+   * comparison. A comparison on another column is an ordinary conjunct.
+   *

+   * @param lookupOutput The output of the join's right side, the lookup side.
+   */

+      streamOutput: AttributeSet,
+      lookupOutput: AttributeSet): Option[LookupComparison] = {

+      lookupOutput.contains(lookupField) && parameter.references.subsetOf(streamOutput)

+      case written: BinaryComparison =>

+          Seq(
+            (written.left, written.right, comparison),
+            (written.right, written.left, comparison.swapped)).collectFirst {
+            case (lookupField: Attribute, parameter, comparison)
+                if isLookupComparison(lookupField, parameter) &&

+          }
+        }
+      case _ => None
+    }
+  }

+   * Whether Spark offers the comparison on this lookup column, with this parameter.
+   *
+   * Spark evaluates every parameter on every stream row, before the other join conditions. That
+   * is safe for an equality, as a hash join evaluates its keys on every row too. A range is a
+   * join condition, which a join evaluates only after its keys match, so its parameter must be
+   * one that cannot fail, as `cannotFail` decides.
+   */

+      comparison: LookupKeyComparison,
+      lookupField: Attribute,
+      parameter: Expression): Boolean =
+    if (comparison.isRange) {
+      ExternalLookupKeyTypes.supportsRange(lookupField.dataType) && cannotFail(parameter)
+    } else {
+      ExternalLookupKeyTypes.supportsEquality(lookupField)
+    }
+
+  /**
+   * Whether a range parameter cannot fail: ExprUtils.canEvaluateUnconditionally accepts it, or it
+   * is a widening numeric cast of such a value. Analysis adds such a cast when the stream side has
+   * a narrower type than the lookup column, as an INT column compared with a BIGINT key.

+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Whether a cast converts every value of its source type: an integral type to a wider one, or
+   * an integral type or DECIMAL to a DECIMAL with room for all of its digits. `Cast.canUpCast`

+   */

+    case (from: IntegralType, to: IntegralType) => from.defaultSize < to.defaultSize

+    case (from: DecimalType, to: DecimalType) => to.isWiderThan(from)

+   */

+      case batchTimestamp: CurrentBatchTimestamp => Literal(null, batchTimestamp.dataType)
+    }.deterministic && !expression.exists {
+      case _: PythonUDF | _: ExternalUserDefinedFunction | _: SubqueryExpression => true
+      case _ => false

+   * parameter reads a stream column. One stored row can then match several parameter rows of a
+   * request, and the source would have to return it once for each of them, with each ordinal.

+   * same value in every parameter row, so a stored row that satisfies it matches only the
+   * parameter rows that the other comparisons select.
+   */
+  def oneParameterRowPerRequest(
+      parameters: Seq[Expression],
+      comparisons: Seq[LookupKeyComparison]): Boolean =
+    parameters.zip(comparisons).exists { case (parameter, comparison) =>
+      comparison.isRange && parameter.references.nonEmpty
+    }
+
+  /**
+   * `plan` with the current time of the micro-batch replaced by its value. IncrementalExecution
+   * replaces it after optimization, which does not reach the lookup-side stages of a prepared
+   * lookup join.
+   */
+  def withBatchTimestampValues(plan: LogicalPlan): LogicalPlan =
+    plan.transformAllExpressionsWithPruning(_.containsPattern(CURRENT_LIKE)) {
+      case batchTimestamp: CurrentBatchTimestamp => batchTimestamp.toLiteral
+    }
+}
+
+/**
+ * The comparison that a lookup predicate makes between a lookup column, on the left, and its
+ * parameter. `predicateName` is the name of the DSv2 `Predicate` that is offered for it: the SQL
+ * operator, as `V2ExpressionBuilder` names it.
+ */
+sealed abstract class LookupKeyComparison(val predicateName: String) extends Serializable {
+  /** The comparison of `key` with `parameter`, as Spark evaluates it. */
+  def apply(key: Expression, parameter: Expression): Expression
+
+  /** The same comparison with the operands swapped, so that `<` becomes `>`. */
+  def swapped: LookupKeyComparison
+
+  /** Whether one lookup column value can satisfy the comparison with several parameter values. */
+  def isRange: Boolean = true
+
+  /** Whether a NULL parameter can match, as with `<=>`. */
+  def nullSafe: Boolean = false
+}
+
+object LookupKeyComparison {
+  case object Equal extends LookupKeyComparison("=") {
+    override def apply(key: Expression, parameter: Expression): Expression =
+      EqualTo(key, parameter)
+    override def swapped: LookupKeyComparison = this
+    override def isRange: Boolean = false
+  }
+
+  case object NullSafeEqual extends LookupKeyComparison("<=>") {
+    override def apply(key: Expression, parameter: Expression): Expression =
+      EqualNullSafe(key, parameter)
+    override def swapped: LookupKeyComparison = this
+    override def isRange: Boolean = false
+    override def nullSafe: Boolean = true
+  }
+
+  case object Less extends LookupKeyComparison("<") {
+    override def apply(key: Expression, parameter: Expression): Expression =
+      LessThan(key, parameter)
+    override def swapped: LookupKeyComparison = Greater
+  }
+
+  case object LessOrEqual extends LookupKeyComparison("<=") {
+    override def apply(key: Expression, parameter: Expression): Expression =
+      LessThanOrEqual(key, parameter)
+    override def swapped: LookupKeyComparison = GreaterOrEqual
+  }
+
+  case object Greater extends LookupKeyComparison(">") {
+    override def apply(key: Expression, parameter: Expression): Expression =
+      GreaterThan(key, parameter)
+    override def swapped: LookupKeyComparison = Less
+  }
+
+  case object GreaterOrEqual extends LookupKeyComparison(">=") {
+    override def apply(key: Expression, parameter: Expression): Expression =
+      GreaterThanOrEqual(key, parameter)
+    override def swapped: LookupKeyComparison = LessOrEqual
+  }
+
+  /** The comparison that `comparison` makes, if it is one that Spark can offer. */
+  def of(comparison: BinaryComparison): Option[LookupKeyComparison] = comparison match {
+    case _: EqualTo => Some(Equal)
+    case _: EqualNullSafe => Some(NullSafeEqual)
+    case _: LessThan => Some(Less)
+    case _: LessThanOrEqual => Some(LessOrEqual)
+    case _: GreaterThan => Some(Greater)
+    case _: GreaterThanOrEqual => Some(GreaterOrEqual)
+    case _ => None
+  }
+}
+
+/** One optimized lookup-side operation, retained in evaluation order. */
+sealed trait ExternalLookupTransform {
+  def input: Seq[Attribute]
+  def output: Seq[Attribute]
+}
+
+case class ExternalLookupProject(
+    projectList: Seq[NamedExpression],
+    input: Seq[Attribute]) extends ExternalLookupTransform {
+  override def output: Seq[Attribute] = projectList.map(_.toAttribute)
+}
+
+case class ExternalLookupFilter(
+    condition: Expression,
+    input: Seq[Attribute]) extends ExternalLookupTransform {
+  override def output: Seq[Attribute] = input
+}
+
+/**
+ * A lookup join after its optimized lookup side has been converted to an external operation.
+ *
+ * @param lookupKeys The table column that each selected lookup predicate compares with the
+ *   parameter at the same position. Spark checks each row that the connector returns against
+ *   them, so the read schema must hold these columns.
+ * @param lookupKeyComparisons The comparison that each selected lookup predicate makes, such as
+ *   `=` or `<`, with the lookup column on the left. It tells how Spark checks the key.
+ */

+    child: LogicalPlan,
+    tableName: String,
+    @transient scan: Scan,
+    readerFactory: ExternalLookupReaderFactory,
+    maxParameterRowsPerRequest: Int,
+    lookupInput: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupOutput: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupTransforms: Seq[ExternalLookupTransform],
+    lookupParameters: Seq[Expression],
+    lookupKeys: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupKeyComparisons: Seq[LookupKeyComparison],
+    joinType: JoinType,
+    residualCondition: Option[Expression]) extends UnaryNode {
+

+    case other => throw SparkException.internalError(s"Unexpected external lookup join type $other")

+    streamCondition: Option[Expression],
+    residualCondition: Option[Expression],
+    readerFactory: ExternalLookupReaderFactory,
+    maxParameterRowsPerRequest: Int,
+    oneKeyPerBatch: Boolean,
+    maxBatchBytes: Long,
+    metrics: ExternalLookupJoinMetrics,
+    readerMetrics: ExternalLookupReaderMetrics)
+  extends PartitionEvaluatorFactory[InternalRow, InternalRow] {
+
+  require(lookupParameters.length == nullSafeParameters.length,
+    "Every external lookup parameter must define its null semantics")
+
+  override def createEvaluator(): PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] =
+    new ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator
+
+  private class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator extends PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] {
+    override def eval(
+        partitionIndex: Int,
+        inputs: Iterator[InternalRow]*): Iterator[InternalRow] = {
+      assert(inputs.length == 1)
+      new PartitionJoinIterator(inputs.head, partitionIndex)
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Joins one partition batch by batch, and closes its reader after the last batch. */
+  private class PartitionJoinIterator(input: Iterator[InternalRow], partitionIndex: Int)
+    extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    private val reader = new LookupReader
+    private val parameters = new LookupParameters(partitionIndex)
+    private val resultRows = new LookupResultRows
+    private val transforms = new LookupTransforms(partitionIndex)
+    private val joinOutput = new JoinOutput(partitionIndex)
+    private var batch: Iterator[InternalRow] = Iterator.empty
+    private var inputExhausted = false
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      batch.hasNext
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      if (!batch.hasNext) {
+        throw new SparkIllegalStateException(
+          errorClass = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+          messageParameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup join exhausted"))
+      }
+      batch.next()
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryAdvance(): Unit = {
+      while (!batch.hasNext && !inputExhausted) {
+        val rows = readBatch()
+        if (rows.nonEmpty) {
+          batch = new BatchJoinIterator(
+            rows, parameters, resultRows, transforms, joinOutput, reader)
+        }
+        inputExhausted = !hasInput
+      }
+      if (inputExhausted && !batch.hasNext) reader.close()
+    }
+
+    private lazy val toUnsafe = UnsafeProjection.create(streamOutput, streamOutput)
+
+    // When a request holds one parameter row because of a selected range, a batch takes the stream
+    // rows of one key rather than one stream row. It ends before the first row with another key,
+    // which starts the next batch. A row that cannot match has no key, and any batch takes it.
+    private var heldRow: UnsafeRow = null
+
+    private def hasInput: Boolean = heldRow != null || input.hasNext
+
+    private def nextRow(): UnsafeRow = if (heldRow != null) {
+      val row = heldRow
+      heldRow = null
+      row
+    } else {
+      input.next() match {
+        case unsafe: UnsafeRow => unsafe.copy()
+        case other => toUnsafe(other).copy()
+      }
+    }
+
+    /** The request row of a stream row that can match, in a reused row, or null. */
+    private def requestRowOf(row: InternalRow): UnsafeRow =
+      if (!joinOutput.canMatch(row)) null else {
+        val requestRow = parameters.requestRow(row)
+        if (parameters.matchesNothing(requestRow)) null else requestRow
+      }
+
+    // An array, because a batch's rows are read by position for every key, match and output row.
+    // The batch holds its rows until its request is read, so it stops once their copies reach
+    // maxBatchBytes, keeping the row that reaches it, as well as at maxParameterRowsPerRequest
+    // rows, or at another key with one key per batch. It always takes one row.
+    private def readBatch(): Array[InternalRow] = {
+      val rows = mutable.ArrayBuffer.empty[InternalRow]
+      var bytes = 0L
+      var batchKey: UnsafeRow = null
+      var keyChanged = false
+      while (!keyChanged && (oneKeyPerBatch || rows.length < maxParameterRowsPerRequest) &&
+          bytes < maxBatchBytes && hasInput) {
+        val row = nextRow()
+        val requestRow = if (oneKeyPerBatch) requestRowOf(row) else null
+        if (requestRow != null && batchKey != null && requestRow != batchKey) {
+          heldRow = row
+          keyChanged = true
+        } else {
+          if (requestRow != null && batchKey == null) batchKey = requestRow.copy()
+          bytes += row.getSizeInBytes
+          rows += row
+        }
+      }
+      rows.toArray
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** The stream rows that share a key, and the one request row sent for them. */
+  private case class KeyEntry(requestRow: UnsafeRow, rowIndexes: mutable.ArrayBuffer[Int])
+
+  /**
+   * Joins one batch of stream rows. Rows whose parameters are equal under Spark equality share
+   * one request row, and every result row for a request row that satisfies the selected lookup
+   * predicates joins all the stream rows sharing it. A stream row is finished, which may emit its
+   * unmatched output row, once no more result rows can match it.
+   *
+   * Output rows are projected into a reused row on `next()`, so the consumer copies the rows it
+   * retains, as with other join iterators.
+   */
+  private class BatchJoinIterator(
+      rows: Array[InternalRow],
+      parameters: LookupParameters,
+      resultRows: LookupResultRows,
+      transforms: LookupTransforms,
+      joinOutput: JoinOutput,
+      reader: LookupReader) extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    metrics.inputRows += rows.length
+    metrics.inputBatches += 1
+
+    private val matched = Array.fill(rows.length)(false)
+    private val finished = mutable.BitSet.empty
+    // Output rows not yet returned: a stream row index and the lookup row it is joined with.
+    private val pending = mutable.Queue.empty[(Int, InternalRow)]
+
+    // One entry for each distinct request row that can match, in the order of first occurrence.
+    // A row that can never match, because it fails the stream condition or has a null parameter,
+    // is finished right away, and its parameters are not requested. The stream condition is
+    // checked before the parameters are evaluated, so that it can guard their expressions.
+    private val keyEntries = {
+      val entries = mutable.LinkedHashMap.empty[UnsafeRow, KeyEntry]
+      rows.indices.foreach { index =>
+        lazy val requestRow = parameters.requestRow(rows(index))
+        if (!joinOutput.canMatch(rows(index)) || parameters.matchesNothing(requestRow)) {
+          finish(index)
+        } else {
+          entries.get(requestRow) match {
+            case Some(entry) => entry.rowIndexes += index
+            case None =>
+              val retained = requestRow.copy()
+              entries.put(retained, KeyEntry(retained, mutable.ArrayBuffer(index)))
+          }
+        }
+      }
+      entries.values.toArray
+    }
+
+    // No connector request, and no reader, when no key can match.
+    private var cursor: ExternalLookupResultCursor =
+      if (keyEntries.isEmpty) EmptyLookupCursor
+      else connectorCall(reader.lookup(keyEntries.map(_.requestRow)))
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      pending.nonEmpty
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      if (pending.isEmpty) throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+      val (index, lookupRow) = pending.dequeue()
+      joinOutput.project(rows(index), lookupRow)
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryFillPending(): Unit = {
+      try {
+        while (pending.isEmpty && advanceCursor()) {
+          reader.resultRowRead()
+          // The join checks for a close() before each connector call, so it makes none after it
+          // has seen one.
+          val start = System.nanoTime()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val ordinal = cursor.inputOrdinal()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val connectorRow = cursor.get()
+          metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+          if (connectorRow == null) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName, "NULL_RESULT", Map("method" -> "ExternalLookupResultCursor.get()"))
+          }
+          val entry = requestedEntry(ordinal)
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val resultRow = resultRows.validatedCopy(connectorRow)

+            transforms(resultRow).foreach { lookupRow =>
+              entry.rowIndexes.foreach(joinMatch(_, lookupRow))
+            }
+          }
+        }
+        if (pending.isEmpty) finishCursor(completed = true)
+      } catch {
+        case error: Throwable =>
+          Utils.tryWithSafeFinally(throw error) {
+            finishCursor(completed = false)
+          }
+      }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Advances the connector's cursor, unless the reader was closed meanwhile. A close() while
+     * next() ran fails the read once next() returns: Spark then reads no row from the closed
+     * cursor, and does not take a missing row for a complete result.
+     */
+    private def advanceCursor(): Boolean = (cursor ne EmptyLookupCursor) && {
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      val advanced = connectorCall(cursor.next())
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      advanced
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Runs a connector call and adds its time to the lookup time metric, which counts only the
+     * time in the connector, not that of the work above the join while a cursor is open.
+     */
+    private def connectorCall[T](call: => T): T = {
+      val start = System.nanoTime()
+      try call finally metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+    }
+
+    private def requestedEntry(ordinal: Int): KeyEntry = {
+      if (ordinal < 0 || ordinal >= keyEntries.length) {
+        throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+          tableName,
+          "INVALID_INPUT_ORDINAL",
+          Map("ordinal" -> ordinal.toString, "numParameterRows" -> keyEntries.length.toString))
+      }
+      keyEntries(ordinal)
+    }
+
+    private def joinMatch(index: Int, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit = {
+      // A semi or anti join knows a stream row's answer at its first match, so it evaluates the
+      // residual condition no further for that row, as the other join operators do. It still
+      // reads the whole result, for the other stream rows of the key.

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), posting on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Fixed in [3bb2bc96d1f](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/3bb2bc96d1fbd8324b1121353de04c3490f478fb): a semi or anti join closes the cursor once every requested row of the batch is decided. Tests cover an equality key that matches several rows, and an open range. From #60087 there's one exception: a batch that fills the cache still reads its keys to the end, because the cache keeps only complete results. The last batch, and range lookups, which cache nothing, still close early.

Thanks, you're right. Fixed in [10381da78d9](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/10381da78d99a4c4f375c6ca1522bc933cf9da41): the scaladoc and the test comment now say that Spark reads a value within the declared length unchanged, drops the trailing blanks past that length from a longer value, and fails if it is still too long. So a store that compares such a longer value as stored could miss a row. The description now says the same, and #60055 uses the same wording for `<=>`.

issue.title: [SPARK-60693][SS][SQL] Add a lookup cache to external lookup join
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR adds a cache to external lookup join, so a repeated key does not cost another remote lookup. The cache is on by default.

This PR implements [SPARK-60693](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60693), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)). It builds on apache/spark#60055 (SPARK-60692, lookup-side projections and filters, semi and anti joins, range predicates).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| #59909 | Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes. |
| #59910 | Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| #60055 | Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns |
| **#60087 (this PR)** | **The lookup cache** |
| #60198 | Predicate pushdown through lookup joins |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

- **Scope and freshness.** There is one cache per input partition, inside a task. It is discarded when the task ends, so a cached result is never older than the task that read it. That is no staler than reading the static side once per micro-batch.
- **Contents.** The cache holds the complete result of each key, including keys with no rows. It stores only rows that pass Spark's own check of the lookup keys, after the lookup-side projections and filters. A result is cached only once it is fully read. A key whose rows take more than a sixteenth of `maxBytes` is still joined in full, but not cached, so the limit never truncates a result.
- **Range lookups are not cached.** When a selected lookup condition is a range whose value reads a stream column, the join caches nothing, even with the cache enabled. A range with a constant bound does not count, because every key carries the same value. Range values, such as event times, rarely repeat, so cached entries would rarely be used.
- **Bounds.** Its memory is bounded by bytes: `maxBytes` per input partition counts each entry's key and rows, with a fixed overhead per entry and per row, so keys with no rows count too. The cache evicts the least recently used keys (Guava), and has an optional time-to-live counted from the write. A partition's last request fills no cache, and the cache is released when the partition's input ends.
- **Metric.** `numCacheHits` counts the distinct keys served from the cache.

| Conf (`spark.sql.join.externalLookup.cache.*`) | Default |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` |
| `maxBytes` | `16m` per input partition |
| `ttl` | `0` (no expiry) |

The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint sets the same options for one join, for example `lookup.hint("external_lookup", "cache_ttl=30s")`. A string parameter that contains `=` is an option; any other string names a relation (#60019). A hint option overrides the session config for that join, and options it does not set follow the session config. An option-only hint above a join fails, because it cannot mark the lookup side. Invalid options fail with `INVALID_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT.*`.

For discussion: **on by default.** The SPIP's examples enable the cache, but the SPIP states no default. Its memory is bounded by `maxBytes`.

### Why are the changes needed?

A stream often repeats lookup keys. Without a cache, each request asks for its keys again, even when an earlier request of the same task has just read them. With the cache, later requests carry fewer parameter rows. A whole request goes away only when all its keys are cached, so the cache helps most when keys repeat across the requests of a partition.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. There are three new SQL configs and three `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint options, and the cache is on by default. Requests carry fewer parameter rows when keys repeat within an input partition, and fewer requests are sent when keys repeat across its requests.

### How was this patch tested?

`ExternalLookupJoinSuite` has new tests. They cover options and their errors, defaults and overrides, freshness, cached misses and expiry. They also cover the byte bound and the per-key cutoff, requests that mix cached and uncached keys, per-partition scope, oversized results, cache hits with lookup-side stages and each join type, and range lookups that skip the cache. Earlier tests that count connector requests opt out of the cache. All pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.

+  ExternalUserDefinedFunction, GreaterThan, GreaterThanOrEqual, LessThan, LessThanOrEqual, Literal,
+  NamedExpression, PythonUDF, SubqueryExpression}

+import org.apache.spark.sql.internal.SQLConf

+  DateType, DecimalType, IntegerType, IntegralType, LongType, ShortType, StringType,
+  TimestampNTZType, TimestampType, VarcharType}
+
+/**
+ * The cache settings of one external lookup join, from the
+ * `spark.sql.join.externalLookup.cache.*` configurations unless the join's `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint
+ * overrides them. A cache lives within a task, per input partition, so these bound each such cache:
+ * its keys and their result rows take at most `maxBytes`, and each is kept for `ttlMillis` (0 keeps
+ * it until evicted). A key whose rows take more than a sixteenth of `maxBytes` is still joined but
+ * not cached, so that one large result cannot evict most of the cache. At present, a join that
+ * selects a range comparison (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`) whose parameter reads a stream column caches
+ * nothing, whatever these settings say.
+ */
+case class ExternalLookupCacheOptions(
+    enabled: Boolean,
+    maxBytes: Long,
+    ttlMillis: Long)
+
+/**
+ * The cache options that one `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint sets. An option that no hint of a join sets
+ * follows its `spark.sql.join.externalLookup.cache.*` configuration when the join is planned, not
+ * the one in effect when the hint was written.
+ */
+case class ExternalLookupHintCacheOptions(
+    enabled: Option[Boolean] = None,
+    maxBytes: Option[Long] = None,
+    ttlMillis: Option[Long] = None) {
+  /** These options, with the ones that they do not set taken from `other`. */
+  def orElse(other: ExternalLookupHintCacheOptions): ExternalLookupHintCacheOptions =
+    ExternalLookupHintCacheOptions(
+      enabled.orElse(other.enabled),
+      maxBytes.orElse(other.maxBytes),
+      ttlMillis.orElse(other.ttlMillis))
+
+  /** These options, with the configurations of `conf` for the ones that they do not set. */
+  def withDefaults(conf: SQLConf): ExternalLookupCacheOptions = ExternalLookupCacheOptions(
+    enabled = enabled.getOrElse(conf.getConf(SQLConf.JOIN_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_CACHE_ENABLED)),
+    maxBytes = maxBytes.getOrElse(conf.getConf(SQLConf.JOIN_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_CACHE_MAX_BYTES)),
+    ttlMillis = ttlMillis.getOrElse(conf.getConf(SQLConf.JOIN_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_CACHE_TTL)))
+}
+
+/**
+ * Marks the plan below it as the lookup side that the `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint asks an external
+ * lookup join to read, with the cache options that the hint sets. The external lookup join rules
+ * consume it when they form the join.
+ *
+ * Join strategy hints are [[ResolvedHint]] nodes with a [[JoinStrategyHint]]. This hint is not,
+ * because that representation cannot keep two of its guarantees:
+ *  - A strategy hint that conflicts with it must fail the query. [[HintInfo]] holds one strategy,
+ *    and `ResolveJoinStrategyHints` merges a strategy hint on an already hinted relation into the
+ *    existing [[ResolvedHint]] with `HintInfo.merge`, which keeps one strategy and only warns.
+ *  - It selects how the lookup side is read, not a physical join. `EliminateResolvedHint` moves
+ *    every [[ResolvedHint]] it can attach into `Join.hint`, for physical join selection.
+ */
+case class ExternalLookupHint(
+    child: LogicalPlan,
+    cacheOptions: ExternalLookupHintCacheOptions) extends UnaryNode {
+  override def output: Seq[Attribute] = child.output
+
+  final override val nodePatterns: Seq[TreePattern] = Seq(EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT)
+
+  override protected def withNewChildInternal(newChild: LogicalPlan): ExternalLookupHint =
+    copy(child = newChild)
+}

+ * A lookup join retained through ordinary expression and operator optimization.
+ *
+ * @param requiredLookupOutput Lookup-side attributes still required above this join. They are
+ *   part of this node's references, so column pruning keeps them on the lookup side.
+ *   `ColumnPruning` narrows them to what the parent reads, and `PrepareExternalLookupJoin` prunes
+ *   the lookup scan to them.
+ */
+case class ExternalLookupJoin(
+    left: LogicalPlan,
+    right: LogicalPlan,
+    joinType: JoinType,
+    condition: Option[Expression],
+    cacheOptions: ExternalLookupCacheOptions,

+import org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.plans.{Inner, JoinType, LeftOuter}
+import org.apache.spark.sql.catalyst.util.ArrayData

+/**
+ * Creates the partition evaluators of an [[ExternalLookupJoinExec]]. The factory is sent to the
+ * tasks, so it holds only what they need; the plan node and its scan stay on the driver.
+ *
+ * An evaluator joins its partition one batch of up to `maxParameterRowsPerRequest` stream rows at
+ * a time. For each batch it sends one request with the distinct parameters that can match, and
+ * streams the connector's result rows into output rows. Parameters are deduplicated per request,
+ * that is within one batch: a key repeated in a later batch is requested again.
+ *
+ * Spark does not trust the connector with the selected lookup predicates: it evaluates
+ * `lookupKeyCheck` on every row that the connector returns, against the request row that the row
+ * answers, and drops a row that fails it, before it joins the row. The stream rows that share a
+ * request row have Spark-equal parameters, so one check serves all of them.
+ *
+ * The join condition comes in two parts: `streamCondition` reads only stream columns and is
+ * evaluated on each stream row before the request, and `residualCondition` is evaluated on the
+ * joined rows. A stream row that fails `streamCondition` cannot match, so its parameters are not
+ * sent.
+ */
+class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory(
+    tableName: String,
+    lookupParameters: Seq[Expression],
+    nullSafeParameters: Seq[Boolean],
+    lookupKeyCheck: Option[Expression],
+    streamOutput: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupInput: Seq[Attribute],
+    output: Seq[Attribute],
+    joinType: JoinType,
+    streamCondition: Option[Expression],
+    residualCondition: Option[Expression],
+    readerFactory: ExternalLookupReaderFactory,
+    maxParameterRowsPerRequest: Int,
+    maxBatchBytes: Long,
+    metrics: ExternalLookupJoinMetrics,
+    readerMetrics: ExternalLookupReaderMetrics)

+
+  require(lookupParameters.length == nullSafeParameters.length,
+    "Every external lookup parameter must define its null semantics")
+
+  override def createEvaluator(): PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] =
+    new ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator
+
+  private class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator extends PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] {
+    override def eval(
+        partitionIndex: Int,
+        inputs: Iterator[InternalRow]*): Iterator[InternalRow] = {
+      assert(inputs.length == 1)
+      new PartitionJoinIterator(inputs.head, partitionIndex)
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Joins one partition batch by batch, and closes its reader after the last batch. */
+  private class PartitionJoinIterator(input: Iterator[InternalRow], partitionIndex: Int)
+    extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    private val reader = new LookupReader
+    private val parameters = new LookupParameters(partitionIndex)
+    private val resultRows = new LookupResultRows
+    private val joinOutput = new JoinOutput(partitionIndex)
+    private var batch: Iterator[InternalRow] = Iterator.empty
+    private var inputExhausted = false
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      batch.hasNext
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      if (!batch.hasNext) {
+        throw new SparkIllegalStateException(
+          errorClass = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+          messageParameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup join exhausted"))
+      }
+      batch.next()
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryAdvance(): Unit = {
+      while (!batch.hasNext && !inputExhausted) {
+        val rows = readBatch()
+        if (rows.nonEmpty) {
+          batch = new BatchJoinIterator(rows, parameters, resultRows, joinOutput, reader)
+        }
+        inputExhausted = !input.hasNext
+      }
+      if (inputExhausted && !batch.hasNext) reader.close()
+    }
+
+    private lazy val toUnsafe = UnsafeProjection.create(streamOutput, streamOutput)
+
+    // An array, because a batch's rows are read by position for every key, match and output row.
+    // The batch holds its rows until its request is read, so it stops once their copies reach
+    // maxBatchBytes, keeping the row that reaches it, as well as at maxParameterRowsPerRequest
+    // rows. It always takes one row.
+    private def readBatch(): Array[InternalRow] = {
+      val rows = mutable.ArrayBuffer.empty[InternalRow]
+      var bytes = 0L
+      while (rows.length < maxParameterRowsPerRequest && bytes < maxBatchBytes && input.hasNext) {
+        val row = input.next() match {
+          case unsafe: UnsafeRow => unsafe.copy()
+          case other => toUnsafe(other).copy()
+        }
+        bytes += row.getSizeInBytes
+        rows += row
+      }
+      rows.toArray
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** The stream rows that share a key, and the one request row sent for them. */
+  private case class KeyEntry(requestRow: UnsafeRow, rowIndexes: mutable.ArrayBuffer[Int])
+
+  /**
+   * Joins one batch of stream rows. Rows whose parameters are equal under Spark equality share
+   * one request row, and every result row for a request row that satisfies the selected lookup
+   * predicates joins all the stream rows sharing it. A stream row is finished, which may emit its
+   * unmatched output row, once no more result rows can match it.
+   *
+   * Output rows are projected into a reused row on `next()`, so the consumer copies the rows it
+   * retains, as with other join iterators.
+   */
+  private class BatchJoinIterator(
+      rows: Array[InternalRow],
+      parameters: LookupParameters,
+      resultRows: LookupResultRows,
+      joinOutput: JoinOutput,
+      reader: LookupReader) extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    metrics.inputRows += rows.length
+    metrics.inputBatches += 1
+
+    private val matched = Array.fill(rows.length)(false)
+    private val finished = mutable.BitSet.empty
+    // Output rows not yet returned: a stream row index and the lookup row it is joined with.
+    private val pending = mutable.Queue.empty[(Int, InternalRow)]
+
+    // One entry for each distinct request row that can match, in the order of first occurrence.
+    // A row that can never match, because it fails the stream condition or has a null parameter,
+    // is finished right away, and its parameters are not requested. The stream condition is
+    // checked before the parameters are evaluated, so that it can guard their expressions.
+    private val keyEntries = {
+      val entries = mutable.LinkedHashMap.empty[UnsafeRow, KeyEntry]
+      rows.indices.foreach { index =>
+        lazy val requestRow = parameters.requestRow(rows(index))
+        if (!joinOutput.canMatch(rows(index)) || parameters.matchesNothing(requestRow)) {
+          finish(index)
+        } else {
+          entries.get(requestRow) match {
+            case Some(entry) => entry.rowIndexes += index
+            case None =>
+              val retained = requestRow.copy()
+              entries.put(retained, KeyEntry(retained, mutable.ArrayBuffer(index)))
+          }
+        }
+      }
+      entries.values.toArray
+    }
+
+    // No connector request, and no reader, when no key can match.
+    private var cursor: ExternalLookupResultCursor =
+      if (keyEntries.isEmpty) EmptyLookupCursor
+      else connectorCall(reader.lookup(keyEntries.map(_.requestRow)))
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      pending.nonEmpty
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      if (pending.isEmpty) throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+      val (index, lookupRow) = pending.dequeue()
+      joinOutput.project(rows(index), lookupRow)
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryFillPending(): Unit = {
+      try {
+        while (pending.isEmpty && advanceCursor()) {
+          reader.resultRowRead()
+          // The join checks for a close() before each connector call, so it makes none after it
+          // has seen one.
+          val start = System.nanoTime()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val ordinal = cursor.inputOrdinal()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val connectorRow = cursor.get()
+          metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+          if (connectorRow == null) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName, "NULL_RESULT", Map("method" -> "ExternalLookupResultCursor.get()"))
+          }
+          val entry = requestedEntry(ordinal)
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val resultRow = resultRows.validatedCopy(connectorRow)
+          if (parameters.selectedPredicatesHold(entry.requestRow, resultRow)) {
+            entry.rowIndexes.foreach(joinMatch(_, resultRow))
+          }
+        }
+        if (pending.isEmpty) finishCursor(completed = true)
+      } catch {
+        case error: Throwable =>
+          Utils.tryWithSafeFinally(throw error) {
+            finishCursor(completed = false)
+          }
+      }
+    }

+     * Advances the connector's cursor, unless the reader was closed meanwhile. A close() while
+     * next() ran fails the read once next() returns: Spark then reads no row from the closed
+     * cursor, and does not take a missing row for a complete result.
+     */
+    private def advanceCursor(): Boolean = (cursor ne EmptyLookupCursor) && {
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      val advanced = connectorCall(cursor.next())
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      advanced
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Runs a connector call and adds its time to the lookup time metric, which counts only the
+     * time in the connector, not that of the work above the join while a cursor is open.
+     */
+    private def connectorCall[T](call: => T): T = {
+      val start = System.nanoTime()
+      try call finally metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+    }
+
+    private def requestedEntry(ordinal: Int): KeyEntry = {
+      if (ordinal < 0 || ordinal >= keyEntries.length) {
+        throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+          tableName,
+          "INVALID_INPUT_ORDINAL",
+          Map("ordinal" -> ordinal.toString, "numParameterRows" -> keyEntries.length.toString))
+      }
+      keyEntries(ordinal)
+    }
