+    var offeredCandidates = Seq.empty[String]
+    val lookup = lookupRelation(PlanningExternalLookupTable(s"id INT, code $codeType", select = {

+        offeredCandidates = candidates.map(_.toString).toSeq
+        candidates.take(1)
+    }))
+    val Seq(lookupId, lookupCode) = lookup.output
+    val streamId = stream.output.head
+    val streamCode = AttributeReference("streamCode", lookupCode.dataType)()
+    val codesEqual = streamCode === lookupCode
+    val prepared = prepare(lookupJoin(lookup, streamId === lookupId && codesEqual,
+      left = LocalRelation(Seq(streamId, streamCode), isStreaming = true)))
+    assert(prepared.residualCondition === Some(codesEqual), codeType)
+    offeredCandidates match {
+      case Seq("id = ?") => false
+      case Seq("id = ?", "code = ?") => true
+      case other => fail(s"Unexpected candidates for $codeType: $other")
+    }
+  }

+      val joinedOutput = stream.output ++ lookup.output
+      val residual = prepared.residualCondition.get
+      val conjunction = keyEqual && mayFail
+      def row(label: String, lookupLabelValue: String): InternalRow = InternalRow(
+        1, UTF8String.fromString(label), 1, UTF8String.fromString(lookupLabelValue))
+      def matches(condition: Expression, input: InternalRow): Boolean = {
+        val interpreted = BindReferences.bindReference(condition, joinedOutput).eval(input)

+      val error = intercept[Exception](matches(conjunction, row("x", null)))
+      // The catalyst DSL turns a String operand of `===` into an expression.
+      assert(error.asInstanceOf[SparkThrowable].getCondition == "CAST_INVALID_INPUT")
+      // Otherwise the residual matches the rows that the conjunction matches.
+      Seq(row("2", "2"), row("-2", "-2"), row("2", "3")).foreach { input =>
+        assert(matches(residual, input) === matches(conjunction, input))
+      }
+    }

+      candidates(0) = candidates(1)
+      candidates(1) = first
+      Array(candidates(0))
+    }))
+    val Seq(id, value) = lookup.output
+    val prepared = prepare(lookupJoin(lookup, streamId === id && streamLabel === value))
+    assert(prepared.lookupParameters === Seq(streamLabel))
+    assert(prepared.residualCondition === Some(streamId === id))
+  }
+
+  test("a connector method that returns null fails with a named error") {
+    Seq(
+      "build" -> "ScanBuilder.build()",
+      "readSchema" -> "Scan.readSchema()",
+      "toExternalLookup" -> "Scan.toExternalLookup()",
+      "createReaderFactory" -> "ExternalLookup.createReaderFactory()").foreach {
+      case (nullFrom, method) =>
+        val lookup = lookupRelation(PlanningExternalLookupTable(nullFrom = nullFrom))
+        checkError(
+          exception = prepareError(lookupJoinOnId(lookup)),
+          condition = "DATA_SOURCE_INVALID_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP.NULL_RESULT",
+          parameters = Map("table" -> QUOTED_TABLE_NAME, "method" -> method))
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("a prepared lookup join keeps the size estimate of the join it replaces") {
+    // Two stream rows, and a lookup side of Spark's default size.
+    withSQLConf(SQLConf.DEFAULT_SIZE_IN_BYTES.key -> "1000") {
+      val rows = Seq(1, 2).map(id => InternalRow(id, UTF8String.fromString("a")))
+      val sizedStream = LocalRelation(stream.output, rows, isStreaming = true)
+      assert(sizedStream.stats.sizeInBytes > 0)
+      // Inner and left outer joins get the product of both sides' sizes. Semi and anti joins, as
+      // ordinary ones, get the stream side's size.
+      Seq(Inner -> 1000, LeftOuter -> 1000, LeftSemi -> 1, LeftAnti -> 1).foreach {
+        case (joinType, lookupFactor) =>
+          val lookup = lookupRelation(PlanningExternalLookupTable())
+          val join = lookupJoin(lookup, sizedStream.output.head === lookup.output.head, joinType,
+            left = sizedStream)
+          val prepared = prepare(join)
+          assert(prepared.stats.sizeInBytes === sizedStream.stats.sizeInBytes * lookupFactor,
+            joinType)
+          assert(prepared.stats.sizeInBytes === join.stats.sizeInBytes, joinType)
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("an external UDF over lookup columns in the join condition") {
+    val lookup = lookupRelation(PlanningExternalLookupTable())
+    val lookupId = lookup.output.head
+    val lookupUDF = ExternalUserDefinedFunction(
+      name = Some("lookup_udf"),
+      workerSpec = UDFWorkerSpecification.getDefaultInstance,
+      payload = Array.emptyByteArray,
+      dataType = BooleanType,
+      children = Seq(lookupId),
+      udfDeterministic = true,
+      udfNullable = false)
+    val condition = stream.output.head === lookupId && lookupUDF
+
+    // An inner join evaluates it above the lookup join, where PlanExternalUDFs extracts it.
+    val prepared = PrepareExternalLookupJoin(lookupJoin(lookup, condition))
+    prepared match {
+      case Filter(filterCondition, join: PreparedExternalLookupJoin) =>
+        assert(filterCondition == lookupUDF)
+        assert(join.residualCondition.isEmpty)
+      case other => fail(s"Expected a filter above a prepared external lookup join: $other")
+    }
+    val conf = SQLConf.get
+    val unifiedUDFExecution = conf.getConf(StaticSQLConf.UNIFIED_UDF_EXECUTION_ENABLED)
+    conf.setConf(StaticSQLConf.UNIFIED_UDF_EXECUTION_ENABLED, true)
+    try {
+      val planned = PlanExternalUDFs(prepared)
+      assert(planned.exists(_.isInstanceOf[ExecuteExternalUDF]))
+      assert(planned.exists {
+        case _: ExecuteExternalUDF => false
+        case node => node.expressions.exists(_.exists(_.isInstanceOf[ExternalUserDefinedFunction]))
+      } === false)
+    } finally {
+      conf.setConf(StaticSQLConf.UNIFIED_UDF_EXECUTION_ENABLED, unifiedUDFExecution)
+    }
+    // A left outer join cannot.
+    checkError(
+      exception = prepareError(lookupJoin(lookup, condition, LeftOuter)),
+      condition = "UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.EXTERNAL_UDF_IN_ON_CLAUSE",
+      parameters = Map("joinType" -> "LEFT OUTER"))
+  }
+
+  test("column pruning never projects the lookup relation under a lookup join") {

+    SemanticKeyExternalLookupDataSource.requestSizes.clear()

+
+  /** The rows of `df` as a streaming DataFrame: one micro-batch, in `numPartitions` partitions. */
+  private def streamOf(df: DataFrame, numPartitions: Int = 1): DataFrame = {
+    val input = MemoryStream[Row](numPartitions)(Encoders.row(df.schema), spark.sqlContext)

+  private case class StreamRun(rows: Seq[Row], execution: IncrementalExecution) {

+    def lookupJoin: ExternalLookupJoinExec = execution.executedPlan.collectFirst {
+      case exec: ExternalLookupJoinExec => exec
+    }.get
+  }
+
+  /** Runs the streaming `df` on a memory sink until it has processed all of its input. */
+  private def runStream(df: DataFrame, outputMode: String = "append"): StreamRun = {
+    val queryName = s"external_lookup_stream_${streamRunCount.incrementAndGet()}"
+    val query =
+      df.writeStream.format("memory").outputMode(outputMode).queryName(queryName).start()
+    try {
+      query.processAllAvailable()
+      StreamRun(

+        query.asInstanceOf[StreamingQueryWrapper].streamingQuery.lastExecution)
+    } finally {
+      query.stop()
+      spark.catalog.dropTempView(queryName)
+    }
+  }
+

+    QueryTest.sameRows(expected, runStream(df).rows).foreach(fail(_))

+  private def streamFailure[T <: Throwable : ClassTag](df: DataFrame): T = {
+    val cause = try {
+      runStream(df)
+      fail("The streaming query did not fail")
+    } catch {
+      case e: StreamingQueryException => e.getCause
+      case e: Throwable with SparkThrowable => e
+    }
+    assert(classTag[T].runtimeClass.isInstance(cause), cause)
+    cause.asInstanceOf[T]
+  }

+  test("a hinted dual-capability source fails when no lookup access path exists") {

+      parameters = Map("table" -> "`DualCapabilityExternalLookupTable`"))
+  }
+
+  test("a physical strategy hint on a lookup-only join is rejected") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1, 3).toDF("id"))
+    val withLookupHint = lookup.hint("external_lookup").hint("shuffle_hash")
+    Seq(
+      "BROADCAST" ->
+        (() => left.join(lookup.hint("broadcast"), left("id") === lookup("id"), "left_outer")),
+      "BROADCAST" ->
+        (() => left.join(broadcast(lookup), left("id") === lookup("id"), "left_outer")),
+      "MERGE" -> (() => left.hint("merge").join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"))),
+      "SHUFFLE_HASH" ->
+        (() => left.join(withLookupHint, left("id") === withLookupHint("id")))).foreach {
+      case (strategy, query) =>
+        checkError(
+          exception = intercept[AnalysisException] { query().queryExecution.analyzed },
+          condition = "EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.CONFLICTING_JOIN_STRATEGY",
+          parameters = Map("strategy" -> strategy, "relation" -> "`SimpleExternalLookupTable`"))
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("an ordinary join over an enriched lookup join result stays ordinary") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val events = streamOf(Seq(1, 2).toDF("id"))
+    val enriched = events.join(lookup, events("id") === lookup("id"))
+      .select(events("id").as("event_id"), lookup("department"))
+    val base = Seq((1, "a"), (2, "b")).toDF("id", "tag")
+    val expected = Seq(
+      Row(1, "a", 1, "engineering"), Row(1, "a", 1, "research"), Row(2, "b", 2, "sales"))
+    def lookupJoinCount(df: DataFrame): Int =
+      runStream(df).plan.collect { case j: PreparedExternalLookupJoin => j }.size
+
+    val joined = base.join(enriched, base("id") === enriched("event_id"))
+    assert(lookupJoinCount(joined) === 1)
+    checkStream(joined, expected)
+
+    withTempView("external_lookup_base", "external_lookup_events", "external_lookup_right") {
+      base.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_base")
+      events.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_events")
+      lookup.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_right")
+      val sqlJoined = sql(
+        """
+          |SELECT b.id, b.tag, e.event_id, e.department
+          |FROM external_lookup_base b JOIN (
+          |  SELECT v.id AS event_id, r.department
+          |  FROM external_lookup_events v JOIN external_lookup_right r ON v.id = r.id) e
+          |ON b.id = e.event_id
+          |""".stripMargin)
+      assert(lookupJoinCount(sqlJoined) === 1)
+      checkStream(sqlJoined, expected)
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("an external lookup hint outside any join is ignored") {
+    val dual = spark.read.format(classOf[DualCapabilityExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val expected = Seq(Row(1, "engineering"), Row(1, "research"), Row(2, "sales"))
+
+    checkAnswer(dual.hint("external_lookup"), expected)
+    assert(dual.hint("external_lookup").count() === 3)
+    withTempView("external_lookup_right") {
+      dual.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_right")
+      checkAnswer(sql("SELECT /*+ EXTERNAL_LOOKUP */ * FROM external_lookup_right"), expected)
+      checkAnswer(sql("SELECT /*+ EXTERNAL_LOOKUP(r) */ * FROM external_lookup_right r"), expected)
+      checkAnswer(
+        sql("SELECT /*+ EXTERNAL_LOOKUP(r) */ id, count(*) FROM external_lookup_right r " +
+          "GROUP BY id"),
+        Seq(Row(1, 2), Row(2, 1)))
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("a lookup side with another operator above the table fails when the DataFrame is built") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val dual = spark.read.format(classOf[DualCapabilityExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1, 3).toDF("id"))
+    withTempView("operator_side_lookup", "operator_side_left") {
+      lookup.createOrReplaceTempView("operator_side_lookup")
+      left.createOrReplaceTempView("operator_side_left")
+      // A lookup-only table, which no other join can read, and a hinted table that supports batch
+      // reads too. The join fails even where the optimizer would remove the operator.
+      Seq(
+        lookup.where(lit(false)),
+        lookup.select($"id", $"department"),
+        dual.select($"id", $"department").hint("external_lookup"),
+        dual.hint("external_lookup").where($"id" > 0)).foreach { right =>
+        checkError(
+          exception = intercept[AnalysisException] {
+            left.join(right, left("id") === right("id"), "left_outer")
+          },
+          condition = "EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.LOOKUP_PLAN",
+          parameters = Map.empty)
+      }
+      checkError(
+        exception = intercept[AnalysisException] {
+          sql("SELECT * FROM operator_side_left l JOIN " +
+            "(SELECT * FROM operator_side_lookup WHERE 1 = 0) r ON l.id = r.id")
+        },
+        condition = "EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.LOOKUP_PLAN",
+        parameters = Map.empty)
+    }
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.readerCount.get() === 0)
+  }
+
+  test("a USING join with the EXTERNAL_LOOKUP hint runs as an external lookup join") {
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1, 3).toDF("id"))
+    Seq[Class[_]](
+      classOf[DualCapabilityExternalLookupDataSource],
+      classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource]).foreach { source =>

+  test("external lookup finishes no stream row after a failed or closed read") {
+    // After a failure or a close the result may be partial, so a stream row without a match could
+    // be one whose match was never read: Spark emits no unmatched row then. Id 1 has two matches
+    // and id 3 has none, and both are in one request.
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    val outerJoin =
+      runStream(left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"), "left_outer")).lookupJoin
+    val input = CoalesceExec(1,
+      LocalTableScanExec(outerJoin.child.output, Seq(InternalRow(1), InternalRow(3)), None))
+    Seq(
+      "cursorFailure" -> 0,
+      "closeDuringNext" -> 0,
+      "closeDuringGet" -> 0,
+      "closeBetweenResultRows" -> 1,
+      "closeAtCursorEnd" -> 2).foreach {
+      case (failure, outputRows) =>
+        SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+        val readerFactory = outerJoin.readerFactory match {
+          case factory: SimpleExternalLookupReaderFactory if failure == "cursorFailure" =>
+            factory.copy(failAt = "cursor")
+          case factory => factory
+        }
+        val failingJoin = outerJoin.copy(readerFactory = readerFactory, child = input)
+        val rdd = failingJoin.execute()
+        val context = TaskContext.empty()
+        TaskContext.setTaskContext(context)
+        try {
+          val rows = rdd.iterator(rdd.partitions.head, context)
+          val completeTask = () => context.markTaskCompleted(None)
+          failure match {
+            case "closeBetweenResultRows" =>
+              rows.next()
+              completeTask()
+            case "closeAtCursorEnd" =>
+              SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeCursorEnds.set(completeTask)
+            // The cursor had a row when the close came, but Spark reads no row from it.
+            case "closeDuringNext" =>
+              SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeNextReturns.set(completeTask)
+            // The close comes while the row is read, so Spark neither copies nor joins it.
+            case "closeDuringGet" =>
+              SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeGetReturns.set(completeTask)
+            case _ =>
+          }
+          intercept[Exception] {
+            while (rows.hasNext) rows.next()
+          }
+          assert(failingJoin.metrics("numOutputRows").value === outputRows, failure)
+          assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.rowReadsAfterClose.get() === 0, failure)
+        } finally {
+          TaskContext.unset()
+        }
+    }
+  }

+  test("external lookup makes no connector call once its task completed") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    val lookupJoin = runStream(left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"))).lookupJoin
+    // Computes the join over a local input, in a task that completes before the join is
+    // consumed, before its first request, while its reader is created, while the request is in
+    // progress, or between the two result rows of the request. Another thread consumes the join,
+    // as when a thread other than the task's drives it.
+    val rdd = lookupJoin
+      .copy(child = LocalTableScanExec(lookupJoin.child.output, Seq(InternalRow(1)), None))
+      .execute()
+    val completions = Seq(
+      "beforeEval", "beforeRequest", "duringReaderCreation", "duringRequest", "betweenResultRows")
+    completions.foreach { completion =>
+      SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+      val context = TaskContext.empty()
+      TaskContext.setTaskContext(context)
+      try {
+        if (completion == "beforeEval") context.markTaskCompleted(None)
+        val rows = rdd.iterator(rdd.partitions.head, context)
+        if (completion == "betweenResultRows") rows.next()
+        val completeTask = () => context.markTaskCompleted(None)
+        completion match {
+          case "duringReaderCreation" =>
+            SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeReaderReturns.set(completeTask)
+          case "duringRequest" =>
+            SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeLookupReturns.set(completeTask)
+          case _ => completeTask()
+        }
+        val resultRowsRead = SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resultRowsRead.get()
+
+        val failure = new AtomicReference[Throwable]()
+        val consumer = new Thread(() => {
+          try rows.hasNext catch { case error: Throwable => failure.set(error) }
+        })
+        consumer.start()
+        consumer.join()
+        // No new reader, request or cursor advance after the close, and every reader and cursor
+        // is closed.
+        val (readers, requests) = completion match {
+          case "beforeEval" | "beforeRequest" => (0, 0)
+          case "duringReaderCreation" => (1, 0)
+          case _ => (1, 1)
+        }
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.readerCount.get() === readers)
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.requestCount.get() === requests)
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resultRowsRead.get() === resultRowsRead)
+        // The close closes the cursor before the reader. A cursor that a request in progress
+        // returns after the close is closed after the reader.
+        val closeEvents = completion match {
+          case "beforeEval" | "beforeRequest" => Seq.empty
+          case "duringReaderCreation" => Seq("reader")
+          case "duringRequest" => Seq("reader", "cursor")
+          case _ => Seq("cursor", "reader")
+        }
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === closeEvents)
+        checkError(
+          exception = failure.get().asInstanceOf[SparkException],
+          condition = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+          parameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup reader used after it was closed"))
+      } finally {
+        TaskContext.unset()
+      }
+    }
+  }

+  /**
+   * Runs the join of `lookupJoin` over stream row 1 in a task, on a consuming thread, and ends the
+   * task on another thread once the consumer has reached `hook`, which then blocks it until
+   * `whileBlocked` has run. Returns the consumer's failure.
+   */
+  private def endTaskWhileConsumerIsIn(
+      lookupJoin: ExternalLookupJoinExec,
+      hook: AtomicReference[() => Unit])(whileBlocked: Thread => Unit): Throwable = {
+    val rdd = lookupJoin
+      .copy(child = LocalTableScanExec(lookupJoin.child.output, Seq(InternalRow(1)), None))
+      .execute()
+    SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+    val reached = new CountDownLatch(1)
+    val release = new CountDownLatch(1)
+    val first = new AtomicBoolean(true)
+    hook.set { () =>
+      if (first.getAndSet(false)) {
+        reached.countDown()
+        assert(release.await(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
+      }
+    }
+    val context = TaskContext.empty()
+    TaskContext.setTaskContext(context)
+    try {
+      val rows = rdd.iterator(rdd.partitions.head, context)
+      val failure = new AtomicReference[Throwable]()
+      val consumer = new Thread(() => {
+        try {
+          while (rows.hasNext) rows.next()
+        } catch {
+          case error: Throwable => failure.set(error)
+        }
+      })
+      consumer.start()
+      val completion = new Thread(() => context.markTaskCompleted(None))
+      try {
+        assert(reached.await(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
+        completion.start()
+        whileBlocked(completion)
+      } finally {
+        release.countDown()
+        consumer.join(TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(10))
+        completion.join(TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(10))
+      }
+      // Both threads have ended, so every close the task makes has happened.
+      assert(consumer.isAlive === false)
+      assert(completion.isAlive === false)
+      failure.get()
+    } finally {
+      TaskContext.unset()
+    }
+  }

+    }

+    case unary: UnaryNode => lookupHints(unary.child, found)
+    case _ => found
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * The physical join strategy hint, such as `BROADCAST` or `MERGE`, that EliminateResolvedHint
+   * would attach to the join, or None if there is none. The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint is never
+   * returned: it is an [[ExternalLookupHint]] marker, not a [[JoinStrategyHint]]. A `HintInfo`
+   * without a strategy asks for nothing, so it is skipped.
+   */
+  private def joinStrategyHint(join: Join): Option[JoinStrategyHint] = {
+    // Only the hints that EliminateResolvedHint will attach to this join count; a strategy hint
+    // on a nested join belongs to that join.
+    val attached = join.hint.leftHint.toSeq ++ join.hint.rightHint.toSeq ++
+      Seq(join.left, join.right).flatMap(EliminateResolvedHint.extractHintsFromPlan(_)._2)
+    attached.flatMap(_.strategy).headOption
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Reports, while a query is analyzed, why a join cannot run as the external lookup join it must
+ * be. It does not change the plan: the join stays a [[Join]] until [[FormExternalLookupJoin]]
+ * converts it, so the APIs and rules that expect an analyzed join keep working. A join that is not
+ * resolved, for example one whose condition is not boolean, is left to the analyzer's own join
+ * checks.
+ *
+ * A missing join condition is reported only for the query of a streaming write, which is analyzed
+ * in full when the query starts, so that `start()` throws it. Other plans can still get their
+ * condition: the classic Dataset API analyzes a USING join first as a join without a condition.
+ */
+object CheckExternalLookupJoin extends (LogicalPlan => Unit) {
+  override def apply(plan: LogicalPlan): Unit = {
+    // A join must run as a lookup join only over a lookup-only table, which is a DSv2 relation, or
+    // under the hint, so other plans need no walk.
+    if (plan.containsPattern(JOIN) &&
+        plan.containsAnyPattern(DATA_SOURCE_V2_RELATION, EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT)) {
+      val complete = plan.isInstanceOf[WriteToStream]
+      plan.foreachUp {
+        case join: Join if join.resolved =>
+          ExternalLookupJoinEligibility(join) match {
+            case ExternalLookupJoinEligibility.Ineligible(error) => throw error
+            case ExternalLookupJoinEligibility.MissingCondition if complete =>
+              throw QueryCompilationErrors.unsupportedExternalLookupJoinError(
+                "MISSING_JOIN_CONDITION")
+            case _ =>
+          }
+        case _ =>
+      }
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+/**
+ * Replaces each join that runs as an external lookup join with an [[ExternalLookupJoin]], and
+ * removes the `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hints that no join consumed.
+ *
+ * It must run at the start of optimization, before Finish Analysis and operator optimization, so
+ * that it sees the join and its lookup side as analysis left them: no hint or alias eliminated,
+ * no predicate pushed into the join and no column pruned. These are the shapes that
+ * [[CheckExternalLookupJoin]] validated. It also runs before CTEs are inlined, so it classifies a
+ * join with the CTEs of its inputs inlined, as the analysis check does, and inlines the CTEs of
+ * the lookup side into the lookup join.
+ */
+object FormExternalLookupJoin extends Rule[LogicalPlan] {
+  import ExternalLookupJoinEligibility._
+
+  // As in CheckExternalLookupJoin, a join runs as a lookup join only over a lookup-only table,
+  // which is a DSv2 relation, or under the hint, so other plans have no join to convert.
+  override def apply(plan: LogicalPlan): LogicalPlan =
+    if (!plan.containsAnyPattern(DATA_SOURCE_V2_RELATION, EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT)) plan
+    else formLookupJoins(plan)
+
+  private def formLookupJoins(plan: LogicalPlan): LogicalPlan = {
+    val cteDefs = cteDefinitions(plan)
+    val formed = plan.transformUpWithPruning(_.containsPattern(JOIN)) {
+      case join: Join =>
+        val inlined = inlineCTEs(join, cteDefs)
+        ExternalLookupJoinEligibility(inlined) match {
+          case Eligible =>
+            val lookupPlan = lookupSide(inlined)
+            ExternalLookupJoin(
+              join.left,
+              lookupPlan,
+              join.joinType,
+              join.condition,
+              lookupPlan.output)
+          // Operator optimization could push a filter's predicate into the join later, but the
+          // condition must be written in the join.
+          case MissingCondition =>
+            throw QueryCompilationErrors.unsupportedExternalLookupJoinError(
+              "MISSING_JOIN_CONDITION")
+          case Ineligible(error) => throw error
+          case NotLookupJoin => join
+        }
+    }
+    // A join with the hint on its lookup side has been converted or has failed, so a hint that is
+    // left is not on the lookup side of any join.
+    formed.transformUpWithPruning(_.containsPattern(EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT)) {
+      case hint: ExternalLookupHint =>
+        logWarning("An EXTERNAL_LOOKUP hint is not on the lookup side of a join and is ignored.")

issue.title: [SPARK-60694][SS][SQL] Push predicates through external lookup joins
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR pushes predicates through external lookup joins. A filter on stream columns then runs before the lookup, so fewer rows are looked up, and a condition on lookup columns can reach the connector as a filter. Query results are the same as for an ordinary join.

This PR implements [SPARK-60694](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60694), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)). It builds on apache/spark#60087 (SPARK-60693, the lookup cache).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| #59909 | Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes. |
| #59910 | Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| #60055 | Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns |
| #60087 | The lookup cache |
| **#60198 (this PR)** | **Predicate pushdown through lookup joins** |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

Worth a reviewer's attention, because existing optimizer rules change and no new rule is added:
- **`PushPredicateThroughJoin`** handles `ExternalLookupJoin` as it handles `AsOfJoin`, reusing its `split`. `PushDownPredicates` also visits plans with a lookup join.
- **`EliminateOuterJoin`** turns a left outer lookup join into an inner one when a filter above it rejects null lookup columns. It also removes a left outer lookup join under an aggregate that reads only stream columns and ignores duplicates, so no lookup runs. Its code is shared between joins and lookup joins.

What moves, for deterministic conjuncts, as for an ordinary join (a conjunct marked as throwing, such as `raise_error`, does not move):

| Where the conjunct is | Inner | Left outer | Left semi | Left anti |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter above, stream side only | stream side | stream side | stream side | stream side |
| Filter above, lookup side only | lookup side | stays above (1) | (not possible) | (not possible) |
| Filter above, both sides | join condition | stays above (1) | (not possible) | (not possible) |
| Join condition, lookup side only | lookup side | lookup side | lookup side | lookup side |
| Join condition, stream side only | stream side | stays | stream side | stays |

(1) Unless the filter rejects null lookup columns. Then `EliminateOuterJoin` makes the join inner, and the filter moves.

Cases specific to lookup joins:
- A comparison between a lookup column and a constant, such as `t.tier >= 2`, moves onto the lookup side as a filter, exactly as for an ordinary join. `PrepareExternalLookupJoin` then pushes it to the connector as a filter, and also offers it as a lookup key candidate. So a connector that needs the constant as part of its key, for example a key `(tenant, id)` with a constant tenant, can still select it, with or without filter pushdown. A range with a constant bound keeps requests batched and cached.
- A lookup key may come from WHERE, as for an ordinary join. An inner lookup join without a condition, such as `FROM s, t WHERE s.id = t.id` or a `CROSS JOIN`, gets its key from the filter above. A cross join counts as an inner join, as for an ordinary join. Only a join that still has no condition after pushdown fails with `MISSING_JOIN_CONDITION`, from `PrepareExternalLookupJoin`, and so as the query starts, through the startup check. The analysis check of #59909 for a streaming write without a condition is removed for this reason.
- A conjunct over lookup columns with a Python UDF, an external UDF or a subquery never moves, because the lookup side cannot evaluate it.
- A conjunct without references stays in the join condition, so a condition that folds to `false` still needs no lookup.

Each rule keeps the result on its own: excluding `EliminateOuterJoin` or `PushDownPredicates` with `spark.sql.optimizer.excludedRules` never changes a query's rows. Excluding `PushDownPredicates` can make a query fail to plan when its only lookup key is written in WHERE, because a lookup join cannot run without a key.

### Why are the changes needed?

Without this PR, a filter on the stream side of a lookup join applies only after every stream row has been looked up. Conditions on lookup columns reach the connector only when it selects them as lookup keys.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

There is no new API. Queries with filters on stream columns send fewer lookup requests, and filters on lookup columns can reach the connector. A left outer lookup join under a duplicate-agnostic aggregate over stream columns no longer runs. An inner lookup join whose key is written in WHERE, such as a comma join or a cross join, now runs.

### How was this patch tested?

`PushPredicateThroughExternalLookupJoinSuite` (new plan tests) covers each join type, the cases specific to lookup joins, and `EliminateOuterJoin`. An end-to-end test in `ExternalLookupJoinSuite` checks the requested keys, the filter that reaches the connector, constant keys that a connector needs, keys written in WHERE, and the same results with either rule excluded. The suites of the shared rules still pass: `OuterJoinEliminationSuite`, `FilterPushdownSuite` and `LeftSemiAntiJoinPushDownSuite`. All pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

issue.title: [SPARK-60693][SS][SQL] Add a lookup cache to external lookup join
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR adds a cache to external lookup join, so a repeated key does not cost another remote lookup. The cache is on by default.

This PR implements [SPARK-60693](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60693), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)). It builds on apache/spark#60055 (SPARK-60692, lookup-side projections and filters, semi and anti joins, range predicates).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| #59909 | Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes. |
| #59910 | Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| #60055 | Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns |
| **#60087 (this PR)** | **The lookup cache** |
| #60198 | Predicate pushdown through lookup joins |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

- **Scope and freshness.** There is one cache per input partition, inside a task. It is discarded when the task ends, so a cached result is never older than the task that read it. That is no staler than reading the static side once per micro-batch.
- **Contents.** The cache holds the complete result of each key, including keys with no rows. It stores only rows that pass Spark's own check of the lookup keys, after the lookup-side projections and filters. A result is cached only once it is fully read. A key whose rows take more than a sixteenth of `maxBytes` is still joined in full, but not cached, so the limit never truncates a result.
- **Range lookups are not cached.** When a selected lookup condition is a range whose value reads a stream column, the join caches nothing, even with the cache enabled. A range with a constant bound does not count, because every key carries the same value. Range values, such as event times, rarely repeat, so cached entries would rarely be used.
- **Bounds.** Its memory is bounded by bytes: `maxBytes` per input partition counts each entry's key and rows, with a fixed overhead per entry and per row, so keys with no rows count too. The cache evicts the least recently used keys (Guava), and has an optional time-to-live counted from the write. A partition's last request fills no cache, and the cache is released when the partition's input ends.
- **Metric.** `numCacheHits` counts the distinct keys served from the cache.

| Conf (`spark.sql.join.externalLookup.cache.*`) | Default |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` |
| `maxBytes` | `16m` per input partition |
| `ttl` | `0` (no expiry) |

The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint sets the same options for one join, for example `lookup.hint("external_lookup", "cache_ttl=30s")`. A string parameter that contains `=` is an option; any other string names a relation (#60019). A hint option overrides the session config for that join, and options it does not set follow the session config. An option-only hint above a join fails, because it cannot mark the lookup side. Invalid options fail with `INVALID_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT.*`.

For discussion: **on by default.** The SPIP's examples enable the cache, but the SPIP states no default. Its memory is bounded by `maxBytes`.

### Why are the changes needed?

A stream often repeats lookup keys. Without a cache, each request asks for its keys again, even when an earlier request of the same task has just read them. With the cache, later requests carry fewer parameter rows. A whole request goes away only when all its keys are cached, so the cache helps most when keys repeat across the requests of a partition.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. There are three new SQL configs and three `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint options, and the cache is on by default. Requests carry fewer parameter rows when keys repeat within an input partition, and fewer requests are sent when keys repeat across its requests.

### How was this patch tested?

`ExternalLookupJoinSuite` has new tests. They cover options and their errors, defaults and overrides, freshness, cached misses and expiry. They also cover the byte bound and the per-key cutoff, requests that mix cached and uncached keys, per-partition scope, oversized results, cache hits with lookup-side stages and each join type, and range lookups that skip the cache. Earlier tests that count connector requests opt out of the cache. All pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

issue.title: [SPARK-60690][SS][SQL] Execute basic stream-static external lookup joins
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

With this PR, a stream-static inner or left outer equi-join runs as an external lookup join when its right side is a lookup-only DSv2 table (`EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` without `BATCH_READ`). In each micro-batch, Spark looks up only the keys of that micro-batch's rows.

This PR implements [SPARK-60690](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60690), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)). It builds on apache/spark#59909 (SPARK-60689, planning rules).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| #59909 | Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes. |
| **#59910 (this PR)** | **Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle** |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| #60055 | Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns |
| #60087 | The lookup cache |
| #60198 | Predicate pushdown through lookup joins |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

```scala
val customers = spark.read.format("kv-store").load()     // lookup-only
orders.join(customers, orders("customerId") === customers("id"), "left_outer")
```

- **Wiring.** `FormExternalLookupJoin` runs at the start of optimization, and `PrepareExternalLookupJoin` runs after operator optimization, before `V2ScanRelationPushDown`. Neither can be excluded. `ExternalLookupJoinStrategy` plans the new `ExternalLookupJoinExec`, which needs no shuffle.
- **Rows that cannot match are not looked up.** This covers a null key, and a row that fails a condition on stream columns alone. Spark checks a condition this early only if it is deterministic and cannot throw. In an inner join, such rows take no slot in a request batch either, as an ordinary inner join filters them out before the join.

**The join's contract.** The SPIP discussion asked how this join behaves. This PR answers as follows:
- **Stream-static only.** The left side must be a streaming query.
- **Lookups read current data.** Each request reads the connector's data as it is at that moment. Requests are not snapshot boundaries, so the same key can match different rows in different requests, even within one micro-batch (SPIP Q6). Within one request, each key is sent once.
- **Spark checks the lookup keys itself.** The connector uses the conditions it selects to find rows. Spark evaluates them on every returned row and drops rows that fail, so a store that matches more loosely than Spark, for example case-insensitively, cannot add rows. Spark cannot detect a row the store fails to return, so the connector must return every matching row. That is why lookup keys are offered only on types with reliable equality (SPARK-60689).
- **A failure is never a miss.** A connector failure fails the task. So a left outer join never turns an error into a row padded with nulls.
- **Spark checks returned values.** A null where the table or the read schema rules it out, at any nested level, or a decimal that does not fit its type, fails the task.
- **Retries can see new values.** A retried or speculative task repeats its requests, and may get different rows.
- **Load on the store.** Each task sends synchronous requests of at most 1000 keys, or the connector's own limit if lower, and stops adding stream rows to a request once they reach 64 MB (`spark.sql.join.externalLookup.maxBatchBytes`), through one reader per input partition. Spark adds no request timeouts, request retries or rate limits; those belong to the connector.
- **Planning errors stop the query as it starts.** When a streaming query starts, its query thread plans the lookup joins once, before it creates any source, and discards the result. So a lookup join that cannot be planned, for example one without a lookup key, stops the query at once, instead of at its first micro-batch, which may come much later. The error reaches the user through `awaitTermination()`, `StreamingQuery.exception` and the listener's `QueryTerminatedEvent`. A join without any condition still fails `start()`, during analysis. Errors raised while the join runs still fail the micro-batch.

**Decision: the operator stays deterministic, on purpose.** It keeps its input's determinism level, usually DETERMINATE, and does not mark its output INDETERMINATE. The reasons:
- **It matches Spark SQL.** No Spark SQL operator is marked INDETERMINATE because its data can change. Scans of changing tables (JDBC, DSv2, files) and nondeterministic expressions such as `rand()` keep their input's level. Spark marks only round-robin repartition without its usual sort, and sampling after a shuffle, because their output depends on row order.
- **Retries are already protected.** The order-independent shuffle checksum, on by default, catches a retry that returns different rows. With `spark.sql.shuffle.orderIndependentChecksum.enableFullRetryOnMismatch` on, the default, and push-based shuffle merge off, Spark then reruns all tasks of the stages that read the shuffle, or aborts the job. In these settings, the scheduler ignores a declared INDETERMINATE level anyway.
- **For a streaming query, an aborted job fails the query.** A store whose data keeps changing makes a mismatch after a lost shuffle output more likely than a static table does. The user documentation will say so.
- **The flag would help only in non-default settings.** It changes behavior only with `enableFullRetryOnMismatch` off, or with push-based shuffle merge on. There it would rerun every lookup and every later stage on each lost shuffle output, even when the store did not change, instead of risking wrong results. A user who turns full retry off takes the same risk with any scan of a changing table.
- **It would block real-time mode.** The scheduler rejects an INDETERMINATE producer of a pipelined shuffle, so every stateful query after the join would fail. Real-time mode never retries part of a batch, so it does not need the flag. This PR rejects real-time mode; supporting it is later work.

Worth a reviewer's attention, because existing Spark code changes:
- `DataFrameReader` loads a lookup-only source as an `ExternalLookupRelation`, and `TableCapabilityCheck` lets it pass analysis. The exception is a command whose query reads one outside a lookup join: it fails during analysis, before it can drop or truncate its target. A provider whose lookup-only table also has a V1 read path fails to load, with a named error.
- `RewriteWithExpression` keeps the common expressions of a lookup join condition, such as the input of `BETWEEN`, inside the join.
- `ApplyCharTypePadding` rejects a lookup-only table that needs CHAR padding, because a lookup join cannot apply it yet.
- `MicroBatchExecution.logicalPlan` runs the startup check, `ExternalLookupJoinStartupCheck`, for a query with a lookup join, in the query thread and before any source is created. So a connector planning call that hangs blocks the query thread, never the user's code that called `start()`. **It optimizes a throwaway copy of the query and discards the result. Nothing from it is reused: each micro-batch plans from the analyzed plan, as before.** It represents the current time as a micro-batch does, and uses the configuration that the offset log pins on restart. The copy keeps only the lookup sides; the other static parts become placeholders, so their scans are not built. It uses the optimizer and configuration of the micro-batches, so it costs about one optimizer run, plus one round of the connector's planning calls, which every micro-batch already makes. Only lookup-specific planning errors stop the query this way; an error that an ordinary join would also raise stays with the micro-batch. The internal config `spark.sql.join.externalLookup.startupCheck.enabled` turns it off.
- `StreamingV2ScanPushDown.forStartup`, the startup plan of the column pruning of streaming scans (SPARK-60734), keeps the lookup sides, so it forms the same lookup joins as the micro-batches. Otherwise it would see an ordinary join, and a micro-batch could need a stream column that the scan does not read. The startup check shares this function.

Limits of this PR: the lookup table must be loaded with `spark.read` and sit directly on the right of the join. The later PRs in the scope table lift the other limits.

### Why are the changes needed?

A stream-static join reads its static side in every micro-batch, even when only a few keys match. A connector that serves key lookups can now run such a join by sending only the keys it needs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A stream-static join over a lookup-only DSv2 table now runs as an external lookup join, or fails with a named error. A lookup join that cannot be planned stops the query as it starts. Before this PR, `spark.read` could not load such a table. Tables without `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` are not affected. There is a new SQL config, `spark.sql.join.externalLookup.maxBatchBytes`.

### How was this patch tested?

`ExternalLookupJoinSuite` (new) runs stream-static joins end to end: planning and errors, results for both join types, request size and deduplication, skipped rows, Spark's checks of returned rows and values, reader lifecycle and metrics. `ExternalLookupJoinStartupCheckSuite` (new) checks which errors stop the query as it starts and which stay with the micro-batch, and that a planning call that blocks doesn't block `start()`. `ExternalLookupJoinRealTimeModeSuite` checks the real-time mode rejection. `TableCapabilityCheckSuite` and `PrepareExternalLookupJoinSuite` have new cases. All pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR pushes predicates through external lookup joins. A filter on stream columns then runs before the lookup, so fewer rows are looked up, and a condition on lookup columns can reach the connector as a filter. Query results are the same as for an ordinary join.

This PR implements [SPARK-60694](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60694), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)). It builds on apache/spark#60087 (SPARK-60693, the lookup cache).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| #59909 | Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes. |
| #59910 | Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| #60055 | Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns |
| #60087 | The lookup cache |
| **#60198 (this PR)** | **Predicate pushdown through lookup joins** |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

Worth a reviewer's attention, because existing optimizer rules change and no new rule is added:
- **`PushPredicateThroughJoin`** handles `ExternalLookupJoin` as it handles `AsOfJoin`, reusing its `split`. `PushDownPredicates` also visits plans with a lookup join.
- **`EliminateOuterJoin`** turns a left outer lookup join into an inner one when a filter above it rejects null lookup columns. It also removes a left outer lookup join under an aggregate that reads only stream columns and ignores duplicates, so no lookup runs. Its code is shared between joins and lookup joins.

What moves, for deterministic conjuncts, as for an ordinary join (a conjunct marked as throwing, such as `raise_error`, does not move):

| Where the conjunct is | Inner | Left outer | Left semi | Left anti |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Filter above, stream side only | stream side | stream side | stream side | stream side |
| Filter above, lookup side only | lookup side | stays above (1) | (not possible) | (not possible) |
| Filter above, both sides | join condition | stays above (1) | (not possible) | (not possible) |
| Join condition, lookup side only | lookup side | lookup side | lookup side | lookup side |
| Join condition, stream side only | stream side | stays | stream side | stays |

(1) Unless the filter rejects null lookup columns. Then `EliminateOuterJoin` makes the join inner, and the filter moves.

Cases specific to lookup joins:
- A comparison between a lookup column and a constant, such as `t.tier >= 2`, moves onto the lookup side as a filter, exactly as for an ordinary join. `PrepareExternalLookupJoin` then pushes it to the connector as a filter, and also offers it as a lookup key candidate. So a connector that needs the constant as part of its key, for example a key `(tenant, id)` with a constant tenant, can still select it, with or without filter pushdown. A range with a constant bound keeps requests batched and cached.
- A lookup key may come from WHERE, as for an ordinary join. An inner lookup join without a condition, such as `FROM s, t WHERE s.id = t.id` or a `CROSS JOIN`, gets its key from the filter above. A cross join counts as an inner join, as for an ordinary join. Only a join that still has no condition after pushdown fails with `MISSING_JOIN_CONDITION`, from `PrepareExternalLookupJoin`, and so as the query starts, through the startup check. The analysis check of #59909 for a streaming write without a condition is removed for this reason.
- A conjunct over lookup columns with a Python UDF, an external UDF or a subquery never moves, because the lookup side cannot evaluate it.
- A conjunct without references stays in the join condition, so a condition that folds to `false` still needs no lookup.

Each rule keeps the result on its own: excluding `EliminateOuterJoin` or `PushDownPredicates` with `spark.sql.optimizer.excludedRules` never changes a query's rows. Excluding `PushDownPredicates` can make a query fail to plan when its only lookup key is written in WHERE, because a lookup join cannot run without a key.

### Why are the changes needed?

Without this PR, a filter on the stream side of a lookup join applies only after every stream row has been looked up. Conditions on lookup columns reach the connector only when it selects them as lookup keys.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

There is no new API. Queries with filters on stream columns send fewer lookup requests, and filters on lookup columns can reach the connector. A left outer lookup join under a duplicate-agnostic aggregate over stream columns no longer runs. An inner lookup join whose key is written in WHERE, such as a comma join or a cross join, now runs.

### How was this patch tested?

`PushPredicateThroughExternalLookupJoinSuite` (new plan tests) covers each join type, the cases specific to lookup joins, and `EliminateOuterJoin`. An end-to-end test in `ExternalLookupJoinSuite` checks the requested keys, the filter that reaches the connector, constant keys that a connector needs, keys written in WHERE, and the same results with either rule excluded. The suites of the shared rules still pass: `OuterJoinEliminationSuite`, `FilterPushdownSuite` and `LeftSemiAntiJoinPushDownSuite`. All pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), posting on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Thanks for the review. Every inline point is addressed in [0c20a33fc99](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/0c20a33fc9915847ea1418b0f9195b0dcc7a3b9a), with a reply on each comment.

**Constant keys (your first two comments).** Constant comparisons now move onto the lookup side exactly as for an ordinary join, and lookup planning also offers them as key candidates. So a query that plans without these rules also plans with them, including for a source that needs a constant as part of its key.

**A key written in WHERE.** The AI review also found that `FROM s, t WHERE s.id = t.id` failed with `MISSING_JOIN_CONDITION`, while `JOIN ... ON TRUE WHERE s.id = t.id` planned. Both now plan, as for an ordinary join. A join that still has no condition after pushdown fails, from `start()`. Excluding `PushDownPredicates` can then make such a query fail to plan, because a lookup join can't run without a key, and the description says so.

+class ExternalLookupJoinSuite extends QueryTest with SharedSparkSession {
+
+  import testImplicits._
+
+  private val EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_CATALOG_NAME = "external_lookup_cat"
+  // The supportedJoinTypes parameter of a JOIN_TYPE error.
+  private val SUPPORTED_JOIN_TYPES = "INNER, LEFT OUTER, LEFT SEMI, LEFT ANTI"
+
+  private val streamRunCount = new AtomicInteger()
+
+  override def beforeEach(): Unit = {
+    super.beforeEach()
+    SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+    SemanticKeyExternalLookupDataSource.requestSizes.clear()
+  }
+
+  /** The rows of `df` as a streaming DataFrame: one micro-batch, in `numPartitions` partitions. */
+  private def streamOf(df: DataFrame, numPartitions: Int = 1): DataFrame = {
+    val input = MemoryStream[Row](numPartitions)(Encoders.row(df.schema), spark.sqlContext)
+    input.addData(df.collect().toSeq)
+    input.toDF()
+  }
+
+  private case class StreamRun(rows: Seq[Row], execution: IncrementalExecution) {
+    def plan: LogicalPlan = execution.optimizedPlan
+    def lookupJoin: ExternalLookupJoinExec = execution.executedPlan.collectFirst {
+      case exec: ExternalLookupJoinExec => exec
+    }.get
+  }
+
+  /** Runs the streaming `df` on a memory sink until it has processed all of its input. */
+  private def runStream(df: DataFrame, outputMode: String = "append"): StreamRun = {
+    val queryName = s"external_lookup_stream_${streamRunCount.incrementAndGet()}"
+    val query =
+      df.writeStream.format("memory").outputMode(outputMode).queryName(queryName).start()
+    try {
+      query.processAllAvailable()
+      StreamRun(
+        spark.table(queryName).collect().toSeq,
+        query.asInstanceOf[StreamingQueryWrapper].streamingQuery.lastExecution)
+    } finally {
+      query.stop()
+      spark.catalog.dropTempView(queryName)
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Runs `body` with `clock` as the clock of the lookup cache TTL. */
+  private def withCacheClock[T](clock: Clock)(body: => T): T = {
+    val previous = ExternalLookupJoinExec.cacheClock
+    ExternalLookupJoinExec.cacheClock = clock
+    try body finally ExternalLookupJoinExec.cacheClock = previous
+  }
+
+  private def checkStream(df: DataFrame, expected: Seq[Row]): Unit =
+    QueryTest.sameRows(expected, runStream(df).rows).foreach(fail(_))
+
+  /** The error that the streaming `df` fails with, when it starts or in a micro-batch. */
+  private def streamFailure[T <: Throwable : ClassTag](df: DataFrame): T = {
+    val cause = try {
+      runStream(df)
+      fail("The streaming query did not fail")
+    } catch {
+      case e: StreamingQueryException => e.getCause
+      case e: Throwable with SparkThrowable => e
+    }
+    assert(classTag[T].runtimeClass.isInstance(cause), cause)
+    cause.asInstanceOf[T]
+  }
+
+  test("a stream whose scan is pruned at the start reads the columns of its lookup joins") {
+    withSQLConf(
+        "spark.sql.catalog.stream_cat" -> classOf[InMemoryTableCatalog].getName,
+        SQLConf.STREAMING_V2_COLUMN_PRUNING_ENABLED.key -> "true") {
+      withTable("stream_cat.ns.badge_swipes") {
+        sql("CREATE TABLE stream_cat.ns.badge_swipes (employee INT, door STRING, minute INT) " +
+          s"TBLPROPERTIES ('${InMemoryBaseTable.STREAMING_COLUMN_PRUNING}' = 'true')")
+        sql("INSERT INTO stream_cat.ns.badge_swipes VALUES (1, 'lobby', 10), (3, 'garage', 20)")
+        val swipes = spark.readStream.table("stream_cat.ns.badge_swipes")
+        val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+        checkStream(
+          swipes.join(lookup, swipes("employee") === lookup("id"))
+            .select(swipes("door"), lookup("department")),
+          Seq(Row("lobby", "engineering"), Row("lobby", "research")))
+        // An aggregate that reads only stream columns and ignores duplicates does not need a left
+        // outer join, so the optimizer removes an ordinary one. A lookup join stays.
+        val latestByDoor = swipes.join(lookup, swipes("employee") === lookup("id"), "left_outer")
+          .groupBy(swipes("door")).agg(max(swipes("minute")))
+        QueryTest.sameRows(
+          Seq(Row("lobby", 10), Row("garage", 20)),
+          runStream(latestByDoor, "complete").rows).foreach(fail(_))
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("external lookup capability produces a unary external lookup join") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    val joined = left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"), "inner")
+
+    val plan = runStream(joined).plan
+    assert(plan.exists(_.isInstanceOf[PreparedExternalLookupJoin]))
+    assert(!plan.toString.contains("SimpleExternalLookupScan"))
+  }
+
+  test("a dual-capability source keeps an ordinary join unless the hint opts in") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[DualCapabilityExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    val expected = Seq(Row(1, 1, "engineering"), Row(1, 1, "research"))
+
+    assert(lookup.queryExecution.analyzed.isInstanceOf[DataSourceV2Relation])
+    assert(lookup.queryExecution.analyzed.isInstanceOf[ExternalLookupRelation] === false)
+    SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+    val ordinary = left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"), "inner")
+    assert(runStream(ordinary).plan.exists(_.isInstanceOf[PreparedExternalLookupJoin]) === false)
+    checkStream(ordinary, expected)
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.readerCount.get() === 0)
+
+    SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+    val hinted = lookup.hint("external_lookup")
+    val lookupJoin = left.join(hinted, left("id") === hinted("id"), "inner")
+    assert(runStream(lookupJoin).plan.exists(_.isInstanceOf[PreparedExternalLookupJoin]))
+    checkStream(lookupJoin, expected)
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.requestCount.get() > 0)
+  }
+
+  test("a hinted or aliased lookup side follows the stream-static contract") {
+    val dual = spark.read.format(classOf[DualCapabilityExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val lookupOnly = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val batch = Seq(1).toDF("id")
+    // Without the hint, a dual-capability table keeps an ordinary batch join.
+    checkAnswer(
+      batch.join(dual, batch("id") === dual("id")),
+      Seq(Row(1, 1, "engineering"), Row(1, 1, "research")))
+    // With it, the batch join fails: a hint the user wrote is never silently dropped.
+    Seq(
+      dual -> "`DualCapabilityExternalLookupTable`",
+      lookupOnly -> "`SimpleExternalLookupTable`").foreach { case (table, relation) =>
+      val hinted = table.hint("external_lookup")
+      checkError(
+        exception = intercept[AnalysisException] {
+          batch.join(hinted, batch("id") === hinted("id"))
+        },
+        condition = "EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.STATIC_LEFT_SIDE",
+        parameters = Map("relation" -> relation))
+    }
+    // A lookup-only table on the left side is found beneath an alias too.
+    val stream = streamOf(batch)
+    checkError(
+      exception = intercept[AnalysisException] {
+        lookupOnly.as("l").join(stream, $"l.id" === stream("id"))
+      },
+      condition = "EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.LOOKUP_TABLE_ON_LEFT",
+      parameters = Map("relation" -> "`SimpleExternalLookupTable`"))
+  }
+
+  test("a physical join strategy hint conflicts with the external lookup hint") {
+    val dual = spark.read.format(classOf[DualCapabilityExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    Seq(
+      "broadcast" -> "BROADCAST",
+      "merge" -> "MERGE",
+      "shuffle_hash" -> "SHUFFLE_HASH",
+      "shuffle_replicate_nl" -> "SHUFFLE_REPLICATE_NL").foreach { case (hint, strategy) =>
+      val lookupSide = dual.hint("external_lookup").hint(hint)
+      val streamSide = left.hint(hint)
+      val hinted = dual.hint("external_lookup")
+      Seq(
+        () => left.join(lookupSide, left("id") === lookupSide("id")),
+        () => streamSide.join(hinted, streamSide("id") === hinted("id"))).foreach { query =>
+        checkError(
+          exception = intercept[AnalysisException] { query().queryExecution.analyzed },
+          condition = "INVALID_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT.CONFLICTING_JOIN_STRATEGY",
+          parameters = Map(
+            "strategy" -> strategy,
+            "relation" -> "`DualCapabilityExternalLookupTable`"))
+      }
+    }
+    // Both hints may name the same relation, in either order. A strategy hint is never merged
+    // into the lookup hint, so the conflict is still reported.
+    withTempView("external_lookup_left", "external_lookup_right") {
+      left.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_left")
+      dual.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_right")
+      Seq("EXTERNAL_LOOKUP(r), MERGE(r)", "MERGE(r), EXTERNAL_LOOKUP(r)").foreach { hints =>
+        checkError(
+          exception = intercept[AnalysisException] {
+            sql(s"SELECT /*+ $hints */ * FROM external_lookup_left l " +
+              "JOIN external_lookup_right r ON l.id = r.id")
+          },
+          condition = "INVALID_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT.CONFLICTING_JOIN_STRATEGY",
+          parameters = Map(
+            "strategy" -> "MERGE",
+            "relation" -> "`DualCapabilityExternalLookupTable`"))
+      }
+    }
+
+    // Without the lookup hint, the strategy hint plans the ordinary join it asks for.
+    SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+    val ordinary = left.join(dual.hint("merge"), left("id") === dual("id"))
+    assert(runStream(ordinary).plan.exists(_.isInstanceOf[PreparedExternalLookupJoin]) === false)
+    checkStream(ordinary, Seq(Row(1, 1, "engineering"), Row(1, 1, "research")))
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.requestCount.get() === 0)
+  }
+
+  test("a hinted dual-capability source fails when no lookup access path exists") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[DualCapabilityExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val invoices = streamOf(Seq((1, "sales")).toDF("invoice", "costCenter"))
+
+    checkStream(
+      invoices.join(lookup, invoices("costCenter") === lookup("department")),
+      Seq(Row(1, "sales", 2, "sales")))
+    val hinted = lookup.hint("external_lookup")
+    checkError(
+      exception = streamFailure[AnalysisException](
+        invoices.join(hinted, invoices("costCenter") === hinted("department"))),
+      condition = "EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.NO_LOOKUP_PREDICATE",
+      parameters = Map("table" -> "`DualCapabilityExternalLookupTable`"))
+  }
+
+  test("a physical strategy hint on a lookup-only join is rejected") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1, 3).toDF("id"))
+    val withLookupHint = lookup.hint("external_lookup").hint("shuffle_hash")
+    Seq(
+      "BROADCAST" ->
+        (() => left.join(lookup.hint("broadcast"), left("id") === lookup("id"), "left_outer")),
+      "BROADCAST" ->
+        (() => left.join(broadcast(lookup), left("id") === lookup("id"), "left_outer")),
+      "MERGE" -> (() => left.hint("merge").join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"))),
+      "SHUFFLE_HASH" ->
+        (() => left.join(withLookupHint, left("id") === withLookupHint("id")))).foreach {
+      case (strategy, query) =>
+        checkError(
+          exception = intercept[AnalysisException] { query().queryExecution.analyzed },
+          condition = "EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.CONFLICTING_JOIN_STRATEGY",
+          parameters = Map("strategy" -> strategy, "relation" -> "`SimpleExternalLookupTable`"))
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("an ordinary join over an enriched lookup join result stays ordinary") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val events = streamOf(Seq(1, 2).toDF("id"))
+    val enriched = events.join(lookup, events("id") === lookup("id"))
+      .select(events("id").as("event_id"), lookup("department"))
+    val base = Seq((1, "a"), (2, "b")).toDF("id", "tag")
+    val expected = Seq(
+      Row(1, "a", 1, "engineering"), Row(1, "a", 1, "research"), Row(2, "b", 2, "sales"))
+    def lookupJoinCount(df: DataFrame): Int =
+      runStream(df).plan.collect { case j: PreparedExternalLookupJoin => j }.size
+
+    val joined = base.join(enriched, base("id") === enriched("event_id"))
+    assert(lookupJoinCount(joined) === 1)
+    checkStream(joined, expected)
+
+    withTempView("external_lookup_base", "external_lookup_events", "external_lookup_right") {
+      base.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_base")
+      events.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_events")
+      lookup.createOrReplaceTempView("external_lookup_right")
+      val sqlJoined = sql(
+        """
+          |SELECT b.id, b.tag, e.event_id, e.department
+          |FROM external_lookup_base b JOIN (
+          |  SELECT v.id AS event_id, r.department
+          |  FROM external_lookup_events v JOIN external_lookup_right r ON v.id = r.id) e
+          |ON b.id = e.event_id
+          |""".stripMargin)
+      assert(lookupJoinCount(sqlJoined) === 1)
+      checkStream(sqlJoined, expected)
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("an external lookup hint outside any join is ignored") {
+    val dual = spark.read.format(classOf[DualCapabilityExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val expected = Seq(Row(1, "engineering"), Row(1, "research"), Row(2, "sales"))
+
+    checkAnswer(dual.hint("external_lookup"), expected)
+    assert(dual.hint("external_lookup", "cache_enabled=false").count() === 3)
+    withTempView("external_lookup_right") {

+  test("a stream row that fails a stream-side conjunct of the condition is not looked up") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(
+      Seq((1, Some(true)), (2, Some(false)), (3, Some(true)), (4, None)).toDF("id", "flag"))
+    val key = left("id") === lookup("id")
+    // The join checks `flag` on each stream row before the lookup. A row where it is false or null
+    // cannot match, so its key is not requested: an inner or left semi join drops the row, a left
+    // outer join pads it with nulls, and a left anti join returns it.
+    val matched = Seq(Row(1, true, 1, "engineering"), Row(1, true, 1, "research"))
+    val unmatched =
+      Seq(Row(2, false, null, null), Row(3, true, null, null), Row(4, null, null, null))
+    Seq(
+      "inner" -> matched,
+      "left_outer" -> (matched ++ unmatched),
+      "left_semi" -> Seq(Row(1, true)),
+      "left_anti" -> Seq(Row(2, false), Row(3, true), Row(4, null))).foreach {
+      case (joinType, expected) =>
+        SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+        checkStream(left.join(lookup, key && left("flag"), joinType), expected)
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.requestedKeys.asScala.toSeq === Seq(1, 3))
+    }
+
+    // A conjunct that can throw is not checked early: it is evaluated on the joined rows only, so
+    // never for id 3, which has no match, and every key is requested.
+    SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+    val throwing = when(left("id") === 3, raise_error(lit("evaluated for id 3"))).otherwise(true)
+    checkStream(
+      left.join(lookup, key && throwing, "left_outer"),
+      matched ++ Seq(Row(2, false, 2, "sales"), Row(3, true, null, null), Row(4, null, null, null)))
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.requestedKeys.asScala.toSeq === Seq(1, 2, 3, 4))
+
+    // A conjunct that is not deterministic is not checked early either. Analysis rejects one in a
+    // join condition, so the physical join gets one directly: `id + rand(0) < 0`. It is false for
+    // every row, but it is evaluated on the joined rows only, so every key is requested.
+    val lookupJoin = runStream(left.join(lookup, key, "left_outer")).lookupJoin
+    val streamId = lookupJoin.child.output.head
+    val nonDeterministic =
+      LessThan(Add(Cast(streamId, DoubleType), Rand(Literal(0L))), Literal(0.0))
+    SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+    val rows = lookupJoin.copy(
+      residualCondition = Some(nonDeterministic),
+      child = LocalTableScanExec(
+        lookupJoin.child.output, Seq(InternalRow(1, true), InternalRow(2, false)), None))
+      .executeCollect()
+    assert(rows.map(row => row.getInt(0) -> row.isNullAt(2)).toSeq === Seq(1 -> true, 2 -> true))
+    // Each row is in its own partition, so the order of the requests can vary.
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.requestedKeys.asScala.toSeq.sorted === Seq(1, 2))
+  }

Fixed in [0c20a33fc99](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/0c20a33fc9915847ea1418b0f9195b0dcc7a3b9a): the test uses an ANSI string-to-INT cast under ANSI mode, which `canEvaluateUnconditionally` rejects with or without SPARK-60882, so only the pushdown moves it.

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), posting on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

We'd keep it. An ordinary join is removed in the same case, and we follow the rule that a lookup join behaves as an ordinary join does, unless a lookup makes that impossible. It costs the shared extractor, and it skips every lookup for such a query. I fixed the stale comment, and that part of the test now also reads a lookup value, so it still runs a lookup join ([0c20a33fc99](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/0c20a33fc9915847ea1418b0f9195b0dcc7a3b9a)).

issue.title: [SPARK-60693][SS][SQL] Add a lookup cache to external lookup join
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR adds a cache to external lookup join, so a repeated key does not cost another remote lookup. The cache is on by default.

This PR implements [SPARK-60693](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60693), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)). It builds on apache/spark#60055 (SPARK-60692, lookup-side projections and filters, semi and anti joins, range predicates).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| #59909 | Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes. |
| #59910 | Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| #60055 | Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns |
| **#60087 (this PR)** | **The lookup cache** |
| #60198 | Predicate pushdown through lookup joins |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

- **Scope and freshness.** There is one cache per input partition, inside a task. It is discarded when the task ends, so a cached result is never older than the task that read it. That is no staler than reading the static side once per micro-batch.
- **Contents.** The cache holds the complete result of each key, including keys with no rows. It stores only rows that pass Spark's own check of the lookup keys, after the lookup-side projections and filters. A result is cached only once it is fully read. A key whose rows take more than a sixteenth of `maxBytes` is still joined in full, but not cached, so the limit never truncates a result.
- **Range lookups are not cached.** When a selected lookup condition is a range whose value reads a stream column, the join caches nothing, even with the cache enabled. A range with a constant bound does not count, because every key carries the same value. Range values, such as event times, rarely repeat, so cached entries would rarely be used.
- **Bounds.** Its memory is bounded by bytes: `maxBytes` per input partition counts each entry's key and rows, with a fixed overhead per entry and per row, so keys with no rows count too. The cache evicts the least recently used keys (Guava), and has an optional time-to-live counted from the write. A partition's last request fills no cache, and the cache is released when the partition's input ends.
- **Metric.** `numCacheHits` counts the distinct keys served from the cache.

| Conf (`spark.sql.join.externalLookup.cache.*`) | Default |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` |
| `maxBytes` | `16m` per input partition |
| `ttl` | `0` (no expiry) |

The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint sets the same options for one join, for example `lookup.hint("external_lookup", "cache_ttl=30s")`. A string parameter that contains `=` is an option; any other string names a relation (#60019). A hint option overrides the session config for that join, and options it does not set follow the session config. An option-only hint above a join fails, because it cannot mark the lookup side. Invalid options fail with `INVALID_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_HINT.*`.

For discussion: **on by default.** The SPIP's examples enable the cache, but the SPIP states no default. Its memory is bounded by `maxBytes`.

### Why are the changes needed?

A stream often repeats lookup keys. Without a cache, each request asks for its keys again, even when an earlier request of the same task has just read them. With the cache, later requests carry fewer parameter rows. A whole request goes away only when all its keys are cached, so the cache helps most when keys repeat across the requests of a partition.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. There are three new SQL configs and three `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint options, and the cache is on by default. Requests carry fewer parameter rows when keys repeat within an input partition, and fewer requests are sent when keys repeat across its requests.

### How was this patch tested?

`ExternalLookupJoinSuite` has new tests. They cover options and their errors, defaults and overrides, freshness, cached misses and expiry. They also cover the byte bound and the per-key cutoff, requests that mix cached and uncached keys, per-partition scope, oversized results, cache hits with lookup-side stages and each join type, and range lookups that skip the cache. Earlier tests that count connector requests opt out of the cache. All pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.
