issue.title: [SPARK-60692][SS][SQL] Support lookup-side projections and filters, semi/anti joins and range predicates in external lookup join
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR lets more queries run as external lookup joins:
- projections and filters on the lookup side, including views and SQL subqueries;
- left semi and left anti joins;
- `<=>` and range comparisons (`<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`), offered to the connector as lookup conditions;
- lookup-only tables with CHAR columns.

This PR implements [SPARK-60692](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60692), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)). It builds on apache/spark#60019 (SPARK-60691, the `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| #59909 | Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes. |
| #59910 | Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| **#60055 (this PR)** | **Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns** |
| #60087 | The lookup cache |
| #60198 | Predicate pushdown through lookup joins |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

```scala
val active = profiles.where($"active").select($"id", upper($"tier").as("tier"))
orders.join(active, orders("userId") === active("id"))                    // lookup-side stages
events.join(rates, events("ccy") === rates("ccy") &&
  events("ts") >= rates("validFrom") && events("ts") < rates("validTo"))  // equality + range
```

Worth a reviewer's attention:
- **Lookup-side stages.** Spark evaluates the lookup side's projections and filters on each row the connector returns, before joining it. Filters go to the connector first, as in `V2ScanRelationPushDown`, and Spark still evaluates every filter on the returned rows, including those the connector accepts. A nondeterministic projection or filter, a Python UDF, an external UDF or a subquery cannot run in a stage, so such a lookup side fails with `LOOKUP_PLAN`.
- **A change to an existing rule.** `ColumnPruning` gets two cases for `ExternalLookupJoin`, next to its case for left existence joins. With them, the join keeps only the lookup columns that are used. The lookup scan is then pruned once the connector has selected its lookup conditions.
- **Comparisons.** A comparison is offered with the lookup column on the left, so `s.ts < t.ts` becomes `ts > ?`. `<=>` is offered on the same types as `=`. Ranges are offered only on integral types, decimal, date and timestamps, because stores order strings and binary values differently from Spark. A range is offered only when its stream-side value cannot fail; a widening numeric cast, such as INT to BIGINT, is allowed. Spark evaluates the selected comparisons itself on every returned row, so column pruning keeps their columns. The others stay in Spark's remaining join condition.
- **One parameter row per range request.** When a selected range comparison reads a stream column, each request holds exactly one parameter row, and a batch takes the consecutive stream rows that share it, up to 1000 rows or the source's lower limit. A range with a constant bound keeps batching. Otherwise one stored row could match several parameter rows of a request, the connector would have to return it for each of them, and Spark could not detect a missing one. Equality lookups keep batching.
- **CHAR columns.** `ApplyCharTypePadding` now pads a lookup-only table as it pads a batch read, as a lookup-side stage. So the `CHAR_VARCHAR_COLUMN` error is removed. CHAR columns are still not offered as lookup keys. VARCHAR columns are offered for `<=>` too, as for `=`.

Semi and anti joins emit a stream row on its first match, or when it has no match. Stream rows that cannot match are skipped for them too, as in SPARK-60690.

### Why are the changes needed?

Real lookup queries project and filter the lookup table, use semi or anti joins, and look up ranges, such as the exchange rate valid at an event's time. These queries failed before this PR.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. These query shapes now run as external lookup joins, and `<=>` and range comparisons reach the connector as lookup conditions.

### How was this patch tested?

`ExternalLookupJoinSuite` has new end-to-end tests: lookup-side stages, filter pushdown and column pruning, semi and anti joins, comparisons and the request size for ranges, CHAR and VARCHAR, and errors. `ColumnPruningSuite`, `PrepareExternalLookupJoinSuite` and `FormExternalLookupJoinSuite` have new cases. All pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

+  private class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator extends PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] {
+    override def eval(

+        inputs: Iterator[InternalRow]*): Iterator[InternalRow] = {

+  /** Joins one partition batch by batch, and closes its reader after the last batch. */

+    extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    private val reader = new LookupReader
+    private val parameters = new LookupParameters(partitionIndex)
+    private val resultRows = new LookupResultRows
+    private val transforms = new LookupTransforms(partitionIndex)
+    private val joinOutput = new JoinOutput(partitionIndex)
+    private var batch: Iterator[InternalRow] = Iterator.empty
+    private var inputExhausted = false
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      batch.hasNext
+    }
+

+      tryAdvance()

+          errorClass = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+          messageParameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup join exhausted"))
+      }
+      batch.next()
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */

+      while (!batch.hasNext && !inputExhausted) {
+        val rows = readBatch()

+          batch = new BatchJoinIterator(
+            rows, parameters, resultRows, transforms, joinOutput, reader)
+        }
+        inputExhausted = !input.hasNext
+      }
+      if (inputExhausted && !batch.hasNext) reader.close()
+    }

+    private lazy val toUnsafe = UnsafeProjection.create(streamOutput, streamOutput)

+    // The batch holds its rows until its request is read, so it stops once their copies reach
+    // maxBatchBytes, keeping the row that reaches it, as well as at maxParameterRowsPerRequest

+    private def readBatch(): Array[InternalRow] = {
+      val rows = mutable.ArrayBuffer.empty[InternalRow]
+      var bytes = 0L
+      while (rows.length < maxParameterRowsPerRequest && bytes < maxBatchBytes && input.hasNext) {
+        val row = input.next() match {
+          case unsafe: UnsafeRow => unsafe.copy()
+          case other => toUnsafe(other).copy()

+        bytes += row.getSizeInBytes
+        rows += row
+      }
+      rows.toArray
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** The stream rows that share a key, and the one request row sent for them. */
+  private case class KeyEntry(requestRow: UnsafeRow, rowIndexes: mutable.ArrayBuffer[Int])
+
+  /**
+   * Joins one batch of stream rows. Rows whose parameters are equal under Spark equality share
+   * one request row, and every result row for a request row that satisfies the selected lookup
+   * predicates joins all the stream rows sharing it. A stream row is finished, which may emit its
+   * unmatched output row, once no more result rows can match it.
+   *
+   * Output rows are projected into a reused row on `next()`, so the consumer copies the rows it
+   * retains, as with other join iterators.
+   */
+  private class BatchJoinIterator(
+      rows: Array[InternalRow],
+      parameters: LookupParameters,
+      resultRows: LookupResultRows,
+      transforms: LookupTransforms,
+      joinOutput: JoinOutput,
+      reader: LookupReader) extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    metrics.inputRows += rows.length
+    metrics.inputBatches += 1
+
+    private val matched = Array.fill(rows.length)(false)
+    private val finished = mutable.BitSet.empty
+    // Output rows not yet returned: a stream row index and the lookup row it is joined with.
+    private val pending = mutable.Queue.empty[(Int, InternalRow)]
+
+    // One entry for each distinct key that can match, in the order of first occurrence. A row
+    // that can never match, because it fails the stream condition or has a null parameter, is
+    // finished right away, and its key is not requested. The stream condition is checked before
+    // the key is computed, so that it can guard the parameter expressions.
+    private val keyEntries = mutable.LinkedHashMap.empty[UnsafeRow, KeyEntry]
+    rows.indices.foreach { index =>
+      lazy val key = parameters.key(rows(index))
+      if (!joinOutput.canMatch(rows(index)) || parameters.matchesNothing(key)) {
+        finish(index)
+      } else {
+        keyEntries.get(key) match {
+          case Some(entry) => entry.rowIndexes += index
+          case None => keyEntries.put(
+            key.copy(),
+            KeyEntry(parameters.requestRow(rows(index)), mutable.ArrayBuffer(index)))
+        }
+      }
+    }
+    private val requestedKeys = keyEntries.keys.toArray
+
+    // No connector request, and no reader, when no key can match. The connector gets copies of
+    // the request rows, so that the ones that Spark checks the results against stay its own.
+    private var cursor: ExternalLookupResultCursor =
+      if (keyEntries.isEmpty) EmptyLookupCursor
+      else connectorCall(reader.lookup(keyEntries.values.map(_.requestRow.copy()).toArray))
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      pending.nonEmpty
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      if (pending.isEmpty) throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+      val (index, lookupRow) = pending.dequeue()
+      joinOutput.project(rows(index), lookupRow)
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryFillPending(): Unit = {
+      try {
+        while (pending.isEmpty && advanceCursor()) {
+          reader.resultRowRead()
+          // A close() during either call fails the read before Spark copies or joins the row.
+          val start = System.nanoTime()
+          val ordinal = cursor.inputOrdinal()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val connectorRow = cursor.get()
+          metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+          if (connectorRow == null) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName, "NULL_RESULT", Map("method" -> "ExternalLookupResultCursor.get()"))
+          }

+          val resultRow = reader.copyRow(resultRows.validatedCopy(connectorRow))
+          if (parameters.selectedPredicatesHold(keyEntries(key).requestRow, resultRow)) {
+            // The lookup-side stages reuse their output row, and several stream rows can join it.
+            transforms(resultRow).foreach(lookupRow => joinResultRow(key, lookupRow.copy()))

issue.title: [SPARK-60690][SS][SQL] Execute basic stream-static external lookup joins
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

With this PR, a stream-static inner or left outer equi-join runs as an external lookup join when its right side is a lookup-only DSv2 table (`EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` without `BATCH_READ`). In each micro-batch, Spark looks up only the keys of that micro-batch's rows.

This PR implements [SPARK-60690](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60690), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)). It builds on apache/spark#59909 (SPARK-60689, planning rules).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| #59909 | Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes. |
| **#59910 (this PR)** | **Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle** |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| #60055 | Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns |
| #60087 | The lookup cache |
| #60198 | Predicate pushdown through lookup joins |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

```scala
val customers = spark.read.format("kv-store").load()     // lookup-only
orders.join(customers, orders("customerId") === customers("id"), "left_outer")
```

- **Wiring.** `FormExternalLookupJoin` runs at the start of optimization, and `PrepareExternalLookupJoin` runs after operator optimization, before `V2ScanRelationPushDown`. Neither can be excluded. `ExternalLookupJoinStrategy` plans the new `ExternalLookupJoinExec`, which needs no shuffle.
- **Rows that cannot match are not looked up.** This covers a null key, and a row that fails a condition on stream columns alone. Spark checks a condition this early only if it is deterministic and cannot throw. In an inner join, such rows take no slot in a request batch either, as an ordinary inner join filters them out before the join.

**The join's contract.** The SPIP discussion asked how this join behaves. This PR answers as follows:
- **Stream-static only.** The left side must be a streaming query.
- **Lookups read current data.** Each request reads the connector's data as it is at that moment. Requests are not snapshot boundaries, so the same key can match different rows in different requests, even within one micro-batch (SPIP Q6). Within one request, each key is sent once.
- **Spark checks the lookup keys itself.** The connector uses the conditions it selects to find rows. Spark evaluates them on every returned row and drops rows that fail, so a store that matches more loosely than Spark, for example case-insensitively, cannot add rows. Spark cannot detect a row the store fails to return, so the connector must return every matching row. That is why lookup keys are offered only on types with reliable equality (SPARK-60689).
- **A failure is never a miss.** A connector failure fails the task. So a left outer join never turns an error into a row padded with nulls.
- **Spark checks returned values.** A null where the table or the read schema rules it out, at any nested level, or a decimal that does not fit its type, fails the task.
- **Retries can see new values.** A retried or speculative task repeats its requests, and may get different rows.
- **Load on the store.** Each task sends synchronous requests of at most 1000 keys, or the connector's own limit if lower, and stops adding stream rows to a request once they reach 64 MB (`spark.sql.join.externalLookup.maxBatchBytes`), through one reader per input partition. Spark adds no request timeouts, request retries or rate limits; those belong to the connector.
- **Planning errors stop the query as it starts.** When a streaming query starts, its query thread plans the lookup joins once, before it creates any source, and discards the result. So a lookup join that cannot be planned, for example one without a lookup key, stops the query at once, instead of at its first micro-batch, which may come much later. The error reaches the user through `awaitTermination()`, `StreamingQuery.exception` and the listener's `QueryTerminatedEvent`. A join without any condition still fails `start()`, during analysis. Errors raised while the join runs still fail the micro-batch.

**Decision: the operator stays deterministic, on purpose.** It keeps its input's determinism level, usually DETERMINATE, and does not mark its output INDETERMINATE. The reasons:
- **It matches Spark SQL.** No Spark SQL operator is marked INDETERMINATE because its data can change. Scans of changing tables (JDBC, DSv2, files) and nondeterministic expressions such as `rand()` keep their input's level. Spark marks only round-robin repartition without its usual sort, and sampling after a shuffle, because their output depends on row order.
- **Retries are already protected.** The order-independent shuffle checksum, on by default, catches a retry that returns different rows. With `spark.sql.shuffle.orderIndependentChecksum.enableFullRetryOnMismatch` on, the default, and push-based shuffle merge off, Spark then reruns all tasks of the stages that read the shuffle, or aborts the job. In these settings, the scheduler ignores a declared INDETERMINATE level anyway.
- **For a streaming query, an aborted job fails the query.** A store whose data keeps changing makes a mismatch after a lost shuffle output more likely than a static table does. The user documentation will say so.
- **The flag would help only in non-default settings.** It changes behavior only with `enableFullRetryOnMismatch` off, or with push-based shuffle merge on. There it would rerun every lookup and every later stage on each lost shuffle output, even when the store did not change, instead of risking wrong results. A user who turns full retry off takes the same risk with any scan of a changing table.
- **It would block real-time mode.** The scheduler rejects an INDETERMINATE producer of a pipelined shuffle, so every stateful query after the join would fail. Real-time mode never retries part of a batch, so it does not need the flag. This PR rejects real-time mode; supporting it is later work.

Worth a reviewer's attention, because existing Spark code changes:
- `DataFrameReader` loads a lookup-only source as an `ExternalLookupRelation`, and `TableCapabilityCheck` lets it pass analysis. The exception is a command whose query reads one outside a lookup join: it fails during analysis, before it can drop or truncate its target. A provider whose lookup-only table also has a V1 read path fails to load, with a named error.
- `RewriteWithExpression` keeps the common expressions of a lookup join condition, such as the input of `BETWEEN`, inside the join.
- `ApplyCharTypePadding` rejects a lookup-only table that needs CHAR padding, because a lookup join cannot apply it yet.
- `MicroBatchExecution.logicalPlan` runs the startup check, `ExternalLookupJoinStartupCheck`, for a query with a lookup join, in the query thread and before any source is created. So a connector planning call that hangs blocks the query thread, never the user's code that called `start()`. **It optimizes a throwaway copy of the query and discards the result. Nothing from it is reused: each micro-batch plans from the analyzed plan, as before.** It represents the current time as a micro-batch does, and uses the configuration that the offset log pins on restart. The copy keeps only the lookup sides; the other static parts become placeholders, so their scans are not built. It uses the optimizer and configuration of the micro-batches, so it costs about one optimizer run, plus one round of the connector's planning calls, which every micro-batch already makes. Only lookup-specific planning errors stop the query this way; an error that an ordinary join would also raise stays with the micro-batch. The internal config `spark.sql.join.externalLookup.startupCheck.enabled` turns it off.
- `StreamingV2ScanPushDown.forStartup`, the startup plan of the column pruning of streaming scans (SPARK-60734), keeps the lookup sides, so it forms the same lookup joins as the micro-batches. Otherwise it would see an ordinary join, and a micro-batch could need a stream column that the scan does not read. The startup check shares this function.

Limits of this PR: the lookup table must be loaded with `spark.read` and sit directly on the right of the join. The later PRs in the scope table lift the other limits.

### Why are the changes needed?

A stream-static join reads its static side in every micro-batch, even when only a few keys match. A connector that serves key lookups can now run such a join by sending only the keys it needs.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. A stream-static join over a lookup-only DSv2 table now runs as an external lookup join, or fails with a named error. A lookup join that cannot be planned stops the query as it starts. Before this PR, `spark.read` could not load such a table. Tables without `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` are not affected. There is a new SQL config, `spark.sql.join.externalLookup.maxBatchBytes`.

### How was this patch tested?

`ExternalLookupJoinSuite` (new) runs stream-static joins end to end: planning and errors, results for both join types, request size and deduplication, skipped rows, Spark's checks of returned rows and values, reader lifecycle and metrics. `ExternalLookupJoinStartupCheckSuite` (new) checks which errors stop the query as it starts and which stay with the micro-batch, and that a planning call that blocks doesn't block `start()`. `ExternalLookupJoinRealTimeModeSuite` checks the real-time mode rejection. `TableCapabilityCheckSuite` and `PrepareExternalLookupJoinSuite` have new cases. All pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

**How much contract the first version commits to.** Agreed. The task-end close now promises no more than `DataSourceRDD` does (see the inline thread).

issue.title: [SPARK-60689][SS][SQL] Add the planning rules for external lookup join
issue.body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

This PR adds the planning pieces of an external lookup join: a stream-static join whose right side is a table that the connector serves by key lookups. Nothing registers the new rules yet, so no query changes. SPARK-60690 registers them and runs the joins.

This PR implements [SPARK-60689](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60689), part of [SPARK-60031](https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/SPARK-60031) (SPIP: External Lookup Join; see the [SPIP](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBPM5cku8UJXacG2fw9df1zqALJ-WFm8E9-b9oiFP5M/edit?tab=t.0) and the [dev@ discussion](https://lists.apache.org/thread/7s6tgy9cm18jnzykr8htrtrw4nxyrhp1)).

**Design and decisions.** The [design document](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) explains the whole feature and the decisions behind it, including those agreed in the SPIP discussion. Read it first for the whole picture, before the details of this PR.

**Scope.** This PR is one of six stacked PRs for external lookup join. The connector API, #59908, is already merged. Please review only this PR's own commits, listed in its first comment. The commits of the PRs it builds on are reviewed there.

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| **#59909 (this PR)** | **Planning rules. They are not registered yet, so no query changes.** |
| #59910 | Execution: stream-static equi-joins on lookup-only tables loaded with `spark.read`; Spark's check of returned rows and values; the reader lifecycle |
| #60019 | The `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` hint; lookup sides reached through aliases, temp views of DataFrames, SQL and catalog references |
| #60055 | Lookup-side projections and filters; semi and anti joins; `<=>` and range comparisons; CHAR columns |
| #60087 | The lookup cache |
| #60198 | Predicate pushdown through lookup joins |

The connector API Javadoc describes the whole feature. Some of its promises are kept only by the later PRs in this table.

- **Logical nodes.** `ExternalLookupRelation` stands for a lookup-only table, one that supports `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP` but not `BATCH_READ`. `ExternalLookupJoin` is the lookup join. `PreparedExternalLookupJoin` is the join after Spark has agreed on the lookup with the connector.
- **Forming the join.** The analyzed plan keeps an ordinary `Join`. `FormExternalLookupJoin` turns an eligible join into an `ExternalLookupJoin` at the start of optimization. `CheckExternalLookupJoin` applies the same test at analysis, so most ineligible joins fail with their reason when the DataFrame is built. For a streaming write, it also rejects a join without a condition, so `start()` throws that error. Eligible means a streaming left side, a lookup-only table directly on the right, an inner or left outer join, and a join condition.
- **Agreeing on the lookup.** `PrepareExternalLookupJoin` offers each `lookupColumn = <stream-side expression>` conjunct to the connector as a possible lookup key. The connector selects the ones it can use. Spark evaluates the rest of the condition on the joined rows, with equalities and conditions that cannot fail first, as a hash join checks its keys first. From SPARK-60690, Spark also evaluates the selected ones itself, on every row the connector returns. The rule also validates what the connector returns.
- **Connector API Javadoc.** This PR also updates the connector API Javadoc. It says which types Spark offers as lookup keys, that Spark checks the selected predicates on every returned row (from #59910), that the read schema's nullability may differ from the table's, at any nested level, when parameter rows count as distinct, and that parameter rows are read-only.

Worth a reviewer's attention:
- **Lookup keys only on types with reliable equality.** A store's equality can differ from Spark's, for example for NaN and `-0.0`, or for case and accent rules. So Spark offers a comparison only on integral types, boolean, decimal, date, timestamps, binary, and strings with the default binary collation. CHAR columns are not offered, because a store may pad or compare them differently. VARCHAR columns are offered, except under `spark.sql.charVarchar.standardSemantics.enabled`. There, Spark drops the trailing blanks past the declared length from a longer stored value when it reads it, so a store that compares the stored value could miss a row. Other comparisons stay in Spark's condition. If no candidate is left, the join fails with `NO_LOOKUP_CANDIDATE`.
- A join strategy hint that attaches to a lookup join fails the query. A lookup join cannot honor a physical strategy, and Spark does not silently drop a hint the user wrote.
- Joins over tables that also support `BATCH_READ` are unchanged. So is a join whose lookup-only table is not its direct right child: it still fails as a plain scan.

New error conditions: `EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.*` for joins that cannot run as lookup joins, and `DATA_SOURCE_INVALID_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP.*` for connectors that break the contract.

### Why are the changes needed?

A lookup join needs planning that other joins do not have. Spark must decide which joins read a lookup-only table, and agree with the connector on which conditions become lookup keys.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The rules are not registered yet.

### How was this patch tested?

New plan tests: `FormExternalLookupJoinSuite` (catalyst) covers eligibility and its errors, and `PrepareExternalLookupJoinSuite` covers the negotiation and the connector contract. They pass on JDK 21 at the top of the PR stack, which includes this PR.

### Was this patch authored or co-authored using generative AI tooling?

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), posting on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Thanks for the review. All inline points are addressed in [e3212ca903a](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/e3212ca903ab0d829feab6150bda53ea5ad88cfa), with a reply on each comment. On the two design questions:

**A separate node instead of a marked `Join`.** The [design doc](https://gist.github.com/HeartSaVioR/0143cdaad3079d1455be8004ee401ec4) now records this trade-off as P8, in section 6. In short:
- **The two joins differ in ways the optimizer cares about.** A lookup join's right side must stay a table read by lookups, and its stream side must stay on the left. So it must never be reordered, swapped, turned into a cross join or planned by `JoinSelection`. Optimizations and hints written for `Join` do not carry over: strategy hints conflict with it, for example.
- **Diverging early is safer than diverging late.** With a marked `Join`, every existing and future `Join` rule applies by default. Each one that can break the points above would need its own guard, and a missing guard silently gives a wrong plan. With a separate node, a missing rule only costs an optimization.
- **Structured Streaming learned this with stateful operators.** They diverged from their batch counterparts only at physical planning, picked up optimizations written for the batch operators, and became fragile.

**Errors after `start()`.** Agreed: they should fail when the query starts. This round does that in two parts. Please check whether the second is more machinery than you had in mind.
- **`MISSING_JOIN_CONDITION`** is now reported during analysis of the streaming write, which is complete when the query starts ([e3212ca903a](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/e3212ca903ab0d829feab6150bda53ea5ad88cfa)). In #60198, a lookup key may also come from a WHERE clause, as for an ordinary join, so there the startup check reports a join that is still without a condition.
- **The other planning errors** need the optimizer, because simplification and predicate pushdown can add lookup conditions. So #59910 adds a dry run in `StreamingQueryManager.createQuery`, in the thread that calls `start()` ([ff67010628f](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/ff67010628ff2215bc180eb23c1d60ae7e4181cc)):
  - **It optimizes a throwaway copy of the query, and discards the result.** Nothing from it is reused: each micro-batch still plans from the analyzed plan, as before.
  - The copy keeps only the lookup sides. The other static parts become placeholders, so their scans are neither built nor planned at the start.
  - It uses the optimizer and the configuration of the micro-batches, including the values that the offset log pins for a restarted query.
  - Only lookup-specific planning errors fail `start()`. An error that an ordinary join would also raise at the first micro-batch stays there, and so do errors raised while the join runs.
  - **Cost:** about one optimizer run, 3 to 7 ms in local tests, plus one round of connector planning calls, which every micro-batch already makes. Only a query with a lookup join pays it. The new check is about 100 lines, of which about 50 are code, plus a one-line hook in `createQuery`. An internal config turns it off.
  - If this is more than you meant, we can keep only the analysis check above, and leave the other errors to the first micro-batch, as for an ordinary join.
- **A bug this uncovered:** the startup column pruning of SPARK-60734 hid the lookup side, so with `spark.sql.streaming.v2ColumnPruning.enabled`, a micro-batch could fail with `STREAMING_SCAN_MISSING_COLUMNS`. Its placeholders, which the new check shares, now keep the lookup sides.

The design doc records these as E5 and O4.

+  /** The rows of `df` as a streaming DataFrame: one micro-batch, in `numPartitions` partitions. */
+  private def streamOf(df: DataFrame, numPartitions: Int = 1): DataFrame = {
+    val input = MemoryStream[Row](numPartitions)(Encoders.row(df.schema), spark.sqlContext)
+    input.addData(df.collect().toSeq)
+    input.toDF()
+  }
+
+  private case class StreamRun(rows: Seq[Row], execution: IncrementalExecution) {
+    def plan: LogicalPlan = execution.optimizedPlan
+    def lookupJoin: ExternalLookupJoinExec = execution.executedPlan.collectFirst {
+      case exec: ExternalLookupJoinExec => exec
+    }.get
+  }
+
+  /** Runs the streaming `df` on a memory sink until it has processed all of its input. */
+  private def runStream(df: DataFrame, outputMode: String = "append"): StreamRun = {
+    val queryName = s"external_lookup_stream_${streamRunCount.incrementAndGet()}"
+    val query =
+      df.writeStream.format("memory").outputMode(outputMode).queryName(queryName).start()
+    try {
+      query.processAllAvailable()
+      StreamRun(
+        spark.table(queryName).collect().toSeq,
+        query.asInstanceOf[StreamingQueryWrapper].streamingQuery.lastExecution)
+    } finally {
+      query.stop()
+      spark.catalog.dropTempView(queryName)
+    }
+  }
+
+  private def checkStream(df: DataFrame, expected: Seq[Row]): Unit =
+    QueryTest.sameRows(expected, runStream(df).rows).foreach(fail(_))
+
+  /** The error that the streaming `df` fails with. */
+  private def streamFailure[T <: Throwable : ClassTag](df: DataFrame): T = {
+    val cause = intercept[StreamingQueryException](runStream(df)).getCause
+    assert(classTag[T].runtimeClass.isInstance(cause), cause)
+    cause.asInstanceOf[T]
+  }

+    val matched = Seq(Row(1, true, 1, "engineering"), Row(1, true, 1, "research"))

+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.requestedKeys.asScala.toSeq === Seq(1, 3))
+    }

+    // A conjunct that can throw is not checked early: it is evaluated on the joined rows only, so
+    // never for id 3, which has no match, and every key is requested.

+    val rows = lookupJoin.copy(

+  test("external lookup finishes no stream row after a failed or closed read") {
+    // After a failure or a close the result may be partial, so a stream row without a match could
+    // be one whose match was never read: Spark emits no unmatched row then. Id 1 has two matches
+    // and id 3 has none, and both are in one request.
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    val outerJoin =
+      runStream(left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"), "left_outer")).lookupJoin
+    val input = CoalesceExec(1,
+      LocalTableScanExec(outerJoin.child.output, Seq(InternalRow(1), InternalRow(3)), None))
+    Seq(
+      "cursorFailure" -> 0,
+      "closeDuringNext" -> 0,
+      "closeDuringGet" -> 0,
+      "closeBetweenResultRows" -> 1,
+      "closeAtCursorEnd" -> 2).foreach {
+      case (failure, outputRows) =>
+        SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+        val readerFactory = outerJoin.readerFactory match {
+          case factory: SimpleExternalLookupReaderFactory if failure == "cursorFailure" =>
+            factory.copy(failAt = "cursor")
+          case factory => factory
+        }
+        val failingJoin = outerJoin.copy(readerFactory = readerFactory, child = input)
+        val rdd = failingJoin.execute()
+        val context = TaskContext.empty()
+        TaskContext.setTaskContext(context)
+        try {
+          val rows = rdd.iterator(rdd.partitions.head, context)
+          val completeTask = () => context.markTaskCompleted(None)
+          failure match {
+            case "closeBetweenResultRows" =>
+              rows.next()
+              completeTask()
+            case "closeAtCursorEnd" =>
+              SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeCursorEnds.set(completeTask)
+            // The cursor had a row when the close came, but Spark reads no row from it.
+            case "closeDuringNext" =>
+              SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeNextReturns.set(completeTask)
+            // The close comes while the row is read, so Spark neither copies nor joins it.
+            case "closeDuringGet" =>
+              SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeGetReturns.set(completeTask)
+            case _ =>
+          }
+          intercept[Exception] {
+            while (rows.hasNext) rows.next()
+          }
+          assert(failingJoin.metrics("numOutputRows").value === outputRows, failure)
+          assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.rowReadsAfterClose.get() === 0, failure)
+        } finally {
+          TaskContext.unset()
+        }
+    }
+  }

+  private def readSchemaLookup(kind: String): DataFrame = spark.read

+    // At each nested level, the table rules out a null that the read schema allows, and the
+    // connector returns that null.

+    Seq(
+      "nullArrayElement" -> "`tags`.`element`",
+      "nullMapValue" -> "`scores`.`value`",
+      "nullStructInArray" -> "`items`.`element`.`a`").foreach { case (kind, field) =>
+      val lookup = readSchemaLookup(kind)
+      checkError(
+        exception = streamFailure[SparkRuntimeException](
+          left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"))),
+        condition = "DATA_SOURCE_INVALID_EXTERNAL_LOOKUP.NULL_IN_NOT_NULL_FIELD",
+        parameters = Map("table" -> "`ReadSchemaExternalLookupTable`", "field" -> field))

+  test("a lookup-only table that needs read-side CHAR or VARCHAR handling is rejected") {

+        condition = "EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN_UNSUPPORTED.CHAR_VARCHAR_COLUMN",

+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))

+  test("external lookup merges the connector metrics of every reader in a task") {

+  test("external lookup closes task-local readers after success and failure") {
+    def lookup(options: (String, String)*): DataFrame = {

+    val successfulLookup = lookup()
+    runStream(left.join(successfulLookup, left("id") === successfulLookup("id")))
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.readerCount.get() === 1)
+    // The cursor is closed before its reader.
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === Seq("cursor", "reader"))
+
+    // A request that fails returns no cursor; a failing cursor is still closed.
+    Seq("request" -> Seq("reader"), "cursor" -> Seq("cursor", "reader")).foreach {
+      case (failAt, closeEvents) =>
+        SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+        val failingLookup = lookup("failAt" -> failAt)
+        val failure = streamFailure[SparkException](
+          left.join(failingLookup, left("id") === failingLookup("id")))
+        assert(failure.getMessage.contains(s"injected external lookup $failAt failure"))
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.readerCount.get() === 1)
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === closeEvents)

+  }
+
+  test("external lookup makes no connector call once its task completed") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    val lookupJoin = runStream(left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"))).lookupJoin
+    // Computes the join over a local input, in a task that completes before the join is
+    // consumed, before its first request, while its reader is created, while the request is in
+    // progress, or between the two result rows of the request. Another thread consumes the join,
+    // as when a thread other than the task's drives it.
+    val rdd = lookupJoin
+      .copy(child = LocalTableScanExec(lookupJoin.child.output, Seq(InternalRow(1)), None))
+      .execute()
+    val completions = Seq(
+      "beforeEval", "beforeRequest", "duringReaderCreation", "duringRequest", "betweenResultRows")
+    completions.foreach { completion =>
+      SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+      val context = TaskContext.empty()
+      TaskContext.setTaskContext(context)
+      try {
+        if (completion == "beforeEval") context.markTaskCompleted(None)
+        val rows = rdd.iterator(rdd.partitions.head, context)
+        if (completion == "betweenResultRows") rows.next()
+        val completeTask = () => context.markTaskCompleted(None)
+        completion match {
+          case "duringReaderCreation" =>
+            SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeReaderReturns.set(completeTask)
+          case "duringRequest" =>
+            SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeLookupReturns.set(completeTask)
+          case _ => completeTask()
+        }
+        val resultRowsRead = SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resultRowsRead.get()
+
+        val failure = new AtomicReference[Throwable]()
+        val consumer = new Thread(() => {
+          try rows.hasNext catch { case error: Throwable => failure.set(error) }
+        })
+        consumer.start()
+        consumer.join()
+        // No new reader, request or cursor advance after the close, and every reader and cursor
+        // is closed.
+        val (readers, requests) = completion match {
+          case "beforeEval" | "beforeRequest" => (0, 0)
+          case "duringReaderCreation" => (1, 0)
+          case _ => (1, 1)
+        }
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.readerCount.get() === readers)
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.requestCount.get() === requests)
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resultRowsRead.get() === resultRowsRead)
+        // The close closes the cursor before the reader. A cursor that a request in progress
+        // returns after the close is closed after the reader.
+        val closeEvents = completion match {
+          case "beforeEval" | "beforeRequest" => Seq.empty
+          case "duringReaderCreation" => Seq("reader")
+          case "duringRequest" => Seq("reader", "cursor")
+          case _ => Seq("cursor", "reader")
+        }
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === closeEvents)
+        checkError(
+          exception = failure.get().asInstanceOf[SparkException],
+          condition = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+          parameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup reader used after it was closed"))
+      } finally {
+        TaskContext.unset()
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Runs the join of `lookupJoin` over stream row 1 in a task, on a consuming thread, and ends the
+   * task on another thread once the consumer has reached `hook`, which then blocks it until
+   * `whileBlocked` has run. Returns the consumer's failure.
+   */
+  private def endTaskWhileConsumerIsIn(
+      lookupJoin: ExternalLookupJoinExec,
+      hook: AtomicReference[() => Unit])(whileBlocked: Thread => Unit): Throwable = {
+    val rdd = lookupJoin
+      .copy(child = LocalTableScanExec(lookupJoin.child.output, Seq(InternalRow(1)), None))
+      .execute()
+    SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resetCounters()
+    val reached = new CountDownLatch(1)
+    val release = new CountDownLatch(1)
+    val first = new AtomicBoolean(true)
+    hook.set { () =>
+      if (first.getAndSet(false)) {
+        reached.countDown()
+        assert(release.await(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
+      }
+    }
+    val context = TaskContext.empty()
+    TaskContext.setTaskContext(context)
+    try {
+      val rows = rdd.iterator(rdd.partitions.head, context)
+      val failure = new AtomicReference[Throwable]()
+      val consumer = new Thread(() => {
+        try {
+          while (rows.hasNext) rows.next()
+        } catch {
+          case error: Throwable => failure.set(error)
+        }
+      })
+      consumer.start()
+      try {
+        assert(reached.await(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS))
+        val completion = new Thread(() => context.markTaskCompleted(None))
+        completion.start()
+        whileBlocked(completion)
+      } finally {
+        release.countDown()
+        consumer.join(TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(10))
+      }
+      assert(consumer.isAlive === false)
+      failure.get()
+    } finally {
+      TaskContext.unset()
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("once the join has seen the task end, it makes no connector call") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    val lookupJoin = runStream(left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"))).lookupJoin
+    // The consumer is inside the cursor's next() or get() when the task ends on another thread.
+    Seq(
+      "next" -> SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeNextReturns,
+      "get" -> SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeGetReturns).foreach { case (call, hook) =>
+      var metricSamples = 0
+      var resultRowsRead = 0
+      val failure = endTaskWhileConsumerIsIn(lookupJoin, hook) { completion =>
+        // The close does not wait for the call: it closes the cursor, then the reader.
+        completion.join(TimeUnit.SECONDS.toMillis(10))
+        assert(completion.isAlive === false, call)
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === Seq("cursor", "reader"))
+        metricSamples = SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.metricSamples.get()
+        resultRowsRead = SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resultRowsRead.get()
+      }
+      checkError(
+        exception = failure.asInstanceOf[SparkException],
+        condition = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+        parameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup reader used after it was closed"))
+      // When the call returns, the consumer sees the close and leaves the cursor and the reader's
+      // metrics to it: each is closed once, and no call follows.
+      assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === Seq("cursor", "reader"))
+      assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.metricSamples.get() === metricSamples, call)
+      assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.resultRowsRead.get() === resultRowsRead, call)
+      assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.rowReadsAfterClose.get() === 0, call)
+    }
+  }
+
+  test("task completion closes the reader only after a copy of a value row in progress") {
+    val lookup = spark.read.format(classOf[SimpleExternalLookupDataSource].getName).load()
+    val left = streamOf(Seq(1).toDF("id"))
+    val lookupJoin = runStream(left.join(lookup, left("id") === lookup("id"))).lookupJoin
+    // The consumer is copying the first value row when the task ends on another thread.
+    val failure = endTaskWhileConsumerIsIn(
+        lookupJoin, SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.beforeValueRead) { completion =>
+      // The close closes the cursor, which must leave the row readable, and then waits for the
+      // copy before it closes the reader, which may own the memory behind the row.
+      eventually(timeout(10.seconds)) {
+        assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === Seq("cursor"))
+      }
+      completion.join(500)
+      assert(completion.isAlive)
+      assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === Seq("cursor"))
+    }
+    // After the copy, the reader is closed, and the consumer then fails on its next read.
+    assert(SimpleExternalLookupDataSource.closeEvents.asScala.toSeq === Seq("cursor", "reader"))

+/** Finalizes an optimized external lookup side immediately before ordinary V2 scan preparation. */
+object PrepareExternalLookupJoin extends Rule[LogicalPlan] with PredicateHelper
+  with QueryErrorsBase {
+  override def apply(plan: LogicalPlan): LogicalPlan = {
+    val prepared = plan.transformUpWithPruning(_.containsPattern(EXTERNAL_LOOKUP_JOIN)) {
+      case join: ExternalLookupJoin if provablyEmpty(join) => emptyJoinResult(join)
+      case join: ExternalLookupJoin => prepare(join)
+    }
+    // Prepared lookup joins no longer contain their lookup relation, so a lookup-only table that
+    // is still read here cannot run.
+    if (prepared.containsPattern(DATA_SOURCE_V2_RELATION)) {

+        ExternalLookupRelations.lookupOnlyTable(node).foreach { table =>
+          throw QueryCompilationErrors.unsupportedBatchReadError(table)

+  // The optimizer folds `WHERE false` on the lookup side into an empty relation, and a condition
+  // such as `s.id = r.id AND false` into `false`. Such a join needs no connector call.
+  private def provablyEmpty(join: ExternalLookupJoin): Boolean =

+      case Some(Literal(value, BooleanType)) => value == null || value == false
+      case _ => false

+  private def emptyJoinResult(join: ExternalLookupJoin): LogicalPlan = {

+    val unmatched = Project(join.left.output ++ nullLookupColumns, join.left)

+      // so that its sources, watermarks and stateful operators still run in every micro-batch.
+      // PruneFilters decides whether a streaming subplan may be pruned.
+      case _ => Filter(Literal.FalseLiteral, unmatched)
+    }
+  }

+  private def prepare(join: ExternalLookupJoin): LogicalPlan = {

+    // join evaluates the conjunct in a filter above the join, and an outer join is rejected.
+    if (join.joinType == LeftOuter) {

+        case _: ExternalUserDefinedFunction =>
+          throw QueryCompilationErrors.useExternalUDFInJoinConditionUnsupportedError(join.joinType)
+        case _ =>
+          throw QueryCompilationErrors.usePythonUDFInJoinConditionUnsupportedError(join.joinType)
+      }

+      case (EqualTo(leftExpr, rightAttr: Attribute), index)

+      case (EqualTo(rightAttr: Attribute, leftExpr), index)
+          if isLookupEquality(join, leftExpr, rightAttr) =>
+        OfferedLookupPredicate(leftExpr, rightAttr, index, "=", false)
+    }
+    if (offeredCandidates.isEmpty) {

+        "NO_LOOKUP_CANDIDATE", Map("table" -> toSQLId(tableName)))

+    }

+      joinOutput: JoinOutput,

+    metrics.inputRows += rows.length
+    metrics.inputBatches += 1
+
+    private val matched = Array.fill(rows.length)(false)
+    private val finished = mutable.BitSet.empty
+    // Output rows not yet returned: a stream row index and the lookup row it is joined with.
+    private val pending = mutable.Queue.empty[(Int, InternalRow)]
+
+    // One entry for each distinct key that can match, in the order of first occurrence. A row
+    // that can never match, because it fails the stream condition or has a null parameter, is
+    // finished right away, and its key is not requested. The stream condition is checked before
+    // the key is computed, so that it can guard the parameter expressions.
+    private val keyEntries = mutable.LinkedHashMap.empty[UnsafeRow, KeyEntry]
+    rows.indices.foreach { index =>
+      lazy val key = parameters.key(rows(index))
+      if (!joinOutput.canMatch(rows(index)) || parameters.matchesNothing(key)) {
+        finish(index)
+      } else {
+        keyEntries.get(key) match {
+          case Some(entry) => entry.rowIndexes += index
+          case None => keyEntries.put(
+            key.copy(),
+            KeyEntry(parameters.requestRow(rows(index)), mutable.ArrayBuffer(index)))
+        }
+      }
+    }
+    private val requestedKeys = keyEntries.keys.toArray
+
+    // No connector request, and no reader, when no key can match. The connector gets copies of
+    // the request rows, so that the ones that Spark checks the results against stay its own.
+    private var cursor: ExternalLookupResultCursor =
+      if (keyEntries.isEmpty) EmptyLookupCursor
+      else connectorCall(reader.lookup(keyEntries.values.map(_.requestRow.copy()).toArray))
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      pending.nonEmpty
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryFillPending()
+      if (pending.isEmpty) throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+      val (index, lookupRow) = pending.dequeue()
+      joinOutput.project(rows(index), lookupRow)
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryFillPending(): Unit = {
+      try {
+        while (pending.isEmpty && advanceCursor()) {
+          reader.resultRowRead()
+          // A close() during either call fails the read before Spark copies or joins the row.
+          val start = System.nanoTime()
+          val ordinal = cursor.inputOrdinal()
+          reader.ensureOpen()
+          val connectorRow = cursor.get()
+          metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+          if (connectorRow == null) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName, "NULL_RESULT_ROW")
+          }
+          val key = requestedKey(ordinal)
+          val resultRow = reader.copyRow(resultRows.validatedCopy(connectorRow))
+          if (parameters.selectedPredicatesHold(keyEntries(key).requestRow, resultRow)) {
+            joinResultRow(key, resultRow)
+          }
+        }
+        if (pending.isEmpty) finishCursor(completed = true)
+      } catch {
+        case error: Throwable =>
+          Utils.tryWithSafeFinally(throw error) {
+            finishCursor(completed = false)
+          }
+      }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Advances the connector's cursor, unless the reader was closed meanwhile. A close() while
+     * next() ran fails the read once next() returns: Spark then reads no row from the closed
+     * cursor, and does not take a missing row for a complete result.
+     */
+    private def advanceCursor(): Boolean = (cursor ne EmptyLookupCursor) && {
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      val advanced = connectorCall(cursor.next())
+      reader.ensureOpen()
+      advanced
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Runs a connector call and adds its time to the lookup time metric, which counts only the
+     * time in the connector, not that of the work above the join while a cursor is open.
+     */
+    private def connectorCall[T](call: => T): T = {
+      val start = System.nanoTime()
+      try call finally metrics.lookupTime += System.nanoTime() - start
+    }
+
+    private def requestedKey(ordinal: Int): UnsafeRow = {
+      if (ordinal < 0 || ordinal >= requestedKeys.length) {
+        throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+          tableName,
+          "INVALID_INPUT_ORDINAL",
+          Map("ordinal" -> ordinal.toString, "numParameterRows" -> requestedKeys.length.toString))
+      }
+      requestedKeys(ordinal)
+    }
+
+    private def joinResultRow(key: UnsafeRow, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit =
+      keyEntries(key).rowIndexes.foreach(joinMatch(_, lookupRow))
+
+    private def joinMatch(index: Int, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit = {
+      if (joinOutput.matches(rows(index), lookupRow)) {
+        matched(index) = true
+        joinOutput.matched(lookupRow).foreach(emit(index, _))
+      }
+    }
+
+    /**
+     * Closes the cursor once. After a complete read, finishes every stream row that was waiting for
+     * its results. After a failure or a close, the results may be partial, so it finishes none:
+     * a row without a match could be a row whose match was never read. Once the reader is closed,
+     * its close owns the cursor and the reader's metrics, so the join makes no further connector
+     * call.
+     */
+    private def finishCursor(completed: Boolean): Unit = if (cursor ne EmptyLookupCursor) {
+      cursor = EmptyLookupCursor
+      if (!reader.isClosed) {
+        try {
+          connectorCall(reader.closeCursor())
+        } finally {
+          reader.updateMetrics()
+        }
+      }
+      if (completed) keyEntries.values.foreach(_.rowIndexes.foreach(finish))
+    }
+
+    private def finish(index: Int): Unit = if (!finished.contains(index)) {
+      finished += index
+      if (!matched(index)) joinOutput.unmatched.foreach(emit(index, _))
+    }
+
+    private def emit(index: Int, lookupRow: InternalRow): Unit = {
+      pending.enqueue(index -> lookupRow)
+      metrics.outputRows += 1
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** The cursor of a batch that sends no request, or whose cursor is finished. */
+  private object EmptyLookupCursor extends ExternalLookupResultCursor {
+    override def next(): Boolean = false
+    override def inputOrdinal(): Int = throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+    override def get(): InternalRow = throw new NoSuchElementException("external lookup result")
+    override def close(): Unit = {}
+  }
+
+  /** A check of one value slot: a field of a row, or an element of an array. */
+  private type SlotCheck = (SpecializedGetters, Int) => Unit
+
+  /**
+   * Validates each row that the connector returns, and copies it once into Spark's own row before
+   * Spark checks, joins or keeps it. A connector may reuse its row and its buffers, byte arrays
+   * included, so a row that Spark still holds must not share them. A value that breaks its type
+   * fails the task, at any nested level: a null in a field, array element or map value that the
+   * table or the read schema declares NOT NULL, or a decimal that does not fit its precision and
+   * scale. Spark already relied on them while it optimized the query. The checks are built once
+   * from the read schema, and a field whose type has nothing to check costs nothing per row.
+   */
+  private class LookupResultRows {
+    private val copy = UnsafeProjection.create(lookupInput, lookupInput)
+    private val fieldChecks = lookupInput.zipWithIndex.flatMap { case (field, ordinal) =>
+      slotCheck(field.dataType, field.nullable, Seq(field.name)).map(ordinal -> _)
+    }
+
+    /** The row, validated and copied into a row that Spark owns. */
+    def validatedCopy(resultRow: InternalRow): UnsafeRow = {
+      fieldChecks.foreach { case (ordinal, check) => check(resultRow, ordinal) }
+      copy(resultRow).copy()
+    }
+
+    /** The check of a slot of this type, at this field path, or None if it has nothing to check. */
+    private def slotCheck(
+        dataType: DataType,
+        nullable: Boolean,
+        path: Seq[String]): Option[SlotCheck] = {
+      val valueCheck = nonNullValueCheck(dataType, path)
+      if (nullable && valueCheck.isEmpty) {
+        None
+      } else {
+        Some { (values, ordinal) =>
+          if (!values.isNullAt(ordinal)) {
+            valueCheck.foreach(_(values, ordinal))
+          } else if (!nullable) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName,
+              "NULL_IN_NOT_NULL_FIELD",
+              Map("field" -> QueryExecutionErrors.toSQLId(path)))
+          }
+        }
+      }
+    }
+
+    /** The check of a value that is not null, or None if its type has nothing to check. */
+    private def nonNullValueCheck(dataType: DataType, path: Seq[String]): Option[SlotCheck] =
+      dataType match {
+        case decimalType: DecimalType => Some { (values, ordinal) =>
+          val value = values.getDecimal(ordinal, decimalType.precision, decimalType.scale)
+          if (!fits(value, decimalType)) {
+            throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+              tableName,
+              "DECIMAL_OUT_OF_RANGE",
+              Map(
+                "field" -> QueryExecutionErrors.toSQLId(path),
+                "type" -> QueryExecutionErrors.toSQLType(decimalType)))
+          }
+        }
+        case structType: StructType =>
+          val checks = structType.fields.toSeq.zipWithIndex.flatMap { case (field, ordinal) =>
+            slotCheck(field.dataType, field.nullable, path :+ field.name).map(ordinal -> _)
+          }
+          Option.when(checks.nonEmpty) { (values, ordinal) =>
+            val struct = values.getStruct(ordinal, structType.length)
+            checks.foreach { case (fieldOrdinal, check) => check(struct, fieldOrdinal) }
+          }
+        case arrayType: ArrayType =>
+          slotCheck(arrayType.elementType, arrayType.containsNull, path :+ "element").map {
+            check => (values, ordinal) => eachElement(values.getArray(ordinal), check)
+          }
+        case mapType: MapType =>
+          // A map key is never null, whatever the value's nullability.
+          val keyCheck = slotCheck(mapType.keyType, nullable = false, path :+ "key")
+          val valueCheck =
+            slotCheck(mapType.valueType, mapType.valueContainsNull, path :+ "value")
+          Option.when(keyCheck.nonEmpty || valueCheck.nonEmpty) { (values, ordinal) =>
+            val map = values.getMap(ordinal)
+            keyCheck.foreach(eachElement(map.keyArray(), _))
+            valueCheck.foreach(eachElement(map.valueArray(), _))
+          }
+        case _ => None
+      }
+
+    private def eachElement(array: ArrayData, check: SlotCheck): Unit = {
+      var index = 0
+      while (index < array.numElements()) {
+        check(array, index)
+        index += 1
+      }
+    }
+
+    /** Whether the decimal has its type's precision and scale without rounding. */
+    private def fits(value: Decimal, decimalType: DecimalType): Boolean = {
+      val rescaled = value.clone()
+      rescaled.changePrecision(decimalType.precision, decimalType.scale) && rescaled == value
+    }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Evaluates the lookup parameters of stream rows: the request row that is sent to the
+   * connector, and the key that identifies equal parameters under Spark equality, which
+   * normalizes floating-point values and collations. Also checks the rows that the connector
+   * returns against the selected lookup predicates.
+   */
+  private class LookupParameters(partitionIndex: Int) {
+    private val requestProjection = UnsafeProjection.create(lookupParameters, streamOutput)
+    private val keyProjection = UnsafeProjection.create(lookupParameters.map { parameter =>
+      NormalizeFloatingNumbers.normalize(CollationKey.injectCollationKey(parameter))
+    }, streamOutput)
+    private val keyCheck = lookupKeyCheck.map(Predicate.create(_))
+    private val requestAndResult = new JoinedRow()
+    requestProjection.initialize(partitionIndex)
+    keyProjection.initialize(partitionIndex)
+    keyCheck.foreach(_.initialize(partitionIndex))
+
+    def requestRow(streamRow: InternalRow): UnsafeRow = requestProjection(streamRow).copy()
+
+    /** The key of a stream row, in a reused row: copy it to retain it. */
+    def key(streamRow: InternalRow): UnsafeRow = keyProjection(streamRow)
+
+    /** Whether a row that the connector returns satisfies the selected lookup predicates. */
+    def selectedPredicatesHold(requestRow: UnsafeRow, resultRow: InternalRow): Boolean =
+      keyCheck.forall(_.eval(requestAndResult(requestRow, resultRow)))
+
+    /**
+     * A null parameter that is not null-safe matches no lookup row, so it is not requested.
+     * The key has the request row's nulls.
+     */
+    def matchesNothing(key: InternalRow): Boolean =
+      nullSafeParameters.indices.exists { index =>
+        !nullSafeParameters(index) && key.isNullAt(index)
+      }
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Evaluates the stream condition on stream rows and the residual condition on joined rows, and
+   * builds output rows per join type.
+   */
+  private class JoinOutput(partitionIndex: Int) {
+    // Value rows follow the read schema, and the residual and output are bound to its fields.
+    private val joinedLookupInput =
+      if (joinType == LeftOuter) lookupInput.map(_.withNullability(true)) else lookupInput
+    private val joinedInput = streamOutput ++ joinedLookupInput
+    private val joinedRow = new JoinedRow()
+    private val streamPredicate = streamCondition.map(Predicate.create(_, streamOutput))
+    private val residual = residualCondition.map(Predicate.create(_, joinedInput))
+    private val projection = UnsafeProjection.create(output, joinedInput)
+    private val nullLookupRow = new GenericInternalRow(lookupInput.length)
+    streamPredicate.foreach(_.initialize(partitionIndex))
+    residual.foreach(_.initialize(partitionIndex))
+    projection.initialize(partitionIndex)
+
+    /** Whether a stream row passes the stream condition; a row that fails it matches nothing. */
+    def canMatch(streamRow: InternalRow): Boolean = streamPredicate.forall(_.eval(streamRow))
+
+    def matches(streamRow: InternalRow, lookupRow: InternalRow): Boolean =
+      residual.forall(_.eval(joinedRow(streamRow, lookupRow)))
+
+    /** The lookup row that the output for a match joins, if the join type emits one. */
+    def matched(lookupRow: InternalRow): Option[InternalRow] = joinType match {
+      case Inner | LeftOuter => Some(lookupRow)
+      case _ => None
+    }
+
+    /** The lookup row that the output for a stream row without a match joins, if any. */
+    def unmatched: Option[InternalRow] = joinType match {
+      case LeftOuter => Some(nullLookupRow)
+      case _ => None
+    }
+
+    /** The output row, projected into a reused row. */
+    def project(streamRow: InternalRow, lookupRow: InternalRow): InternalRow =
+      projection(joinedRow(streamRow, lookupRow))
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * The connector reader of one partition and its active cursor. The reader is opened by the
+   * first request, and closed once, after the last batch or when the task completes. A thread
+   * other than the task's may still drive the join then. The close then owns every close: it
+   * closes the active cursor, keeps the reader's final metrics, waits for a copy of a value row
+   * in progress, and closes the reader. Once the join has seen the close, it makes no further
+   * connector call, not even to close its cursor. Closing may overlap the one connector call in
+   * progress, which it does not wait for, and it reads the metrics of the task's readers while that
+   * call runs. Requests, cursor calls and copies take no lock. Metrics reads do: closing keeps the
+   * reader's final metrics under the lock of the task's `TaskLookupReaders`, so it can wait for a
+   * metrics read in progress, which calls `currentMetricsValues()` on the task's readers.
+   */
+  private class LookupReader {
+    private val taskReaders = readerMetrics.forCurrentTask()
+    private val closed = new AtomicBoolean(false)
+    // Set while Spark copies a value row that the cursor returned.
+    private val copying = new AtomicBoolean(false)
+    // Each is taken by exactly one of the join and close(), so it is closed once.
+    private val openReader = new AtomicReference[ExternalLookupReader]()
+    private val activeCursor = new AtomicReference[ExternalLookupResultCursor]()
+    private var resultRowsSinceMetricsUpdate = 0
+    Option(TaskContext.get()).foreach(_.addTaskCompletionListener[Unit](_ => close()))
+
+    /** Sends one request and returns the cursor over its result rows. */
+    def lookup(requestRows: Array[UnsafeRow]): ExternalLookupResultCursor = {
+      ensureOpen()
+      metrics.requests += 1
+      metrics.parameterRows += requestRows.length

+        // A close() since the check above took the reader. It marks the reader closed first, so
+        // this check sees it, and no second reader is created.
+        ensureOpen()
+        createReader()
+      }
+      val cursor = Option(reader.lookupBatch(requestRows.asInstanceOf[Array[InternalRow]]))
+        .getOrElse {
+          throw QueryExecutionErrors.invalidDataSourceExternalLookupError(
+            tableName, "NULL_RESULT_CURSOR")
+        }

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), posting on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Fixed in [7412930c368](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/7412930c3688d84fc17527b204fcbbc5a6d3a751). The close now claims the cursor slot as it starts, so a cursor that a request publishes later counts as late. When the consuming thread then sees the close, it waits until the reader is closed, and only then closes that cursor. So the order matches the Javadoc. Only the consuming thread waits, and the close still never waits for a connector call. A new test returns the request inside the close's window.

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), posting on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Fixed in [7412930c368](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/7412930c3688d84fc17527b204fcbbc5a6d3a751). The Javadoc now says what Spark does on each path. `spark.read` and `CREATE TEMPORARY VIEW … USING` fail. A session-catalog table created `USING` such a provider loads the V2 table. A custom session catalog may return a V1 table. A source listed in `spark.sql.sources.useV1SourceList` is read through V1.

+/**
+ * Creates the partition evaluators of an [[ExternalLookupJoinExec]]. The factory is sent to the
+ * tasks, so it holds only what they need; the plan node and its scan stay on the driver.
+ *
+ * An evaluator joins its partition one batch of up to `maxParameterRowsPerRequest` stream rows at
+ * a time. For each batch it sends one request with the distinct parameters that can match, and
+ * streams the connector's result rows into output rows. Parameters are deduplicated per request,
+ * that is within one batch: a key repeated in a later batch is requested again.
+ *
+ * Spark does not trust the connector with the selected lookup predicates: it evaluates
+ * `lookupKeyCheck` on every row that the connector returns, against the request row that the row
+ * answers, and drops a row that fails it, before it joins the row. The stream rows that share a
+ * request row have Spark-equal parameters, so one check serves all of them.
+ *
+ * The join condition comes in two parts: `streamCondition` reads only stream columns and is
+ * evaluated on each stream row before the request, and `residualCondition` is evaluated on the
+ * joined rows. A stream row that fails `streamCondition` cannot match, so its parameters are not
+ * sent.
+ */
+class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluatorFactory(
+    tableName: String,
+    lookupParameters: Seq[Expression],
+    nullSafeParameters: Seq[Boolean],
+    lookupKeyCheck: Option[Expression],
+    streamOutput: Seq[Attribute],
+    lookupInput: Seq[Attribute],
+    output: Seq[Attribute],
+    joinType: JoinType,
+    streamCondition: Option[Expression],
+    residualCondition: Option[Expression],
+    readerFactory: ExternalLookupReaderFactory,
+    maxParameterRowsPerRequest: Int,
+    maxBatchBytes: Long,
+    metrics: ExternalLookupJoinMetrics,
+    readerMetrics: ExternalLookupReaderMetrics)

+

+
+  override def createEvaluator(): PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] =

+
+  private class ExternalLookupJoinEvaluator extends PartitionEvaluator[InternalRow, InternalRow] {
+    override def eval(
+        partitionIndex: Int,
+        inputs: Iterator[InternalRow]*): Iterator[InternalRow] = {
+      assert(inputs.length == 1)
+      new PartitionJoinIterator(inputs.head, partitionIndex)
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** Joins one partition batch by batch, and closes its reader after the last batch. */
+  private class PartitionJoinIterator(input: Iterator[InternalRow], partitionIndex: Int)
+    extends Iterator[InternalRow] {
+    private val reader = new LookupReader
+    private val parameters = new LookupParameters(partitionIndex)
+    private val resultRows = new LookupResultRows
+    private val joinOutput = new JoinOutput(partitionIndex)
+    private var batch: Iterator[InternalRow] = Iterator.empty
+    private var inputExhausted = false
+
+    override def hasNext: Boolean = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      batch.hasNext
+    }
+
+    override def next(): InternalRow = {
+      tryAdvance()
+      if (!batch.hasNext) {
+        throw new SparkIllegalStateException(
+          errorClass = "INTERNAL_ERROR",
+          messageParameters = Map("message" -> "External lookup join exhausted"))
+      }
+      batch.next()
+    }
+
+    /** Reads more only when nothing is buffered; safe to call repeatedly. */
+    private def tryAdvance(): Unit = {
+      while (!batch.hasNext && !inputExhausted) {
+        val rows = readBatch()
+        if (rows.nonEmpty) {
+          batch = new BatchJoinIterator(rows, parameters, resultRows, joinOutput, reader)
+        }
+        inputExhausted = !input.hasNext
+      }
+      if (inputExhausted && !batch.hasNext) reader.close()
+    }
+
+    private lazy val toUnsafe = UnsafeProjection.create(streamOutput, streamOutput)
+
+    // An array, because a batch's rows are read by position for every key, match and output row.
+    // The batch holds its rows until its request is read, so it stops once their copies reach
+    // maxBatchBytes, keeping the row that reaches it, as well as at maxParameterRowsPerRequest
+    // rows. It always takes one row.
+    private def readBatch(): Array[InternalRow] = {
+      val rows = mutable.ArrayBuffer.empty[InternalRow]
+      var bytes = 0L
+      while (rows.length < maxParameterRowsPerRequest && bytes < maxBatchBytes && input.hasNext) {
+        val row = input.next() match {
+          case unsafe: UnsafeRow => unsafe.copy()
+          case other => toUnsafe(other).copy()
+        }
+        bytes += row.getSizeInBytes
+        rows += row
+      }
+      rows.toArray
+    }
+  }
+
+  /** The stream rows that share a key, and the one request row sent for them. */
+  private case class KeyEntry(requestRow: UnsafeRow, rowIndexes: mutable.ArrayBuffer[Int])
+
+  /**
+   * Joins one batch of stream rows. Rows whose parameters are equal under Spark equality share
+   * one request row, and every result row for a request row that satisfies the selected lookup
+   * predicates joins all the stream rows sharing it. A stream row is finished, which may emit its
+   * unmatched output row, once no more result rows can match it.
+   *
+   * Output rows are projected into a reused row on `next()`, so the consumer copies the rows it
+   * retains, as with other join iterators.
+   */
+  private class BatchJoinIterator(

+      parameters: LookupParameters,
+      resultRows: LookupResultRows,
+      joinOutput: JoinOutput,

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), posting on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Fixed in [bceaf1d1d2a](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/bceaf1d1d2a3188ed183978044ff6494fec92702), in both directions you described.
- **Cache:** `CacheManager.useCachedData` now leaves alone the lookup side of each join that must run as a lookup join, and any CTE definition that side reads. So a cached table that is then hinted, and a cached hinted DataFrame, both run as lookup joins that read current data. A lookup-only DataFrame cannot be cached at all, because `cache()` plans a batch scan and fails; the test checks that too.
- **WITH clauses:** `FormExternalLookupJoin` classifies a join with the CTEs of its inputs inlined, as the analysis check does, and inlines the lookup side's CTEs into the lookup join. To keep the two in agreement, `InlineCTE`'s code for inlining one reference moved into a helper that both use, with no change to `InlineCTE` itself. Tests cover a lone WITH clause, a hinted one, and an ineligible one.

> [!NOTE]
> **DISCLAIMER:** This comment was written by an LLM, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), posting on behalf of @HeartSaVioR.

Fixed in [bceaf1d1d2a](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/bceaf1d1d2a3188ed183978044ff6494fec92702). The hint now accepts relation names given as strings, as `ResolveJoinStrategyHints` does, so `df.hint("external_lookup", "p")`, PySpark, Spark Connect and `/*+ EXTERNAL_LOOKUP('p') */` all work. Tests cover the Dataset and SQL forms. From #60087, which reads string parameters as cache options, a string that contains `=` is an option and any other string names a relation ([258ac90960a](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/258ac90960ae6058bef4c4779526fb08cf052138)).
